5.6 · A capability a running session claims carries one flag in that session's colour, standing in its territory at a constant size on screen, a pennant on its pole however far out the globe is zoomed and never a dot (ADR-1039); it drops in with one ring at its foot, stands still while held, furls and greys when the session is quiet, and lifts away when the claim goes, with no movement under reduced motion. On an island with no code the claimed share is marked as a lot. The flag is the only claim mark: no band, outline or fill, and no coast tint (ADR-0968, ADR-0923 D1, narrowing ADR-0804 D9)

5.7 · Replaying a growth, the sessions recorded with the latest stage the replay has reached flag the territories they held, each flag arriving as the replay reaches it, none before the first (ADR-0968, ADR-0923 D3)

capabilities.title: 7 · Running sessions
capabilities.description: A see-through strip along the forest pane's bottom, spanning its width and collapsible by its header (contract 7.17) lists one plain row per session that has not ended, claimed or not (ADR-0749 D1; ADR-0737 D1's removal of off-plan rows and their evidence stands, and capability 6 stays retired), showing facts as labels and no prose on the owner's behalf: anything that needs the owner is an open question on the arc surface (ADR-0824). An unclaimed row is named from its harness and what it works in; a session working in several worktrees says so (D2). Each row shows what it is doing, its context bar and its available context total. Explicitly related subagents and supervised lanes fold beneath their parent behind “+N”. (Narrowed in place, 2026-11-03, by ADR-1218, decision_c3bb98f4b0e1: children show beneath a parent at work, indented with their own dots, a finished one greyed; “+N” and the expander fold them only once the tree is idle; the expander still starts closed on the row's own detail, contracts 7.2 and 7.8.) Each row has one expander (the same control as “+N”), closed at first; expanded, it lists each worktree the session works in (full path on hover) labelled unmerged or merged, the commands it started and has not seen finish, and the files in its window, read from the agent link's window reading (9.10) only when expanded, then its children. Each row leads with a status dot of its state (working, waiting for you, idle), and each root row wears its session’s own colour, the colour of its wisps on the forest (capability 5, ADR-0736), and a hovered wisp highlights its row. Hovering or focusing a row lights its claimed islands and dims the others. Waiting rows carry no mark beyond their dot, working and waiting read from each session's turns (ADR-0754 D5); rows neither working nor waiting are idle by their state alone, and an idle session is not listed: the list shows only the sessions at work, while an idle child of a session at work stays under it with the idle dot (ADR-1225, superseding ADR-1221 D2; there is no History tab, ADR-1221 D1); ended sessions are hidden. Parent relationships and totals are read only when recorded or supplied by the agent link; missing values are not guessed. *Narrowed in place, 2026-10-05 (ADR-0804 D9, decision_5aadb523c1cb; ADR-0923 D2, decision_027f3b08bb8b): no wisps are drawn, so a row's colour is the colour of its traversal and of its claimed territories' outlines, and the hovered-wisp clause no longer applies. Hovering or focusing a row lights only the islands holding capabilities it, or a subagent folded under it, claimed; an increment it holds lights none, whatever its touches name (contract 7.4).* *Narrowed in place, 2026-11-03 (ADR-1217, decision_e7888402d873): the owner put a status dot on every row, on trial, so a row reads dot, colour swatch, name, context bar; no row text is a model's summary (contract 7.9).* *Overtaken in place, 2026-11-03 (ADR-1219, decision_727e318c6bda; owner-directed): the list is no strip along the forest pane's bottom but the Sessions tab of the app's full-height left rail, filling it, with no header toggle or size control (contract 7.17).*

dependsOn.title: 4 · Look inside and inspect an artifact

contracts.title: 4.1 · Clicking an artifact dot in Forest or Library opens the existing pinned-artifact card in the right-hand story-panel slot. It shows kind, title and description or another summary field; with no summary it shows the whole text. It contains no links list, read counts, depth or entrances.

4.6 · Opening an artifact card closes an open story panel, and opening a story closes the card. Close and Escape dismiss the card. The shared core pin and summary renderer serve both globe modes without writing to the library.

4.7 · With no session selected, no session lights a note, though the listed sessions have read them: the knowledge dots stay unlit, with no shared marks and no lines; selecting a session lights exactly what it read (ADR-0921).

4.8 · Drilling into a listed session colours its orchestrator in the session's own colour and each subagent in a distinct shade of that hue; an unknown agent stays pale, and a session with no row keeps the fixed palette (ADR-0738).
4.9 · The globe's knowledge dots light exactly as the core does: nothing with none selected, or the selected session alone in its agents' colours (ADR-0738 D5, ADR-0921).

4.10 · A selected session's reading path draws as curved lines: from each full read to the same known agent's next, in recorded order, pointing to the later read, bowed away from the globe's centre, in its agents' colours, only when it has no window to read, a subagent's first read stepping from the session's latest full read before it (where it was spawned); otherwise its window's traversal draws instead (4.16, ADR-0756). With none selected no path draws (ADR-0921). A peek or an unknown agent draws none, and a curve never claims a followed link (ADR-0740).

4.12 · A new step's line grows from its earlier read to its later one (one agent's new steps one after another, different agents at once), and opening the view grows nothing. With a session selected one replay walks all its agents' steps in recorded order, growing each line and lighting each note as it is reached, holds the finished picture, then clears and replays (ADR-0797). No looping glow is drawn (ADR-0921). Reduced motion neither grows nor replays; paths carry no arrowheads and no wisp model (ADR-0742).

4.15 · A note lit by a new read stays unlit until the growing line into it arrives (including a line queued behind that agent's earlier steps), then lights in its session's colour; a note already lit, or reached only by steps read before the view opened, is never held (ADR-0742 D2).

4.16 · Selecting a session reads its window from the host and draws it on the knowledge dots (ADR-0756): one line per step from each note it opened in full to the next, in reading order (files between do not break the chain; a note gone from the library is stepped over; a step taken twice draws once), in the session's colour, solid where a stored link joins the two notes either way round and dotted where none does, growing toward the later note when new and then showing direction with a faint fill that runs from the earlier note to the later. A note whose read is in the window now has a ring; one compacted out since is lighter, and its lines fade with it; one only glimpsed is tinted faint with no line. An answer for a session no longer selected is dropped, and with none selected no window is drawn or asked for.

4.20 · A selected session's file opens join its traversal where the land hands the core a place for them (ADR-0804 D5): each file whose path names a placed surveyed file (any path ending packages/<package>/src/…) is a stop on the code's surface, beside the notes it opened, in reading order; a step between two files is solid when one imports the other and dotted otherwise, a step between a file and a note dives into the core (or rises out of it), a compacted file's read fades with its steps, and a path that names no placed file is stepped over, never drawn. The map hands it no file places since ADR-1212, so there every file open is stepped over and the chain runs note to note. Opening a capability lights its territory; an arc, an increment or any other plan record is drawn nowhere and breaks nothing.

4.18 · With no session selected, the core asks the host for no session's window, whatever the running-sessions list holds; selecting one asks for that session's window alone, and never again while its last ask is out (ADR-0921).

4.21 · Each knowledge dot is sized by its note's reach: the distinct sessions that read it in the last 90 days, a whole read counting 1 and a peek 0.3, a session once at its strongest read. Its area grows linearly from a visible floor for a note no session read (or when no reads are recorded) to a ceiling for the most-read note on the globe. A note a selected session lights or holds in its window keeps its size: that read shows in colour, brightness and rings (ADR-0926).
4.22 · Clicking a Library note answers within 100 ms with no frame over 50 ms, and its card is open within 1 s or shows progress (verified by the Mint box's lag run)
4.23 · A product's globe draws the system notes it reads from its factory, and their card says they come from it

7.1 · The list includes once each session the agent-link reading lists (agent link 4.9, 4.12) that is at work (7.10, ADR-1225), whether or not it holds a claim; that reading excludes a verified close-out, or an ended or quiet session with no open work past the user's leave-after setting (1 hour by default, read as idle-after is) (ADR-0754 D4, ADR-0758 D3, D5, narrowing ADR-0749 D1 and ADR-0737 D1), and the list excludes every idle one it keeps. A waiting row carries no mark beyond its status dot (7.9, ADR-1217); working and waiting come from the session's turns (agent link 4.8), and only a session whose hooks report no turns is judged by the user's idle-after setting. A row's task uses its claim reason or held increment title; a session with neither is named from its harness and what it works in (its latest claim's branch, else its last folder), held to 40 characters, and never labelled off plan. A session whose lines name more than one folder shows how many worktrees it works in, naming them on hover (D2).

7.2 · An explicit parent relation or subagent-started record puts that child under its parent, indented, with its own status dot. While the parent or one of its children is at work (not idle; an observed subagent, whose state is not known, keeps no tree open by itself), the children show beneath it without a click and no "+N" is drawn; a child known to be idle stays listed, greyed. Once nothing in the tree is at work, the tree folds behind the row's "+N" expander (7.8), which reveals the children and collapses them again (ADR-1218); a root row is listed only while at work (7.10, ADR-1225), so the trees that fold are those of an idle child under it. No child is duplicated at the top. A recorded subagent lacking its own session reading is shown as observed, without inventing a live state, until its end is recorded (a subagent-ended line, before or after its start): then it reads idle; absent parent relations are never inferred from claim wording.

7.4 · Hovering or keyboard-focusing a row lights the forest islands containing the capabilities it, or a subagent folded under it, claimed, and dims the other islands; an increment it holds lights none, whatever its touches name (ADR-0923 D2). Leaving the row restores the ordinary forest appearance. With no claimed capability the row does not arbitrarily select one.

7.5 · Every row reserves an empty context-bar slot. When an agent-link context total is supplied the row displays that total; when absent it displays an unavailable mark, never zero. This increment draws no composition segments, thresholds or estimated totals.

7.6 · Each row's bar is its session's tokens used (agent link 9.5), read again every 10 seconds, on one scale for every row: 1,000,000 tokens across the full width (the display's choice; a reading has no window size, ADR-0728). A Claude Code reading's bar is split into Injected, Grounding, Implementation and Other in proportion to its composition (9.8), and hovering gives the tokens and each group's estimated share; a Claude Code row marks its reading's context guidance (the user's setting, 600,000 by default; ADR-0739 D1), one mark; a row whose reading carries no guidance has none; a Codex row is one raw segment with no marks. With 400,000 tokens split 2:2:3:1, the segments are 10%, 10%, 15% and 5% wide. The list's header names the four groups in bar order, each beside a swatch in its segment's colour.

7.7 · The list hands the knowledge core its rows as the core's roster, each row with its children in the row's colour. Clicking a row selects its session in the core and marks the row (a child's row selects its parent); clicking the selected row again clears the selection, and the core then shows no session's traversal. The list and the core share one selection (ADR-0738 D5, ADR-0921).

7.8 · Every row has one expander, an arrow at the row's start, closed at first, opening the row's detail only when the user expands it; a row whose children are folded (7.2) counts them as "+N" after its name, and its expander opens them too (7.2's control, not a second one), while the children of a row at work show without it. Expanded, a row lists, under a small "Worktrees" label, every worktree it works in, oldest first, each by its folder's own name with its full path on hover and its merge label (7.15); then its "Running" block (7.16); then, under a small "Files" label, the files in its window (agent link 9.10), each once, in the order first opened, with files no longer in the window muted; then its children. Files are read from the agent link's window reading only when a row is expanded, never from a second reader; a session without a window reading says why and lists no files. Collapsing hides the detail, and folded children, again.

7.9 · The running-sessions list shows facts as labels and prints no prose about a session: no 'needs you' chip or line, no close-out why, no 'holding unmerged' line, and no text made by a model's summary. Every listed row shows, after its expander, a status dot read from its state alone: working (or a child at work), waiting for you within the idle-after time, or idle (an observed subagent's says its state is unavailable), named on hover, then, on a root row, its colour swatch, then its name and its context bar (ADR-1217). A row is idle by its state alone (neither working nor waiting within the idle-after time): a root row that is idle is not listed (7.10), so the idle dot is a child row's. Owner decisions surface only as open questions on the arc surface (ADR-0824 D1, D2, narrowing ADR-0758 D1; ADR-1225 D1).

7.10 · The list shows only the sessions at work: working, waiting for you within the idle-after time, or a parent with a child working. A session that is neither is not listed, whatever keeps the agent link's listing holding it (unmerged work, an unverified close-out, work on main, an app record not yet archived); there are no tabs and no "N idle" row. The header counts the rows. With none listed it says "No running sessions" (ADR-1225 D1, superseding ADR-1221 D2; narrowing ADR-0758 D5; ADR-0824).

7.13 · When the listed sessions run on more than one machine, each row names the machine its session runs on (the latest its activity lines name), beside its name, when the row has room: a row too narrow for it drops the machine first, before its name or its context bar are cut; when they all run on one machine, no row names one.

7.14 · A row whose session holds no claim is named by its app's title (agent link 4.19), held to the label limit, before falling back to its harness and place. Expanding any row opens with up to three lines describing it, from recorded words only: the app's title where the row's name is not it, the objective of the increment it holds, and the app's latest status. A row with none of these shows no description.

7.15 · Each worktree in a row's detail carries one short label from the branches its session recorded there: "merged" when none still holds open work; for an open branch with a pull request, "PR #n" and what it waits on (in merge queue, draft, failing, or in CI while its checks run), or "PR #n" alone when its checks pass or it has none; "unmerged" when no open branch there has a pull request read. The main line, or no branch, carries no label; a branch recorded with no folder is folded under the folder last worked in, and none is dropped.

7.16 · An expanded row's Running block lists the commands its session started and has not seen finish, background ones included, each by its first words (one line, ellipsised, full command on hover) and how long it has run.

7.17 · The list is the Sessions tab of the app's left rail (ADR-1219), filling the tab and scrolling vertically inside it, never horizontally. Its header names it and counts it and carries the colour legend; nothing on it hides the rows or sizes the list, since the rail's tabs choose what shows. Every row starts collapsed and its expander opens it (7.8): its detail, while the children of a row at work show without it (7.2), with no expand-all control; an expanded row lists its Worktrees, Running and Files one under another.
7.18 · A session that has named itself is listed by its own name

7.20 · A session the agent link flags for work on main shows it in its row's one-click detail, not on its row: a warning, "on main", for work outside a workspace; a neutral "first commit" while a new repository's first commit is pending; each with the reading's full words; an unflagged session shows none (ADR-0906 as narrowed by ADR-1223)

7.24 · The sessions list and the forest re-read the plan only when their news holds a change to a story, capability, contract, arc or health record: news of other records, or of lines alone, draws from the tree they already have; their first news always reads.
7.25 · Landing news refreshes the code survey without re-reading an unchanged plan
7.27 · A health change that re-records the state the tree already shows does not re-read the tree: news whose only tree changes are such health records draws from the tree held
7.29 · Clicking a session's row answers within 100 ms with no frame over 50 ms, and the row reads selected within 1 s or shows progress (verified by the Mint box's lag run)
7.30 · The reading starts from the survey kept at the last start
7.31 · A start is settled once the fresh tree and the start's first code survey are drawn (or the survey changed nothing or failed), and the page takes its progress bar away then
7.32 · After the start's first survey lands, the page asks for the survey once more at once, so a newer main fetched meanwhile still arrives
7.33 · A failed refresh says what failed; only persisting failures raise the banner
7.34 · An unreachable library reads as one plain banner

openWork.arcTitle: Capability tree: a map of capabilities, their interfaces, and the work landing on them
openWork.title: Session file reads on the land after the dots: show them another way, or delete the unfed traversal code

capabilities.title: 1 · Work states
capabilities.description: Every part, increment and arc shows exactly one state, worked out by one rule from the records, so no two views, and no two lines of one view, can disagree. A part is planned, in progress or landed; an increment, once closed, is landed or not completed (failed, withdrawn, or closed with nothing recorded), and before that is waiting on you, queued, held by an agent or open; an arc is waiting, blocked, claimed, idle, quiet, parked or closed.

contracts.title: 2.1 · Two separate processes write lines for two sessions, and reading from the start returns every line once, in the order written.
2.2 · Reading "since line N" returns only the lines after N, in order, each carrying the number to pass next time.
2.3 · Lines written for project "site" never appear when reading project "app".
2.4 · The log never shows up in the library's list of projects, and writing lines leaves the library's own records and change feed untouched.

2.5 · The log opens on whichever server the library resolved to, reached through the library's connection: lines two machines write for one project on one Cloud SQL instance are both read back from either, in order (live, opt-in).

2.6 · A line may name the earlier line of its own project's log that caused it (`causedBy`, ADR-0746 D2), and reads back naming it. A line naming a line its project's log does not hold (another project's, or none) is refused, whether appended alone or under the project's lock, and nothing is written.

2.7 · A bounded read sends only the lines it asks for, oldest first: by kind, session, cursor and time, by a field's value, values or absence, by a field carried, the latest for each key, the newest or oldest few, and inside folders whatever their case or slashes, with the fields it never reads left out.
2.8 · A read inside folders, latest line per session, on a log of many lines elsewhere is served by an index: it never scans the project's whole log

2.9 · An activity line can be formatted with its complete recorded command, including quotes and line breaks, for both started and finished commands; its number, time, session, kind and recorded cause remain visible. Compact formatting still clips long commands to 60 characters.

2.10 · A claim-refused line's text names the part, the session holding it, the file whose edit asked for it and the refused session's reason; a claimed line's text names its file and the session it was taken over from

2.11 · A line appended for a hook event is not added again when the log holds a line exactly like it, of the same event, that came the other way within two minutes of its time; the same way twice adds it twice

2.12 · A log opened in a storytree home whose settings name an experiment and arm stamps both on every line it writes (ADR-1064 D2); a log opened in a home that names none writes its lines without them.

2.13 · Lines written earlier, appended as one batch, go in at their own times and in order in a few round trips however many they are; a line exactly like one the log holds at that time, or like an earlier one of the batch, is added once, and a line of an event that came the other way within two minutes is kept once
5.1 · Session A claims "email form", and the claim shows A and the reason.

5.2 · A second live claimant is refused naming the holder and why it still binds, including any unverified close-out disagreement; a claim-refused line records the refusal. An idle holder, including one whose standing safe close-out is verified against its branches and running work, permits takeover even with stale command telemetry. A prompt, admitted claim or non-compaction restart voids that close-out.
5.3 · When A reports it landed, the claim ends and a "landed" line is written. A release, or A's session ending, also ends it.
5.4 · A claim on a capability the library doesn't have is refused, and when two agents claim at the same instant exactly one wins.
5.5 · An edit made while A holds "email form" counts toward it, and an edit from a session holding nothing counts as unplanned activity.
5.6 · While a command A started is still running, past the quiet time, B's claim on A's capability is refused, naming A.

5.7 · Session A claims a proposed increment, and the claim shows A and the reason while the library shows the increment active; B's claim on it is refused, naming A. An active one is not started again, and a closed one is refused.

5.8 · Claiming an increment whose own wait holds, or whose arc's wait holds, is refused, naming each blocker and its reason, and one held on an open question is refused as waiting on the owner. Nothing is written and the increment is not started. Once the wait releases, the claim succeeds.
5.9 · A capability claim is never refused because the open increments naming it in their touches wait: touches is a plan, never a lock (ADR-0944 D2). The waiting increment itself is still refused.

5.10 · A claim taken on branch `feature/signup` ends with a "merged" line once GitHub shows a pull request from that branch merged after the claim was taken, found at the next tool call or hook line; a pull request merged before the claim, or still open, ends nothing.

5.11 · The public readings list current capability and increment claims and find the holder of one unit, with the same live or idle result on the terminal and the board. Released work and a unit in another project have no holder.

5.12 · Claude Code session A makes a workspace for a proposed increment: a new folder where its harness keeps worktrees, on a fresh branch cut from `origin`'s main as just fetched (a commit pushed after the clone is in it), and A holds the increment there, the claim naming that branch, and the increment is active. For Codex, preparation fetches main and returns its exact commit and a work-derived name for the app's `create_worktree`, without creating a folder, branch or claim. The agent then attaches the app's returned directory: Storytree verifies it is a linked worktree of this repository with HEAD at that exact commit, names a detached HEAD `codex/<name>` (keeps an existing named branch), and claims the work for that session on that branch. Moving `origin/main` after preparation does not change the expected commit.

5.13 · Making a workspace for work another live session holds, or for waiting work, is refused naming the holder or the blocker, and no folder, branch or claim is made, only a claim-refused line for held work (5.2); for work the session already holds it is refused naming the branch it holds it on. Codex checks before app creation and again when attaching; a claim lost to another session between the steps is refused naming that holder, leaving the app's worktree untouched.

5.14 · When main cannot be fetched fresh, as from a folder with no `origin`, it is refused saying why, and nothing is claimed or started. Attaching a directory from another repository, the main checkout, a subdirectory, or a worktree at the wrong commit is refused without claiming or changing it. If attaching fails after taking the claim (including naming a detached branch), that claim is released; the app's worktree is never removed (a started increment stays active).

5.15 · A claim cancelled while waiting for the activity lock or the increment activation write lock leaves no claimed line, activation or activation history. A capability or already-active increment claim checks cancellation before its claimed line too. Once admitted, a claim completes normally; a workspace claim creates or attaches its workspace only after admission.

5.16 · A claim's reason is its session's name in the running-sessions list, so it is held to 40 characters (measured from the list's label column at its default width): a claim, or a workspace, whose reason is longer is refused naming the limit and the reason's length, nothing is written and nothing is started; a reason of 40 characters or fewer is claimed as before (ADR-0737 D2).
5.17 · A holder last seen on this machine before it restarted is taken over at once

5.19 · Making a workspace for a capability from inside a worktree whose branch this session already holds work on claims the capability there, on that branch, and makes no second worktree or branch. Asking for a workspace for an available increment from inside any linked worktree (named or detached, from any subfolder, either harness) is refused with the command that claims it there, and no worktree, branch, preparation, claim or activation is made

5.23 · A claim takes from the library what deciding it needs and no more: one the session already holds takes almost nothing, and a capability claim takes about as much with five open increments naming it as with one.

5.25 · Making a workspace for work that already has an open pull request (a head branch named for it, `*/increment-<id>-*`) is refused naming each pull request and its branch, before anything is claimed or made, unless the session says to build beside it; a GitHub that cannot be asked refuses nothing
5.26 · The session manager ends a quiet session's claim with a release naming the holder and why; a live holder's claim is refused

5.27 · Closing or releasing an increment ends every capability claim taken while it was held, whoever closes it and whatever the disposition, in every reading; one claimed before it stands (ADR-0944 D5, ADR-0949 D4)
5.29 · Releasing an active increment without closing it, by the release tool, the session manager's release or close-out, returns it to proposal; a capability or a closed increment is untouched

5.31 · An edit tool aimed at a capability its session's claimed increment does not list, or that another live session holds by claim or on its increment's list, is refused before the edit, naming the way through or the holder; a file that declares no capability, or a session's own listed capability, is never refused (ADR-0949 D3)

5.33 · The session manager's worklist lists claimed increments whose holder is quiet, with no running command and no open pull request, routing a gone holder's to release and a quiet one's to ask; nothing is ended until the manager releases (ADR-0953 D4)
5.34 · A takeover's claimed line names the holder, how long it was quiet and why
5.35 · A refused claim names the increment its holder holds the work for

5.36 · A question one live session is putting to the owner is refused to another, naming it, and read as presented; it is free again once that session stops, ends or closes out, and a settled question is refused

5.37 · When a claim on an increment ends because its branch's pull request merged, that increment's pending plan changes are applied first, marked with the pull request and written by the session that saw the merge
5.38 · A refused capability claim names the increment its session holds it under
5.39 · A claim's mark is one shape and one colour wherever it is drawn

5.40 · An edit to a file in an imported folder is refused unless the session's increment lists the explored capability covering it; when it does, the user is asked (Claude Code) or the edit refused, never passed on the agent's own increment
5.41 · One user yes covers an increment's edits to imported code
5.42 · A yes said in the conversation counts for the session that heard it

5.43 · With `idle-after` set to 10m, a claim whose holder was last seen 15 minutes ago, with no command running, reads idle and can be taken over, and a session whose hooks report no turns reads waiting; unset (30 minutes), neither: a session whose hooks report its turns is never judged by it (ADR-0754 D5).
5.44 · A handed-over pull request keeps its session's claims until it merges or closes
5.45 · A fix session on the pull request's branch takes over its held claims
5.46 · Letting go of a pull request ends the claims held for it

5.47 · A worktree git makes while printing to stderr is made and claimed; one git fails to make is refused with git's own error line, never its progress line, and leaves no claim, folder or branch behind

5.48 · A session claiming again, from a linked worktree, work it holds on another branch holds it on that worktree's branch from then on; claiming it again from the main checkout leaves it where it is
5.49 · A red the watcher handles is a pr-red line on its pull request's holder
5.50 · A hand-over holds none of the claims taken on another branch
5.51 · A holder whose heartbeat stopped reads idle at once
5.52 · A renumbered file is placed by its session's increment's pending moves before the live plan, so a fold asks for no capability it never touches (ADR-0966)
5.53 · A capability on another live session's increment's list is refused at the claim, naming that increment and its holder
5.54 · A CI rerun the watcher starts is a ci-rerun line on the watcher, which reads as no session
5.55 · Several capabilities are claimed in one call, in ascending id order, all or nothing
5.56 · A hand-over also holds the session's branchless claims on the handed increment
5.57 · Clearing an owner wait to finish the work claims the increment first, through that wait
5.58 · Only an increment's live holder closes it; the owner's shell, the watcher, and anyone once it reads idle or unheld close it too
5.59 · A workspace for an increment claims every capability on its list, all or nothing, before the worktree is made

5.60 · The owners query names each file's capability and who holds it: another live session by its own claim or by an increment whose list names it, the caller itself, or nobody; a file with no capability names its story's package, and the free capabilities are offered to claim in one call
5.61 · Letting go of a merged pull request applies each held increment's pending plan changes, marked with it, before its claims end; an apply that fails ends none

5.62 · Claiming an increment says how to close it in this project: with its outcome and its pull request where the folder's origin is on GitHub, otherwise with its outcome and a note naming the local commit

5.63 · land on a checkout whose code is only in languages the map cannot read says it cannot read the code, naming those languages and the ones it reads, rather than naming its planned contracts as unproven or its story as having no code here
5.64 · Claiming an increment that waits on a capability's claim is refused while another live session holds that capability, and succeeds once it is released
1.1 · A part no line names is planned. A claim makes it in progress, a landed report makes it landed, and a new claim after landing makes it in progress again.
1.2 · A part that is released, or whose window closes, without landing stays in progress, with nobody on it.
1.3 · A story is planned while every part is planned or it has no parts, landed once every part has landed, and in progress otherwise.

1.4 · A closed increment reads landed only when a landing was recorded or it carries a pull request. Every other close, whether failed, withdrawn or closed with nothing recorded, reads not completed (red), with the hover naming which. Nothing reads landed merely because it closed.

An open increment gets one reading, first match wins: waiting on you (held on a question you have not settled, or by a wait for an action of yours with its note while it waits on no open work; it drops back the moment you settle or clear it), then queued (its own wait, or its arc's, still holds, or a wait for an outside event before its check-back day, or a wait for an action of yours on work that still waits on open work, until that work lands), then held (an agent holds it, idle or not), then blocked (unclaimed, and its capabilities list names a capability another open increment holds through a live session; it names that increment and clears when it closes or releases, ADR-0949 D3), then open. An event wait past its check-back day holds nothing, and the reading says check-back passed (ADR-0938 D1). A proposal is never by itself waiting on you, but a question you have not settled holds it as it holds any open increment (ADR-0909 D2). An active increment whose agent released it reads open, still in progress, with nobody on it.

An arc reads one state, first match wins: closed or parked, as recorded; then waiting (a question on it you have not settled); then blocked (its own wait still holds); then queued (every open increment is held, on a wait, on you or blocked by another increment, and it names what it waits on); then in progress (a live session holds one of its open increments, ADR-0949 D1); then ready · N to take (N open increments nobody holds and nothing holds up), even while an idle agent holds other work on it: an idle claim does not hide free work (ADR-0938 D3); then idle, shown "in progress · idle N min" (every agent on it is idle and nothing is free); then quiet (nothing open). Queued, ready and quiet are read from its increments on every live reading (ADR-0760 D1).

capabilities.title: 2 · Agents on the board
capabilities.description: Every increment and part an agent holds shows which agent: Claude Code or Codex, when its window opened, the reason it gave when it claimed, and whether it is live or idle, and for how long. It reads the agent link's own claim reading, so the overlay and the claim tool always agree, and an idle holder still holds its work.

contracts.title: 4.1 · A start line makes a working session labelled "Claude Code", with its folder, when it started and when it was last seen.
4.2 · A session whose hooks report no turns reads as waiting once no line has come for longer than the quiet time, and after its end line it reads as ended.
4.3 · A resumed window continues the same session instead of starting a second one.
4.4 · A Codex session whose hooks never ran, but which calls a storytree tool, still appears and is flagged "hooks not running", so a missing hook never looks like an agent doing nothing.

4.5 · A command that started 40 minutes ago and has not finished keeps its session working. Once it finishes, or its turn ends with no background task left running, it no longer counts, and one started longer ago than the longest a command may run no longer counts.

4.6 · A session is its harness session id, never a folder: one whose lines name two folders reads with both as its worktrees, in the order it first worked in each, while its folder stays the one it started in (ADR-0749 D2).

4.7 · A session with no line for longer than a command may run (12 hours) and no end line has stopped reporting: it reads as gone, never as ended, since nothing said it ended; up to that limit it reads as idle (ADR-0749 consequences).

4.8 · Working comes from turn state (ADR-0754 D5): a prompt makes its session working until its turn ends, however long the turn writes no line, and compacting mid-turn does not end it; its end makes it waiting at once; a turn that ends with background tasks still running leaves their command running, so the session stays working until it finishes.

4.9 · Who is listed (ADR-0754 D4): a session whose branches (every branch other than main its lines name, a merged line's excepted) still hold open work stays listed whatever its end line or silence says; once its work resolves (the latest branch-state line for each branch says resolved), a session leaves on its end line or after the leave-after quiet time, counted from its last line or the resolution, whichever is later; a session the Claude or Codex app keeps (a session-archived or session-unarchived line names it) shows done instead of leaving, is removed at once when archived, and comes back when un-archived.

4.10 · Each branch a session worked on is marked resolved once a pull request from it merged (asked of GitHub from any machine), or, on the machine it was worked on, once it has nothing ahead of the main line or is deleted (a branch with no commit yet is neither); one still ahead stays open, and one worked on again after it resolved is looked at again and reads open when it is ahead. A branch-state line is written only when the state changes, on the session that saw it (ADR-0754 D4). The hooks take this look once a minute through a copy of themselves that may run longer than a hook, so a merge is recorded though GitHub answers later than a hook may run. A claim's `merged` line resolves its branch as a branch-state line does, until a later look reads it open.

4.11 · Closing out records whether the session says it is safe to close and why, releases every capability and increment claim it still holds regardless of branch or whether a tool or edit hook took it, and returns the released ids. Other sessions keep their claims; repeating close-out releases nothing. Verification of safe still checks unfinished work and runs.

4.12 · A yes is checked, never trusted: it leaves the list at once when its branches are resolved and nothing of its own runs; otherwise it stays and needs you, naming the disagreement; a no stays with its why; a later prompt or new admitted claim voids it (ADR-0758 D3). Closing out first asks whether the project’s branches have merged, so a merge no hook recorded still bears a yes out.

4.25 · The sessions the Claude desktop app and Codex keep are read, read-only, from their own files on each machine (Claude's claude-code-sessions/<account>/<org>/local_*.json: cliSessionId and isArchived; Codex's state_5.sqlite threads: id and archived, headless runs and subagents excluded), and each session the project's log knows gets a session-archived or session-unarchived line when its state there changes, never otherwise. Absent files read as absent and damaged ones as unreadable, and neither writes anything (ADR-0754 D4).

4.13 · The sessions listing (`storytree session list`) first asks whether the project's branches have merged, so it never waits on a hook to have recorded a merge, then shows each session the list shows, one block each, with its state, listing, folder, open and resolved branches, its work on main as its flag or label (4.26), close-out and what needs you; a hidden one (a verified close-out) only with --all; --json gives the same sessions as data.

4.18 · The hooks reap a worktree once it can go (ADR-0790): a clean linked worktree whose head is in the main line, whose every session (at least one) has a verified close-out or is archived, which is not locked and holds neither the hook's folder nor a registered hook script, is removed and unregistered and its branch deleted; a dirty, unmerged, locked, unused, still-used, protected or hook-running one stays; its folder is moved to a trash folder first and the trash emptied out of the hook's way.

4.19 · How the app that keeps a session names and describes it reaches the log: for each session this project knows, the Claude desktop app's title and its post-turn summary's status, or Codex's thread name (else its title), are written as one `session-described` line (by whichever session read the records, never on the session it is about), scrubbed as transcripts are and held to 120 and 300 characters, and written again only when those words change. Each session read from the log carries the latest title and status.

4.20 · A line about other sessions (a claim's merge, a branch's state, what an app keeps or how it names a session) never makes its writer a session: a person, or the app, that only looked is not listed, and an agent's look does not count as its own work.

4.21 · The app looks at each project's branches itself, once a minute while it runs, asking from the latest folder this machine still has and writing under app:<machine>, so its sessions list never waits on a hook to have recorded a merge.

4.22 · A session reads, for each folder its lines name, the branches recorded there, in the order first recorded, with whether each still holds open work and, while open, its pull request as the latest look read it (4.24). The main line is no branch; a branch with no folder is placed in the folder the session last worked in.

4.23 · A session reads the commands it started and has not seen finish, each with its command text and start time, background ones a turn left running included: the same reading that keeps a session working (4.5, 4.8).

4.24 · The branch look reads every open pull request of the project's repository in one GitHub call, alongside its merged-pull-request call, under the same once-a-minute stamp and fail-soft rules: for each open branch, its number, whether it is a draft, its head commit's checks taken together (pending, passing or failing; none when it has none), and whether it waits in the merge queue. The branch-state line carries these and is written again only when one changes; GitHub not answering erases nothing; a pull request closed unmerged leaves the branch open with none. The Session reading carries them on each open branch in branchesByFolder.

4.26 · Work on main is never silently dropped (ADR-0906): a session that edited files inside a folder on the main line while the latest look on its machine finds that folder's main uncommitted, or that holds an increment it claimed on main, stays listed whatever its end or silence, flagged "worked on main, outside a workspace"; while the repository has no commit yet it is labelled "setting up git, first commit pending" instead; a yes close-out is not verified while the flag stands; once the work is committed (and the claim gone) the flag goes and it leaves as 4.9 says. A file edited outside the folder, or a capability claimed on main, raises no flag.

4.27 · The branch look (4.10) also looks, on this machine, at each folder a session edited files in, or claimed an increment in, while on the main line: it writes a main-state line saying whether that folder's main holds uncommitted changes and whether its repository has no commit yet, only when that changes, under the same once-a-minute stamp and fail-soft rules; a folder no longer on the main line reads as holding none.

4.28 · The sessions read from the lines that decide them, and the claims read from those standing, are what a fold of the whole log gives at any time, from a share of its lines; the list's own read leaves out only sessions the list hides, and the status line's states agree.

4.29 · A session last seen on its machine before that machine's recorded start reads gone, not working, to a reader on any machine, with no command running, and its claims read free; one seen since the start, or on another machine, reads as before

4.30 · The first hook on a machine to reach a project's log after the machine starts records that start there, once: a later hook reading the same start a moment apart writes nothing; the next start, or another project, is recorded again
4.32 · A session in a harness storytree has no hooks for reads as connected in the sessions list, never flagged hooks not running; a watched harness's session without hooks still is
4.33 · A project's folder is its marker's folder, even when its sessions worked in a subfolder
4.34 · Naming a session, closing it out and listing the sessions are verbs declared once: closing out or naming answers in the same sentence for either door, writing to the calling session's log
4.35 · The hook times read back by harness, event and machine

4.36 · The hooks sweep worktree folders git no longer lists (ADR-0790 D4): an idle one under .claude/worktrees whose every unignored file git already has is removed, its links removed and never followed; one holding content git lacks, one a live process works in, or one a session wrote in lately stays.

4.37 · A worktree the hooks reap while a test Postgres still runs on its .pgtest/data has that server stopped first (its postmaster.pid checked to name a live Postgres process) and the folder removed.
4.38 · A pool lane-failed or lane-reoffered line makes no session read live
4.39 · The branch-state look's git calls learn this machine's speed, floored at 2 s and capped at 5 s
4.41 · A print-mode session whose turn ended reads ended without its end line
4.42 · The person row (a person: session, where commands with no session id land) never reads working and is never listed; its lines stay recorded against the person
5.1 · Session A claims "email form", and the claim shows A and the reason.

5.2 · A second live claimant is refused naming the holder and why it still binds, including any unverified close-out disagreement; a claim-refused line records the refusal. An idle holder, including one whose standing safe close-out is verified against its branches and running work, permits takeover even with stale command telemetry. A prompt, admitted claim or non-compaction restart voids that close-out.
5.3 · When A reports it landed, the claim ends and a "landed" line is written. A release, or A's session ending, also ends it.
5.4 · A claim on a capability the library doesn't have is refused, and when two agents claim at the same instant exactly one wins.
5.5 · An edit made while A holds "email form" counts toward it, and an edit from a session holding nothing counts as unplanned activity.
5.6 · While a command A started is still running, past the quiet time, B's claim on A's capability is refused, naming A.

5.7 · Session A claims a proposed increment, and the claim shows A and the reason while the library shows the increment active; B's claim on it is refused, naming A. An active one is not started again, and a closed one is refused.

5.8 · Claiming an increment whose own wait holds, or whose arc's wait holds, is refused, naming each blocker and its reason, and one held on an open question is refused as waiting on the owner. Nothing is written and the increment is not started. Once the wait releases, the claim succeeds.
5.9 · A capability claim is never refused because the open increments naming it in their touches wait: touches is a plan, never a lock (ADR-0944 D2). The waiting increment itself is still refused.

5.10 · A claim taken on branch `feature/signup` ends with a "merged" line once GitHub shows a pull request from that branch merged after the claim was taken, found at the next tool call or hook line; a pull request merged before the claim, or still open, ends nothing.

5.11 · The public readings list current capability and increment claims and find the holder of one unit, with the same live or idle result on the terminal and the board. Released work and a unit in another project have no holder.

5.12 · Claude Code session A makes a workspace for a proposed increment: a new folder where its harness keeps worktrees, on a fresh branch cut from `origin`'s main as just fetched (a commit pushed after the clone is in it), and A holds the increment there, the claim naming that branch, and the increment is active. For Codex, preparation fetches main and returns its exact commit and a work-derived name for the app's `create_worktree`, without creating a folder, branch or claim. The agent then attaches the app's returned directory: Storytree verifies it is a linked worktree of this repository with HEAD at that exact commit, names a detached HEAD `codex/<name>` (keeps an existing named branch), and claims the work for that session on that branch. Moving `origin/main` after preparation does not change the expected commit.

5.13 · Making a workspace for work another live session holds, or for waiting work, is refused naming the holder or the blocker, and no folder, branch or claim is made, only a claim-refused line for held work (5.2); for work the session already holds it is refused naming the branch it holds it on. Codex checks before app creation and again when attaching; a claim lost to another session between the steps is refused naming that holder, leaving the app's worktree untouched.

5.14 · When main cannot be fetched fresh, as from a folder with no `origin`, it is refused saying why, and nothing is claimed or started. Attaching a directory from another repository, the main checkout, a subdirectory, or a worktree at the wrong commit is refused without claiming or changing it. If attaching fails after taking the claim (including naming a detached branch), that claim is released; the app's worktree is never removed (a started increment stays active).

5.15 · A claim cancelled while waiting for the activity lock or the increment activation write lock leaves no claimed line, activation or activation history. A capability or already-active increment claim checks cancellation before its claimed line too. Once admitted, a claim completes normally; a workspace claim creates or attaches its workspace only after admission.

5.16 · A claim's reason is its session's name in the running-sessions list, so it is held to 40 characters (measured from the list's label column at its default width): a claim, or a workspace, whose reason is longer is refused naming the limit and the reason's length, nothing is written and nothing is started; a reason of 40 characters or fewer is claimed as before (ADR-0737 D2).
5.17 · A holder last seen on this machine before it restarted is taken over at once

5.19 · Making a workspace for a capability from inside a worktree whose branch this session already holds work on claims the capability there, on that branch, and makes no second worktree or branch. Asking for a workspace for an available increment from inside any linked worktree (named or detached, from any subfolder, either harness) is refused with the command that claims it there, and no worktree, branch, preparation, claim or activation is made

5.23 · A claim takes from the library what deciding it needs and no more: one the session already holds takes almost nothing, and a capability claim takes about as much with five open increments naming it as with one.

5.25 · Making a workspace for work that already has an open pull request (a head branch named for it, `*/increment-<id>-*`) is refused naming each pull request and its branch, before anything is claimed or made, unless the session says to build beside it; a GitHub that cannot be asked refuses nothing
5.26 · The session manager ends a quiet session's claim with a release naming the holder and why; a live holder's claim is refused

5.27 · Closing or releasing an increment ends every capability claim taken while it was held, whoever closes it and whatever the disposition, in every reading; one claimed before it stands (ADR-0944 D5, ADR-0949 D4)
5.29 · Releasing an active increment without closing it, by the release tool, the session manager's release or close-out, returns it to proposal; a capability or a closed increment is untouched

5.31 · An edit tool aimed at a capability its session's claimed increment does not list, or that another live session holds by claim or on its increment's list, is refused before the edit, naming the way through or the holder; a file that declares no capability, or a session's own listed capability, is never refused (ADR-0949 D3)

5.33 · The session manager's worklist lists claimed increments whose holder is quiet, with no running command and no open pull request, routing a gone holder's to release and a quiet one's to ask; nothing is ended until the manager releases (ADR-0953 D4)
5.34 · A takeover's claimed line names the holder, how long it was quiet and why
5.35 · A refused claim names the increment its holder holds the work for

5.36 · A question one live session is putting to the owner is refused to another, naming it, and read as presented; it is free again once that session stops, ends or closes out, and a settled question is refused

5.37 · When a claim on an increment ends because its branch's pull request merged, that increment's pending plan changes are applied first, marked with the pull request and written by the session that saw the merge
5.38 · A refused capability claim names the increment its session holds it under
5.39 · A claim's mark is one shape and one colour wherever it is drawn

5.40 · An edit to a file in an imported folder is refused unless the session's increment lists the explored capability covering it; when it does, the user is asked (Claude Code) or the edit refused, never passed on the agent's own increment
5.41 · One user yes covers an increment's edits to imported code
5.42 · A yes said in the conversation counts for the session that heard it

5.43 · With `idle-after` set to 10m, a claim whose holder was last seen 15 minutes ago, with no command running, reads idle and can be taken over, and a session whose hooks report no turns reads waiting; unset (30 minutes), neither: a session whose hooks report its turns is never judged by it (ADR-0754 D5).
5.44 · A handed-over pull request keeps its session's claims until it merges or closes
5.45 · A fix session on the pull request's branch takes over its held claims
5.46 · Letting go of a pull request ends the claims held for it

5.47 · A worktree git makes while printing to stderr is made and claimed; one git fails to make is refused with git's own error line, never its progress line, and leaves no claim, folder or branch behind

5.48 · A session claiming again, from a linked worktree, work it holds on another branch holds it on that worktree's branch from then on; claiming it again from the main checkout leaves it where it is
5.49 · A red the watcher handles is a pr-red line on its pull request's holder
5.50 · A hand-over holds none of the claims taken on another branch
5.51 · A holder whose heartbeat stopped reads idle at once
5.52 · A renumbered file is placed by its session's increment's pending moves before the live plan, so a fold asks for no capability it never touches (ADR-0966)
5.53 · A capability on another live session's increment's list is refused at the claim, naming that increment and its holder
5.54 · A CI rerun the watcher starts is a ci-rerun line on the watcher, which reads as no session
5.55 · Several capabilities are claimed in one call, in ascending id order, all or nothing
5.56 · A hand-over also holds the session's branchless claims on the handed increment
5.57 · Clearing an owner wait to finish the work claims the increment first, through that wait
5.58 · Only an increment's live holder closes it; the owner's shell, the watcher, and anyone once it reads idle or unheld close it too
5.59 · A workspace for an increment claims every capability on its list, all or nothing, before the worktree is made

5.60 · The owners query names each file's capability and who holds it: another live session by its own claim or by an increment whose list names it, the caller itself, or nobody; a file with no capability names its story's package, and the free capabilities are offered to claim in one call
5.61 · Letting go of a merged pull request applies each held increment's pending plan changes, marked with it, before its claims end; an apply that fails ends none

5.62 · Claiming an increment says how to close it in this project: with its outcome and its pull request where the folder's origin is on GitHub, otherwise with its outcome and a note naming the local commit

5.63 · land on a checkout whose code is only in languages the map cannot read says it cannot read the code, naming those languages and the ones it reads, rather than naming its planned contracts as unproven or its story as having no code here
5.64 · Claiming an increment that waits on a capability's claim is refused while another live session holds that capability, and succeeds once it is released
2.1 · An increment Claude Code holds shows "Claude Code", when that window opened, and its reason. Two Claude Code windows are told apart by when they opened.
2.2 · After 30 quiet minutes the holder reads "idle for N min" and still holds the increment. Once it releases or lands it, its window closes, or its pull request merges, nobody is on it.
2.3 · A Codex holder whose hooks never ran is flagged "hooks not running".

2.4 · An arc's holders come only from its open increments: the agent holding one of them, or a capability claimed under one of them (ADR-0949 D1). A capability claim counts toward the increment it was taken under, never an arc directly; a closed increment contributes nothing, so a capability held by another arc's session reads nothing on an arc whose landed increment lists it.

capabilities.title: 3 · Arc surface
capabilities.description: A full-width arcs-only bar sits below the app story's separate gear-only app bar and opens one read-only drawer over the forest. The bar carries no project name. Both bars reserve their space above the forest so its controls remain reachable, and the drawer opens below them. The drawer, half the window's height, leaves the forest usable below; it can be expanded to fill the window below the bars and restored (3.10). It lists root arcs as dense two-line lanes (state chip, title and small counted wait marks, then the bars alone, wrapping), with a bar for each increment, finished work first, each bar coloured by its work state, a count of what landed and what is open spoken on the bars' label but not shown (ADR-0980), and a chip with the lane's state and who is on it; Active, Parked and Closed each show their own arcs. It stays current while it is open: about every two seconds it asks for what changed in the library and the agent log, which the app carries to it, and it re-checks the clock once a minute, so an agent that goes quiet turns idle without any new record. *Overtaken in place, 2026-11-03 (ADR-1219, decision_727e318c6bda; owner-directed): there is no arcs bar or drawer; the arcs are the Arcs tab of the app's full-height left rail, read while mounted, and an arc's briefing is a card over the map that opens only on its row's click (contracts 3.1, 3.7, 5.1).*

contracts.title: 3.1 · The arcs are the Arcs tab of the app's left rail (ADR-1219): they fill the tab, their scopes then their lanes, scrolling inside it, and are read from the page's start settling (ADR-1224) for as long as they are mounted, whichever tab is on show. An arc's detail opens only when its row is clicked, as a card over the map beside the rail; clicking that row again, the card's close button or Escape closes it and returns focus to the row, and no card opens on its own. Across the active arcs the surface tells the frame what waits on the owner (each lane's question-mark count, summed), which the Arcs tab's badge shows. No action writes library data, and it carries no Library switch or artifact links. While its first read is on the way it says so, and a read that fails says so rather than drawing an empty board, keeping the last board it drew.

3.2 · Each root lane has its state chip, its title and its wait marks on line one, then its increments alone below: one fixed-size flat oval per increment in its state colour, finished ones first and then open ones, longest-waiting first, wrapping onto further lines when they do not fit, never more than four lines at the width drawn at (ADR-1226): past four, the landed ovals fold into one "N landed" mark at the strip's start, and open ovals still beyond four lines into a "+N" mark at its end, each mark's hover naming what it folds; a strip that fits is drawn whole. A claimed increment's oval carries its holder's flag (the globe's pennant in the session's colour, furled and greyed while the holder is idle), and the ovals sit close under the title, leaving only a flag's headroom (ADR-1003). The count ("3 landed · 1 not completed · 2 open", skipping zeros, never a percentage) is not shown; it is the ovals' accessible label, whole even when marks fold some (ADR-0980).

3.3 · Lanes sort by their arc's priority first, 1 first and unranked last, and a ranked lane shows it as "P1" beside its chip (ADR-0963). Within one priority they sort waiting, blocked, in progress, idle, ready, quiet, then the most recently active; a ready lane that also has idle claims sorts with the ready lanes. An arc tag never says claimed: a live holder reads "in progress" and an idle chip carries its age on its face ("in progress · idle 42 min", ADR-0949 D1), and its hover names who holds what; a ready lane that also has idle claims names them, with their age and the work held, in its chip's hover. At the right of its title a lane counts what its open increments wait on: an hourglass with the number of distinct other work and event note waits that still hold, and a question mark with the number of its open questions and owner note waits that still hold; a mark with nothing to count is not drawn, and each mark's hover and accessible label carry the full wording. Each bar's hover names its note waits (ADR-0938 D2, ADR-0980). Active shows on the first launch, then the saved scope is restored; Parked and Closed show only their own arcs, and there is no "All".
3.4 · In the app: a claim written while the overlay is open shows on it within about two seconds, without reopening.
3.5 · In the app: with no new line, a holder turns idle once the quiet time passes. The test uses a stand-in clock.

3.6 · In the app: the smoke check visits every scope and opens every root arc's caret, then judges document.body.dataset.drew.arcSurface against the expected root lanes, expanded queue chips, root-lane increment bars and their agent marks. It does not count +N descendants, queued increments or the increment rows an open caret shows as drawn bars.

3.7 · Between launches, each project remembers the arcs' scope (Active, Parked or Closed). No picked arc is kept, so no arc's card reopens on its own; a value kept before the rail is read for its scope alone.
3.8 · The app's Surfaces menu lists the arc surface as Arcs, with no settings, on until the user switches it off; switched off, it is saved and reads off at the next launch (ADR-0750)

The open board re-reads the work only when its news holds an arc, increment or question change: news of lines alone, or of other records, redraws it from the work it already has, with the new lines. It reads the work itself once when it starts and draws fresh when that lands, without waiting on the page reading's first read: told the page's start, it starts once that has settled, reading nothing and hearing no news before, so the start never waits on it (ADR-1224; story node render 3.49); told none, it starts when it is mounted. News the page held by then is not read again, and until its own read lands the board kept at the last start is drawn as refreshing. Each reading carries the library's waits for the owner or an event (waitsFor) with the holds; an absent one reads as none.

3.11 · The arc surface declares the `arc` family, with `arc increment` within it, and the `question` family, that the command line lists 2nd and 3rd: a question raised holding an increment on its arc holds it, an empty --held-on clears the hold, and retiring a record that is no question names library retire

3.12 · The board reads live arcs and those closed yesterday and today; the Closed tab's Today and Yesterday draw from that, and 7 days or a From–to asks the library for its window when it changes, the kept board holding only the routine read

3.13 · `arc status` gives one line per active arc, moving ones first, each with its state and why: Working (increment, session, machine, since), Landed since --since (with its pull request), Ready, Waiting on you (question titles or owner-wait notes), Blocked (on what, until when) or Idle (nothing parked); the strongest state printed, the other mentioned

3.14 · `arc status` reads the board's arcs and the holds once each however many arcs there are, counts landings from the last two hours unless --since names a time or a span (30m, 2h, 1d), and refuses any other --since
3.15 · `arc recent` lists what landed since --since grouped by arc, each landing with its title and its pull request, then the arcs that closed since then; withdrawn, open and older work is left out
3.16 · `arc recent` reads the board's arcs once, counts from the last 24 hours unless --since names a time or a span (30m, 2h, 1d), and refuses any other --since

3.17 · `arc increment edit --escape-of <pr|increment> --escape-story <story>` records the escape an increment fixes, `--escape-of none` clears it, and one flag without the other is refused with nothing written
3.18 · The mounted arcs say once when they first draw a freshly read board
3.19 · Once the project has a repository cut-over, arc recent and arc show say a pull request closed before it as the old repository's owner/name#n, and one closed on or after it as #n
3.20 · The opened arc's title stays selected in its card across a refresh that changes nothing, and a copy button beside it puts the title on the clipboard as plain text, saying Copied

3.21 · Opening an arc row's gutter caret shows under the row its questions, then its increments (open first, landed folded behind "N landed"), then its queued arcs, never its intent; a question's row opens the card on that question, and the open caret survives the live redraw.
3.22 · The question family declares predict, prediction, score and prep, each calling the library's step for it and printing what was stored or read; a refused step prints its reason and exits 1

3.23 · question deviation prints, for questions settled in its window (default the last 14 days), per confidence band, how many would-be answers matched, matched with changes, differed or were rejected, beside the raiser's recommendation on the same questions

capabilities.title: 4 · Waits
capabilities.description: Every arc or increment that waits on other work says so and names what it waits for: an arc queued behind another arc folds away under that arc’s lane, behind a ▸/▾ caret in a fixed gutter; expansion shows chips, and an increment waiting on another increment, on any arc, draws yellow and names its blocker and why. A blocker shows what it holds up, a wait that will never release by itself says so, and an arc with something waiting on you is never hidden under its blocker.

contracts.title: 4.1 · An arc waiting on an open arc, or whose every open increment waits on work in another open arc, appears only as a chip under that arc's initially collapsed caret, not also at the top; waiting on several, it sits under the first on the board. Selecting the chip opens the queued arc's briefing. Once the wait releases, or it has work nothing holds up, it returns to the top, with nothing written. Waits that form a loop are cut at the loop's first arc on the board, so no arc disappears (ADR-0760 D1).

4.2 · A one-behind-one queue draws as a chain (A → B → C). Two arcs behind one blocker draw as a set, with a · separator and no arrow between them. A queued arc that holds up others carries "+N", one also waiting on another arc says "+1 other wait", and one queued by its increments names the increment it waits on in the arc above it.
4.3 · An arc with a question waiting on you stays at the top while it waits on another arc, and its other open bars still read queued.

4.4 · An increment waiting on another names it, its arc and the reason, and the blocker names what it holds up. If the blocker closed without landing, or cannot be found, the wait says it will not release by itself.

capabilities.title: 5 · Briefing
capabilities.description: Picking a lane, or a queued arc, opens its briefing: rows you scan, each a door into its prose, and no prose until something is opened (ADR-0980 D5). The arc's intent is one folded line. Its questions are one table, open first, each row a title and a status (open or settled); opening a row replaces the table with the full reading, the answer on top when settled, and “← back to questions” restores it. The reading is statement first, with its stakes, diagram, options as for and against, a recommendation marked not binding, and the longer parts folded with their word counts. After the questions, every increment on the arc is a row: its colour, its title and one short cell of chips for what it is doing, landed ones folded behind one row; opening a row shows its objective, its waits by name, the questions it waits behind, what it holds up, who holds it and how it closed.

contracts.title: 5.1 · Clicking an arc's row opens its card, which shows its title, its intent folded behind one closed line, then its questions as one table, open first, each row its title and its status (open or settled); an arc with no questions shows no questions section. A card opens only on that click: none at launch or after a refresh, and one whose arc leaves the board closes.

5.2 · Opening a question row swaps the card's briefing for one full reading; “← back to questions” restores it. The full reading is statement first, then stakes, the diagram or "no diagram stored", options split into for and against, the recommendation marked not binding, and analogy and context folded with their word counts. The row itself shows no word count, no diagram note and none of the question's prose.

5.3 · A settled question stays in the one table, below the open ones, with its status "settled"; it stops counting as waiting, and its answer shows only when it is opened, on top of its reading. A settled question published with only its title and answer opens on those two alone, with no empty headings.
5.4 · A parked arc's briefing says once, on its questions, that the open ones are parked with the arc (they wait for it to be unparked), never "Waiting on you"

5.5 · After the questions, every increment on the arc is one row: its bar's colour, its title on one line and one short cell of chips, never a sentence: "you" when it waits on the owner (a held question, an owner note, or questions behind its waits), "N increment(s)" for waits on other work, "event", "check-back passed", "blocked" by another increment's claim, the holder's label with its quiet minutes, "to take", "not completed", or a landed one's pull request number. Open work comes first (waiting, in progress, to take), then not completed, then landed, folded behind one "N landed" row.

5.6 · Opening an increment row shows in place its objective, each wait by name with its reason (the name alone when it has none), the owner's questions it waits behind, what it holds up, who holds it and how it closed (disposition, pull request, note), never its planning body; the intent fold, the landed fold and opened rows stay open across the live redraw.

openWork.arcTitle: An assistant pass preps the owner's open questions before they reach him
openWork.title: Owner questions carry a sealed would-be answer, a prep mark and a score, with a deviation report

capabilities.title: 1 · Front door
capabilities.description: `storytree <family> <verb>` works out which project the folder you are in belongs to, opens that project's library, and hands the command to the owning story's function, keeping no rule of its own. Every answer is a short plain sentence or listing; where it names records it may offer, under `next:`, the commands that open them, and nothing else (ADR-0786). A failure exits non-zero and says what to do; a command it does not have answers with the real one for that job.

contracts.title: 7.2 · `changesSince(n)` returns only changes after `n`, in order, each carrying the new cursor to pass next time.

7.3 · The package's public entry exports exactly the documented API and nothing else, and its internals cannot be imported through the package. At runtime it exports `ANCHOR_ID`, `CONNECT_TIMEOUT_MS`, `CONTRACT_DEFINITION`, `ConnectionError`, `DependencyLoopError`, `LONG_CONTRACT_TITLE`, `LifecycleError`, `LinkLoopError`, `MissingReferenceError`, `MissingUpgradeError`, `NEW_LINE`, `NOT_VERIFIED`, `NewerSchemaError`, `NumberTakenError`, `OWNER_TIME_ZONE`, `ProjectGoneError`, `ProjectNameError`, `RestoreRefusedError`, `RetireRefusedError`, `SEED_CONNECTION`, `SchemaError`, `SupersessionLoopError`, `UnknownTypeError`, `WaitLoopError`, `anchorGaps`, `beforeCutover`, `connect`, `connectionString`, `explainConnectTimeout`, `heldBack`, `knowledgeGuidance`, `parseSchedule`, `planGuidance`, `pluginSchema`, `pullSaid`, `wordAndWhy`. Everything else exported is a data type, including WriteOptions, HistoryEntry, HistoryFilter and the literal phrase query options and page. The connection offers exactly `openProject`, `listProjects`, `projectIdentities`, `snapshot`, `restore`, `dropProject`, `ownDatabase`, `close`. A project library offers exactly `name`, `identity`, `factory`, `markFactory`, `recordFactory`, `get`, `list`, `inherited`, `history`, `addStory`, `createArc`, `addCapability`, `editStory`, `editCapability`, `addContract`, `editContract`, `editArc`, `projectTree`, `arcsFor`, `addIncrement`, `advanceIncrement`, `closeIncrement`, `moveIncrement`, `editIncrement`, `parkArc`, `unparkArc`, `arcView`, `arcViews`, `addWait`, `removeWait`, `waitHolds`, `addWaitFor`, `removeWaitFor`, `waitsFor`, `holds`, `raiseQuestion`, `settleQuestion`, `questions`, `heldOnQuestion`, `checkQuestion`, `renewQuestion`, `editQuestion`, `lapsedQuestions`, `reportHealth`, `recordVerified`, `health`, `healthHistory`, `healthWorklist`, `recordDecision`, `numberDecision`, `numberDecisionsFromFullRecord`, `numberFoundingDecisions`, `setDecisionNumberFloor`, `setProposed`, `decisionNumberPlan`, `defineTerm`, `writeKnowledge`, `definitions`, `editNote`, `search`, `searchEach`, `rank`, `rankAll`, `findPhrase`, `relatedNotes`, `related`, `relatedEach`, `frontCovers`, `decision`, `decisions`, `composeStatement`, `retire`, `changesSince`, capability 27's fixed data questions `counts`, `latestChanges`, `findByTitle` and `decisionNumbered`, `recordFyi`, `unheardFyis`, `markFyisHeard`, `createPluginRecord`, `editPluginRecord`, `pluginRecords`, `removePluginRecords`, `dormantKinds`, `close`. Project handles expose no pool, store or table; the connection's ownDatabase is the deliberate exception described by 7.7.

7.1 · An end-to-end "agent's day" against a real local Postgres: open a project, create an arc, add a story, a capability and a contract, report passing, record verified, record a decision as the capability's front cover and write a definition inside it, then read `projectTree()` and `changesSince(0)`. Every step is visible where the next step expects it.

7.4 · `editStory`, `editContract` and `editArc` change only the fields they name, merged onto what is stored now, and check a new reference as adding does (a contract's capability, an arc's stories). Each gives `null`, writing nothing, for an id that is not a live record of its type.

7.5 · `get`, `list` and `history` return whole records through the public API, agreeing with the in-memory twin. Live reads upgrade old records; history preserves original writes, including actors and retirement reasons, and can filter by id and sequence. Reads write nothing.
7.6 · Every public write carries its optional actor to history, as in 2.10. Health can name a writer separately from its reporter; omitting the writer preserves its existing `by` attribution.

7.7 · A connection hands its caller one named database of its own beside the projects, on the same server, local or Cloud SQL: created the first time (borrowing a granted creator role where the user may not create databases), never listed as a project, closed with the connection. Handed its table definitions, the library sets it up too (ADR-0973): only the statements the database has not yet applied, in one transaction under the database's own lock, so connections setting it up at once all succeed and one opening a database already set up runs no DDL a concurrent writer could block or deadlock; a caller that only reads may leave them out.
7.8 · `arcViews()` returns every live arc's view in a few reads, not one per arc
7.10 · projectTree marks a parked capability with its arc

7.18 · sendFeedback writes a feedback record, with the element it points at, and keeps its screenshot and the crop to that element beside it, out of the record's history; feedbackScreenshot returns the bytes, and none for a note sent without one

7.19 · routeFeedback marks a new feedback record routed with its route, target and reason; a missing, non-feedback or already routed record is refused with nothing written, and a routed record must carry its route and reason

7.20 · printable(text) turns every control character a terminal would act on (C0 but line breaks, tabs and a line-ending carriage return, DEL, C1) into a placeholder, from a light entry that imports nothing
7.21 · createPluginRecord saves a record of a plugin's kind the project was opened with, and refuses any other
7.22 · pluginRecords lists a plugin's records by kind with count and ids; removePluginRecords removes exactly that listing, refusing a stale one
