15.4 · A contract the increment rewords through a pending change is in its brief in the pending text, marked pending, and one it retires through a pending change is listed as retired with its reason and is not to be answered; a return that answers a retired one is refused, naming it. Each appears in the brief once: its plan change is not listed again among the pending plan changes, so a return answering it once is taken.
15.5 · The brief lists each contract under its story and capability, so two stories' contracts sharing a number both appear, each with its story
15.6 · The diff read from a worktree holds its uncommitted work too, edits and new files Git does not ignore; a folder whose origin names no default branch is read against its own commit

15.7 · In a repository with no origin/main the brief's diff is read against its local default branch (init.defaultBranch, else main, else master), and the brief names that branch as the repository's own
15.8 · The brief reads the change from the worktree on the branch its increment was claimed on, wherever the brief runs, and is refused naming that branch when no worktree is on it
15.9 · A return names the review it answers, and take refuses one naming another review, such as a return left from an earlier review, recording nothing
15.10 · A plan-only change, whose diff touches no file, gets a brief listing its pending plan changes as the thing under review; one with neither a diff nor a pending change is still refused
15.11 · A low-tier change gets a light pass, judged from its diff alone; medium, high or an unread tier gets the full brief

15.12 · The brief lists each change-triggered guardrail of the stories and capabilities the increment names; the return answers each passed or failed with pictures, and a failed one stands until a later review passes it

15.13 · A return says of each contract whether the change touches it; a touched contract answered met names the test that covers it, or is taken as a hit at the changed line asking for one, and one the change adds or rewords cannot be answered untouched
15.14 · A new test with no saved red run naming it failing is a hit
15.15 · A red run saved in another worktree counts when its commit is in this worktree's history
15.16 · `quality brief` and `take` review a change in a named checkout outside the project, as the owner's factory repo is, and record it in the project's ledger

15.17 · A check that names the projects it applies to is in the brief only of a change in one of those projects; a check that names none is in every project's brief, so a user's project, reading its factory's checks, is not asked storytree's own

15.18 · The brief of a change to a factory plugin's story carries the factory branch's diff and the plugin plan's contracts, refuses to count them met when that branch is unread, and reads the plugin crossed only when no branch carries the change

15.19 · `quality brief --also <folder>`, given once per checkout, lists each outside checkout's diff beside the change's own in one brief, and `quality take --also` runs the graduated checks there too
15.20 · A test a factory worktree's or an --also checkout's diff adds is listed with whether that checkout's saved red runs name it failing, and one none names is a hit
15.21 · A test that only moved or was renumbered is not a new test
15.22 · The brief lists the library records the increment's sessions wrote since claiming it, as part of the change under review

15.23 · A check's answer may name places without tripping it, each with its file, line and what it is; the take keeps them in the return and prints them under their check, and refuses a named place with no file, line or words

15.24 · `quality brief` and `take` run with no --checkout read the factory's worktree on a branch carrying the increment's id as the change's other half, though no capability the increment names is a plugin's, and the brief is refused naming such a branch with no worktree on it

15.25 · A brief whose change spans more than one repository opens with an index of its diffs: one line per repository, naming its checkout, its changed files' count and the brief line its diff starts at; a one-repository brief has none

15.26 · A brief whose contracts would run past what one read shows lists each contract the change leaves untouched in one short line, its id and the start of its title under its capability, with the command that reads it whole; every check, and every contract the change rewords or its diffs name by number, stays whole

capabilities.title: 16 · QA ledger
capabilities.description:
The record of what quality control finds, kept in the library's Postgres (ADR-0956 D4). Every review records, for each check it ran, whether it hit, and for each hit the implementer's answer: fixed, or rejected with a reason. Rows are scoped by check, project and package from the first row, because products differ in shape and a global count hides where a check matters. Its reading gives the counts per check per package, the same from both front doors. It only records: nothing here samples, reduces or retires a check (ADR-0956 D6).

Not settled by this plan (2026-10-10, raised with the dispatching session): where the rows sit inside the library's Postgres, as a record type the library declares, or as this story's own tables reached through the library's connection, as the agent link's activity log is. The contracts hold either way.

contracts.title: 7.2 · `changesSince(n)` returns only changes after `n`, in order, each carrying the new cursor to pass next time.

7.3 · The package's public entry exports exactly the documented API and nothing else, and its internals cannot be imported through the package. At runtime it exports `ANCHOR_ID`, `CONNECT_TIMEOUT_MS`, `CONTRACT_DEFINITION`, `ConnectionError`, `DependencyLoopError`, `LONG_CONTRACT_TITLE`, `LifecycleError`, `LinkLoopError`, `MissingReferenceError`, `MissingUpgradeError`, `NEW_LINE`, `NOT_VERIFIED`, `NewerSchemaError`, `NumberTakenError`, `OWNER_TIME_ZONE`, `ProjectGoneError`, `ProjectNameError`, `RestoreRefusedError`, `RetireRefusedError`, `SEED_CONNECTION`, `SchemaError`, `SupersessionLoopError`, `UnknownTypeError`, `WaitLoopError`, `anchorGaps`, `beforeCutover`, `connect`, `connectionString`, `explainConnectTimeout`, `heldBack`, `knowledgeGuidance`, `parseSchedule`, `planGuidance`, `pluginSchema`, `pullSaid`, `wordAndWhy`. Everything else exported is a data type, including WriteOptions, HistoryEntry, HistoryFilter and the literal phrase query options and page. The connection offers exactly `openProject`, `listProjects`, `projectIdentities`, `snapshot`, `restore`, `dropProject`, `ownDatabase`, `close`. A project library offers exactly `name`, `identity`, `factory`, `markFactory`, `recordFactory`, `get`, `list`, `inherited`, `history`, `addStory`, `createArc`, `addCapability`, `editStory`, `editCapability`, `addContract`, `editContract`, `editArc`, `projectTree`, `arcsFor`, `addIncrement`, `advanceIncrement`, `closeIncrement`, `moveIncrement`, `editIncrement`, `parkArc`, `unparkArc`, `arcView`, `arcViews`, `addWait`, `removeWait`, `waitHolds`, `addWaitFor`, `removeWaitFor`, `waitsFor`, `holds`, `raiseQuestion`, `settleQuestion`, `questions`, `heldOnQuestion`, `checkQuestion`, `renewQuestion`, `editQuestion`, `lapsedQuestions`, `reportHealth`, `recordVerified`, `health`, `healthHistory`, `healthWorklist`, `recordDecision`, `numberDecision`, `numberDecisionsFromFullRecord`, `numberFoundingDecisions`, `setDecisionNumberFloor`, `setProposed`, `decisionNumberPlan`, `defineTerm`, `writeKnowledge`, `definitions`, `editNote`, `search`, `searchEach`, `rank`, `rankAll`, `findPhrase`, `relatedNotes`, `related`, `relatedEach`, `frontCovers`, `decision`, `decisions`, `composeStatement`, `retire`, `changesSince`, capability 27's fixed data questions `counts`, `latestChanges`, `findByTitle` and `decisionNumbered`, `recordFyi`, `unheardFyis`, `markFyisHeard`, `createPluginRecord`, `editPluginRecord`, `pluginRecords`, `removePluginRecords`, `dormantKinds`, `close`. Project handles expose no pool, store or table; the connection's ownDatabase is the deliberate exception described by 7.7.

7.1 · An end-to-end "agent's day" against a real local Postgres: open a project, create an arc, add a story, a capability and a contract, report passing, record verified, record a decision as the capability's front cover and write a definition inside it, then read `projectTree()` and `changesSince(0)`. Every step is visible where the next step expects it.

7.4 · `editStory`, `editContract` and `editArc` change only the fields they name, merged onto what is stored now, and check a new reference as adding does (a contract's capability, an arc's stories). Each gives `null`, writing nothing, for an id that is not a live record of its type.

7.5 · `get`, `list` and `history` return whole records through the public API, agreeing with the in-memory twin. Live reads upgrade old records; history preserves original writes, including actors and retirement reasons, and can filter by id and sequence. Reads write nothing.
7.6 · Every public write carries its optional actor to history, as in 2.10. Health can name a writer separately from its reporter; omitting the writer preserves its existing `by` attribution.

7.7 · A connection hands its caller one named database of its own beside the projects, on the same server, local or Cloud SQL: created the first time (borrowing a granted creator role where the user may not create databases), never listed as a project, closed with the connection. Handed its table definitions, the library sets it up too (ADR-0973): only the statements the database has not yet applied, in one transaction under the database's own lock, so connections setting it up at once all succeed and one opening a database already set up runs no DDL a concurrent writer could block or deadlock; a caller that only reads may leave them out.
7.8 · `arcViews()` returns every live arc's view in a few reads, not one per arc
7.10 · projectTree marks a parked capability with its arc

7.18 · sendFeedback writes a feedback record, with the element it points at, and keeps its screenshot and the crop to that element beside it, out of the record's history; feedbackScreenshot returns the bytes, and none for a note sent without one

7.19 · routeFeedback marks a new feedback record routed with its route, target and reason; a missing, non-feedback or already routed record is refused with nothing written, and a routed record must carry its route and reason

7.20 · printable(text) turns every control character a terminal would act on (C0 but line breaks, tabs and a line-ending carriage return, DEL, C1) into a placeholder, from a light entry that imports nothing
7.21 · createPluginRecord saves a record of a plugin's kind the project was opened with, and refuses any other
7.22 · pluginRecords lists a plugin's records by kind with count and ids; removePluginRecords removes exactly that listing, refusing a stale one

7.23 · recordFyi keeps what the owner should know with its title, what happened, when (now when not given), what it is about and who noticed it; unheardFyis lists those he has not heard, oldest first; markFyisHeard marks them heard, so they are listed no more but stay in history, and refuses an id that is no FYI with nothing written (ADR-1184 D3)
7.24 · editPluginRecord changes a record of a plugin's kind the project was opened with, once-only when checkCurrent refuses, and refuses any other

7.25 · `changesSince(n, { types, actions })` hands out only the changes of those record types and actions after `n`, oldest first, with the cursor of the last change it kept, or `n` when it kept none, so a seed export reads only the change kinds it keeps.

16.1 · Recording a review writes, for each check it ran and each package the change touches, that the check ran there and each hit it made (the file and the line), with the review, the project and the time; a check that ran and did not hit is recorded as ran, and a second connection to the library's Postgres reads the rows back.

16.2 · The implementer's answer is recorded on a hit as fixed, or as rejected with its reason; a rejection with no reason, and an answer to a hit the ledger does not hold, are refused and nothing is written; a hit not yet answered reads unanswered.

16.3 · The ledger's reading gives, for each check and each package of a project, how many reviews ran it, how many hits it made, and those hits by answer (fixed, rejected, unanswered); a check that ran and never hit reads ran with no hits, never absent, and another project's rows are never counted.
16.4 · The command line and the agent link's tool give the same ledger reading, each through this package's public API; the tool is the one this package registers on the agent link's server.
16.5 · The project records this package contributes through its manifest's projectRecords forget a project's ledger runs and hits as it is deleted, and leave another project's

capabilities.title: 17 · Review loop bound
capabilities.description: A review may loop: one iteration is one review and the implementer's answer to each finding. A change is not ready for the gate while a finding stands, which is a hit nobody has answered, or one rejected for a reason the reviewer has not accepted. From the second review on, the brief reads only what changed since the last review (ADR-1120 D2). After three iterations with a finding still standing the loop stops and becomes the owner's question on the owning arc, which the session raises in ADR-0944 D4's order (ADR-1120 D1, replacing ADR-0956 D7's ten). The three are the branch's: an increment landed in several pull requests gets three reviews on each. It is a bound on disagreement, not a checklist to pass: the implementer's reasoned rejection is an answer the reviewer may accept.

contracts.title: 17.1 · A change's standing findings are the hits nobody has answered, the rejections no later review has accepted, and the contracts the latest review found not met; a hit answered fixed, a rejection a later review accepted, or a contract a later review found met, does not stand, and a change with none reads ready for the gate.

17.2 · From a change's second review on, the brief also holds each earlier hit with the implementer's answer to it, and the return must say of each rejection whether the reviewer accepts its reason; a return that leaves a rejection unjudged is refused, naming it, and nothing is recorded.

17.3 · Each review of one change is one iteration: with a finding still standing after the third, a fourth brief is refused, and the refusal names the owning arc and the findings that stand, for the session to raise as an open question there; the refusal itself raises no question and releases no claim, and a change with no finding standing after the third is not refused.
17.4 · The command line and the agent link's tools record the same answer to a hit and give the same standing findings, each through this package's public API.

17.5 · From a change's second review on, a brief read from its worktree holds only the diff since the last review taken, naming that review, while its packages stay the whole change's; once the branch has taken in its default branch since, the brief holds the whole diff again.

17.6 · A change's three reviews are its branch's: a review whose commit its default branch has since taken in (an earlier merged pull request's of the same increment), whose commit the repository does not hold at all (another repository's, as a branch rebuilt in a fresh history finds), or whose commit the branch's own history does not hold (another branch's of the same increment, an earlier lane's), does not count toward the three, while one branch still stops at three
17.7 · A contract finding stands only while the increment still names its contract
17.8 · An accepted rejection is not re-taken by a later review

17.9 · A finding standing only on a line the change's diff does not change does not refuse the fourth brief on its own, so a fourth review judges it; with it still standing after the fourth, the fifth brief is refused

capabilities.title: 18 · Graduation
capabilities.description: Graduating a check moves all of it, or the part of it that is a fixed pattern, from the reviewer to a deterministic check in Graduated checks (capability 22, ADR-0956 D5). The check's record says which part graduated and where it is now enforced; the part that still needs judgement stays with the reviewer. Graduated checks do not reach the library, so this capability runs them on the change under review and records what they find in the QA ledger, under the check each graduated from.

contracts.title: 18.1 · Graduating a check, whole or in part, writes on its record which part graduated and the graduated check that now enforces it, and the checks reading shows both; naming a graduated check that does not exist is refused, and nothing is written.
18.2 · A check graduated whole is no longer in the review brief; one graduated in part stays in it with the graduated part named, so the reviewer judges only the rest.

18.3 · Recording a review also records what the graduated checks (capability 22) find on the same change: each as ran, with each hit, under the check it graduated from, by project and package, marked as the graduated check's and not the reviewer's; the ledger's reading counts them under that check.

capabilities.title: 19 · Risk reading
capabilities.description: Reads a change's risk line (tier, rating, depth, radius, flags, stories) from its diff and the package graph, and each story's standing risk reading from its package's code, deterministically (question_1740edf77e9e, question_0f21964e8ce0).

contracts.title: 19.1 · A change's risk line is read from its diff and the package graph
19.2 · Each story's standing risk reading is read from its package's code and its place in the graph
19.3 · `quality risk` writes an increment's risk line, and `quality story-risks` every story's reading, each run as a write, so its history entries name the session or person who ran it
19.4 · `quality story-risks` writes no history for a story whose reading has not changed since its last run, whatever day it is read

capabilities.title: 20 · Mutation report
capabilities.description: Each change gets a small mutation report (ADR-1153 D1): at most one deliberate break per changed line, about 15 at most, run against only the tests that reach the line's file; arid lines are left out, and each break no test notices is a hit recorded with the review, ranked by what depends on its file. It never blocks a merge.

contracts.title: 20.1 · A change's breaks are at most one per changed source line, about 15 in all spread across them, and none on an arid line: a logging or output call, an upper-case constant's setting, or a line on the arid list

20.2 · Each break runs against only the tests that reach its file; one no test notices survives, ranked by how many files depend on its file, a file no test reaches survives untried, and tests that fail unbroken are left out, a break with none left not run and said so

20.3 · The brief read from a change's worktree carries its mutation report, and taking that review's return records each survivor as a hit found by the mutation report, which the implementer answers like any other

20.4 · A rejected survivor's line joins the arid list and is not offered again, and the rejection stands without a reviewer accepting it, so the report never holds a change back; a report that cannot run says why and never refuses a brief

20.5 · A break its own package's tests miss, or cannot judge because they all fail unbroken, is run against the tests downstream that reach its file before it is called a survivor; one those tests cannot judge either, or the report's time runs out on, is not run, never a survivor
20.6 · A break is caught when a test that passed with nothing broken no longer passes with it planted, so a test failing unbroken leaves out only itself, not the other tests in its file
20.8 · A report never changes the checkout it is given: its breaks are planted in a copy, and a killed report's copy is removed by the next one
20.9 · A killed report's throwaway Postgres is stopped, and its folder removed, by the next report

20.10 · The brief's mutation report also runs on each outside checkout it reads, a factory worktree or an --also checkout, its survivors recorded as hits with the review, or says why it did not run there
20.11 · A line the change adds exactly as a line it deletes, in its own diff or an outside checkout's, gets no break; the lines it edited still do
20.12 · Beside a file's judged breaks, a report names each test file reaching it that it left out for failing with nothing broken

capabilities.title: 21 · Verified test run
capabilities.description: storytree runs a project's test command itself and records the result against the folder's files, so the next role in a user's build loop (the orchestrator after the green builder, the reviewer) reads that run instead of running a slow suite again.

contracts.title: 21.1 · run_tests runs the command in the folder and records its exit code, time and last lines against the folder's files and the command, answering passed or failed with them

21.2 · run_tests with the same command at the same files, committed or not, answers from the recorded run, naming who ran it and when, without running it; an edited or new file, another command, or fresh runs it again
21.3 · run_tests in a folder outside any Git repository is refused, saying why, with nothing run

21.4 · storytree run-tests <command> [--fresh], with no library or MCP server, runs and records the same verified run as run_tests and prints its answer; a run either door recorded at the same files and command is answered by the other without running it; outside a Git repository it is refused, saying why

capabilities.title: 22 · Graduated checks
capabilities.description: Deterministic checks on a change, run from a checkout far more often than CI runs. Each is all of a quality control check, or the part of one that is a fixed pattern, graduated from the reviewer (ADR-0956 D5). Run on the files a branch changes against origin/main, it reports every place a graduated check trips, by the check's name, the file and the line. It reads the checkout alone and records nothing: Graduation (capability 18) runs it and records its hits in the QA ledger. Moved from storytree's Architecture checks story (its capability 4, packages/guardrails) by increment_9a2329880e8b.

contracts.title: 22.1 · Run on a change in a checkout (the files its branch changes against origin/main), each graduated check reports every place it trips, with the check's name, the file and the line (for example a constant asserted equal to itself); a change that trips none reports none, and a tripping line in a file the change does not touch is not reported.
22.2 · It needs no plan, library or running app and writes nothing: it reads the checkout alone, and what it found is its answer, for the caller to record.

capabilities.title: 23 · The check command
capabilities.description: `storytree check`, run in a checkout, runs storytree's package rule and allocation rule (repo-checks' capabilities 9 and 10, imported through the storytree link) and the graduated checks (capability 22) over it and reports every failure plainly, exiting non-zero, or says it passes and exits zero. It reads the checkout alone. The same allocation rule is contributed as a claim check, so a landing on a capability is held while its story package has a source file no numbered test reaches. Moved from storytree's Architecture checks story (its capabilities 3 and 2's claim check, packages/guardrails) by increment_9a2329880e8b; the pipeline job that ran it in a user's CI waits on question_79c1d337e180.

contracts.title: 23.1 · `storytree check` run in a checkout reports every package-rule and allocation failure plainly and exits non-zero; a checkout that keeps both rules prints that it passes and exits zero.
23.2 · It needs no plan, library or running app: it reads the checkout alone.
23.4 · A project whose package depends on an imported app outside it, by link: and deep file paths, passes the check; a rule broken inside the project still fails it
23.5 · `storytree check` reads the frames a checkout declares in its storytree.check.json: a package in a declared frame passes the package rule, one in no story and no declared frame fails it
23.6 · `storytree check` reads the sanctioned edges a checkout declares in its storytree.check.json: a sanctioned story-to-frame edge passes the package rule, an unsanctioned one fails it

23.7 · micks-dev-loop declares the `check` verb the command line mounts: run with no caller, in a folder that is no project, it answers with the check's report and refuses with it when a rule is broken

23.8 · `storytree check` runs the graduated self-equal assertion check on what the branch changes against origin/main: a test asserting an expression equal to itself fails the check, named by file and line; without origin/main it says the check did not run, never that it was kept

23.11 · micks-dev-loop contributes its allocation rule as a claim check: for a capability, the source files of its story's package no numbered test reaches; none for a capability the plan lacks (ADR-1170 D2)

capabilities.title: 24 · The placement report
capabilities.description: Rule 5 of the story rules (the journey principle, ADR-1078), counted at the package level as ADR-1085 D3 narrows it. For each package of a checkout it counts the other packages whose production code imports it, type-only imports included, as the map's code survey reads them. Delivery mechanisms (the front-door frames, and the composition root the checkout declares) and plumbing calls (forwarders the survey detects; build steps and cleanups the checkout declares) are listed but not counted. It says the placement each count implies, and names each package placed differently from today, with the loop a move would make. `storytree check` prints it, and it never fails the check. Its settings live in the checkout's storytree.check.json: the threshold, the composition root, the declared plumbing, and off. Moved from storytree's Architecture checks story (its capability 5, packages/guardrails) by increment_9a2329880e8b.

contracts.title: 24.1 · A package's counted callers are the other packages whose production code imports it, type-only imports included; tests and testing helpers make none
24.2 · The front-door frames' imports and the declared composition root's are listed as delivery mechanisms, not counted
24.3 · A forwarder the code survey detects, and a build step or cleanup storytree.check.json declares, is listed as plumbing by its kind, not counted

24.4 · Each count implies a placement: at or above the threshold its own story, one caller inside that story, none its own story, between them separate ways; a package placed differently from today is named, with the loop moving it would make
24.5 · storytree check prints the placement report and never fails on it; placement off leaves it out

openWork.arcTitle: An assistant pass preps the owner's open questions before they reach him
openWork.title: catch_up and grill-me read the prep: retirements, agreements, then disagreements in full

capabilities.title: 8 · Code survey
capabilities.description: Surveys story source packages and app frame paths (apps/desktop/src) for file ownership, source line counts and imports. Retains tests with numbered N.M titles and import edges, separately tagged as tests and excluded from source line counts. Ownership follows existing nearest numbered-test reach, execution coverage and type-import rules (8.1, 8.6, 8.7); unmatched files remain unclaimed. Lives in packages/map under ADR-0864; the forest consumes this survey for drawing. Callers may survey the current checkout explicitly. The main default reads immutable Git blobs from fetched origin/main, with shared bounded asynchronous fetches, keeping the last fetched main offline and reporting failure when none exists. A start's reader (the desktop's) answers its first ask from the main already fetched while it fetches, and its next ask waits on that fetch (8.27). No checkout is changed. Without origin, the primary folder is surveyed; non-Git folders are read directly. Unchanged blob identities retain file and story surveys. The forest owns request pacing; each later request checks for the next landing, so no cooldown can swallow its only refresh.

contracts.title: 8.1 · A source file a test titled "N.M …" reaches belongs to capability N of that test's story, whether the test imports it directly or reaches it through any number of further ordinary imports and re-exports. When tests of several capabilities reach it, the capability whose tests reach it nearest (fewest ordinary imports away; a re-export adds none) owns it, then the one whose tests reach it that near most, then the lower number.
8.3 · A file's lines of code are counted for source files only: a test file, or a test helper under a testing/ folder, adds no lines to any file, capability or story.
8.4 · A relative import from one source file to another is reported as a link from the importing file to the imported one.
8.5 · Surveying again reads no unchanged file (same path and Git blob in a merged snapshot, or size and modified time on disk), reads changed files again, and reuses an unchanged story survey.

8.6 · A source file a numbered test's runs executed, in its own process or one it started, belongs to the capability whose tests executed it most (the package's coverage map); a direct import outranks it, and it outranks a file reached only through further imports.

8.7 · A source file a numbered test reaches only through type imports (a file of types, or one imported only for its types) belongs to the capability whose tests reach it so nearest, then most; any reach by a value import or by running it outranks a reach by types.
8.8 · Each surveyed story names the stories whose packages its package depends on, through any dependency field of its package.json.
8.9 · The survey includes apps/desktop/src files under the app story, attributing their capabilities by the same numbered-test ownership rules as package source files.

8.10 · The survey retains test files tagged as tests, their N.M numbered test titles and their import edges, without adding them to source file, capability or story line counts. Number lists are validated before expansion: at most 256 entries per title and 4096 per surveyed test file, counting repeated entries before deduplication; invalid or over-budget titles supply no proof identities and do not stop other files from surveying.

8.11 · Selecting current surveys that checkout, including local changes. The main default surveys fetched origin/main without changing any checkout, follows subsequent landings, and shares bounded asynchronous Git work per repository. If origin is unavailable it retains the last fetched main; without one it reports failure, in words that name why (Git's own reason, such as an origin with no main or one that cannot be read, or the reason its fetch was skipped) and that tell the refusal apart by its message alone. A repository without origin, or a non-Git folder, keeps the primary-folder reading.

8.12 · A CommonJS `require` of a string naming a relative file, or the package's own exported subpath, is an ordinary import: a test reaches what it requires and everything that requires in turn, so a CommonJS package's files fall in the capabilities whose tests reach them

8.13 · A numbered test outside the package’s src reaches its source as a test in src would; outside src the reader follows test files and their helper dependencies within the package, without counting their lines as source or reading unrelated scripts
8.14 · A test file that runs an imported behaviour suite carries the suite's numbered titles

8.15 · A source file's opening "Capability N · <title>" declaration (after a shebang) puts it on capability N's territory when N's numbered tests or coverage map reach it; a declaration they do not reach, or an undeclared file, is allocated by inference
8.16 · A survey can be read on a worker thread: the same answer as reading it in place, while the asking thread's event loop stays free

8.17 · A changed file is placed in its capability by its own declaration, else by the survey's inference, flagged as inferred; a file in no story's package, or a file that cannot be read, is placed nowhere
8.18 · A source file's import of a name from another story's package is an edge from its capability to the capability of the file that defines the name, type-only when every import behind it is
8.19 · A derived edge whose file at either end has no capability is kept as a story-to-story edge, naming the files that cause it

8.20 · A mapped story is surveyed from the folder this machine imports it from: the files of a language the survey reads tracked at its checkout's commit under its folders, leaving out the skip list's folders and a folder another package of the same import maps, each with its non-blank lines and no capability, read without parsing; a mapped story whose import this machine does not name is absent
8.21 · A mapped story's package dependency on another mapped story's package is a road between them; a loop among mapped stories is reported with the stories round it, and refuses nothing
8.22 · Surveying again while an imported checkout is at the same commit reads none of its files and keeps each mapped story's survey; at a new commit only the files whose blob changed are read
8.23 · A built story's package dependency on a mapped story's package is a road from it to the mapped story; a mapped story's dependency on a built story's package is never a road

8.24 · Work done at source in an imported checkout counts before it is committed there: a changed or new file Git does not ignore is read from disk over the commit's tree, a deleted one leaves, and only those files are read; while that work is unchanged a survey again reads none of them

8.25 · A start whose fetched main is the commit last surveyed, with the same plan, answers from the survey kept between starts without reading or parsing a file; another plan or a newer main is surveyed afresh and kept in its turn

8.26 · a mapped story's file under the folders or files an explored capability covers carries that capability, work not yet committed included; the rest carry none, and a change of covers is read at the same commit
8.27 · A start's reader answers its first ask from the main already fetched while it fetches, and its next ask waits on that fetch and surveys what it brought

8.28 · A '#' specifier the importing package's package.json imports field names literally is an ordinary import of the file it maps to, so a file reached only that way falls in the capability whose numbered test imports it

8.29 · A source file whose opening header's title is not the title of the capability its number names in its story (as a file moved from another story keeps) declares nothing: it is placed by the survey's inference, or nowhere, never in the capability its stale number names

8.30 · A story that owns several packages has each package's files surveyed under its capabilities, paths from the package named after its title, and its edit claims and tested numbers read from every one
8.31 · An edge file whose source file declares nothing of its own, imports nothing of its own package and passes on names from one other story's package is marked a forwarder
8.32 · A numbered test in any script extension's test file carries its contract's number
8.33 · Declared build steps and cleanups are marked on survey edges

8.34 · A test file's esbuild entry point, written as a literal new URL("./x", import.meta.url) inside an entryPoints array, is an ordinary import of the file it names, so a module a numbered test bundles for the browser falls in that test's capability

8.35 · The survey's Git runs no program its repository's settings name, and its fetch of main is skipped, with the reason, when those settings name an upload program, an ssh command or a credential helper

8.36 · A pytest test whose name is test_<n>_<m>_… or whose docstring starts <n>.<m>, in a test_*.py or *_test.py file anywhere in the checkout but Git's ignored files, carries that contract number for the landing check
8.37 · A pytest number prefixed with a story's package counts for that story only, and an unprefixed one counts for a story only while no other story plans a contract with that number

8.38 · Each path given, absolute or relative to the folder, is placed in its checkout: its story and that story's package, apps/desktop for the desktop app's, even for a file the survey does not read, and its capability when it declares one or the survey infers it; a path in no story's package is placed nowhere

8.39 · A bare specifier naming another package of the same story is an ordinary import of the file its exports map it to, so a test in one of a story's packages reaches the files of its other package it imports; another story's package stays unreached

8.40 · Reading a capability's story tests says whether its story's package was seen in the checkout: a story with no package there, and no pytest numbers, is unseen; testedNumbers still reads the numbers alone

8.41 · Deciding which strings are a call's first argument reads each prefix of a test file at most once in total, so the characters its patterns read grow with the file, not with strings × file length
8.42 · a current-checkout reader given its code's name answers a fresh start on an unchanged checkout from the survey kept in the checkout's Git directory, reading no file
8.43 · the survey code's name changes when any of the survey's own source files changes, or its bundle does, and is none when they cannot be read

8.44 · reading a mapped story's tests finds its numbered titles where it was imported from: the checkout itself when that is the import (by its top or its origin), else the folder this machine imports it from; a mapped story whose import is neither is unseen

8.45 · an import from a source file of one capability to a source file of another in the same story derives an edge between them in the story's survey edges, to its own story, following re-exports to the file that defines what it takes, type-only when every such import takes types alone; imports within one capability derive none

8.46 · a source file that calls composeParts with a literal manifest kind derives an edge from its capability to the capability of the file defining each part of that kind that a story package its own package depends on declares in its storytree manifest
8.47 · tree-sitter's Python grammar loads from its wasm bytes and parses a .py file's imports and definitions

8.48 · a bundle built with the survey's tree-sitter plugin carries the engine and the grammar in itself: as CommonJS, as the app's survey worker is, and as split ES modules, as the commands and hooks are, it parses a .py file from a folder with no node_modules
8.49 · A mapped Python package's .py files are drawn on its island through the survey's Python reader, each with its non-blank lines, its test files and conftest.py among them; nothing parses them

8.50 · a built Python story's imports are edges in its survey: import a.b, from a import y (a submodule, else the package), a wildcard, relative levels, nested imports and namespace packages, searched from its src/ then its root; a mapped island's from src/ then the top
8.51 · a Python source file's opening "# Capability N · title", after an optional shebang, declares its capability when the title is its number's, and nothing when the title is another's
8.52 · a built Python story's pyproject.toml makes roads to the stories whose projects it names, by [project].dependencies or a [tool.uv.sources] workspace source, names compared normalised

8.53 · The code survey names the languages a folder's code is in: those it reads, agreeing with the files its readers read, and those it cannot read, from Git's tracked files in a checkout, else a walk

8.54 · a built Python story's pytest tests, module functions and methods of a Test* class, carry the number their name (test_2_3_…, perhaps after the package) or their docstring starts with, and pin the files they reach to that capability
8.55 · a built Python story's numbered pytest test, read by both the survey and the checkout-wide pytest read, is counted once in its story's tested numbers
8.56 · the map's index bundles for the browser, as the desktop page does, with no Node module reachable from it: a reader importing one goes red here, naming the import and its importer

capabilities.title: 1 · Joined graph
capabilities.description: Read-only graph of plan, code and tests, owned by packages/map. Demonstrate Projects 2.5 reached from the desktop view file using a fixture plan.

contracts.title: 4.1 · Add a story, a capability under it and a contract under that, and `projectTree()` returns them nested: story › capability › contract.
4.2 · An arc listing that story is returned by `arcsFor(storyId)`. An arc listing no stories is accepted.
4.3 · A capability naming a missing (or retired) story is refused, as is a contract naming a missing capability and an arc listing a missing story.
4.4 · A capability depending on another capability that does not exist is refused.
4.5 · A dependency loop between capabilities (A → B → A, or longer) is refused, and nothing is written.

4.6 · A capability is born proposed. The agent switches the flag off, and back on, and history names the writer; only a live capability has the flag, and a capability written before the flag reads proposed.

4.7 · A contract planned without a number is given its capability's next free one (after the highest its live contracts carry); a title whose number another live contract of the capability carries is refused, on planning and on correcting, and nothing is written. A capability with no number numbers nothing.

4.8 · A capability planned without a number is given its story's next free one (after the highest its live capabilities carry), so the contracts planned on it are numbered from the start; a number given is kept.

4.9 · Retiring a capability with live dependents is refused, naming every dependent and dependsOn, with nothing written; after those links are removed or the dependents retired, retirement succeeds with its reason and writer kept in history.
4.10 · A contract planned without a number skips the numbers the capability's tests already carry, past the highest; a number given is kept
4.11 · a contract planned without a number never takes the number of a numbered test no live contract carries: it gets the next free number past it, and only a number given binds it to that test
4.12 · A story is made mapped only by mapStories: a mapped field given to addStory or editStory is refused, and nothing is written

4.13 · mapStories(from, packages) adds a mapped story, with no capabilities, for each package no live story of that import maps, retires that import's stories whose package is gone, and leaves every other story as it stands
4.14 · The plan's tree carries a mapped story's import, package and folders as mapStories recorded them; a story storytree built carries none
4.15 · A number given in a contract's title is written in the numbered form, number then " · ", so every reader of contract numbers finds it

4.16 · a capability on a mapped story is planned with the folders and files of its import it covers, several roots allowed and written plainly; one with none, or a path outside its story's folders, is refused, as are covers on a built story
4.17 · no two capabilities of a mapped story cover one file: a path equal to, inside or around another's is refused, naming the capability that covers it, on planning and on correcting

4.19 · The project's anchor is written a half at a time, what it is and who it is for (setAnchor), at one id, and read back by anchor() and the plan's tree; a half given as undefined is removed, and an empty half is refused with nothing written (ADR-1085 D1).
4.20 · anchorGaps(tree) reads what the plan has not said, the anchor's missing halves only, and nothing when both are said; no story is ever named (ADR-1085 D1, ADR-1096); it fails nothing.

4.21 · a story carries no audience (ADR-1096): one given an audience is refused with nothing written, and one stored with an audience before reads without failing, its tree node carries none, and its next edit stores it without one
4.22 · The plan's tree carries a story's risk reading and guardrails, and a capability's guardrails, as stored; one without them carries none

4.23 · A pull request number resolves through the project's repository cut-over by when it was recorded: before it, the old repository's (none when that one was deleted); on its day or after, the new one's; with no cut-over, the project's one repository's
4.24 · A capability planned or retitled with a number another live capability of its story carries is refused, naming that one and the story's next free number; nothing is written

4.25 · importPluginPlan writes a plugin's story, capabilities and contracts from its plan, adopting a live story the first time; a later import matches capabilities by number and contracts by theirs, edits what changed, adds what is new and retires what the plan no longer holds, keeping ids
4.26 · a plugin's story, its capabilities and its contracts are refused every plan edit (story, capability, proposed flag, contract), each naming the plugin's plan; nothing is written

4.27 · a plugin plan with a capability or contract carrying no number, a number twice, or a contract numbered under another capability is refused, as is adopting a mapped story or another plugin's, with nothing written

1.1 · The graph joins library stories, capabilities, contracts and declared capability dependencies with surveyed files, file ownership, file imports and numbered tests joined to their contracts, marking stored plan edges declared and survey or test-title edges inferred.
1.3 · a mapped file an explored capability covers implements it, and the map answers for either; the capability reads mapped until it has a contract

capabilities.title: 2 · Focus selection
capabilities.description: Select any file, capability, promise or story by upstream and downstream dependency depth and node kind.

contracts.title: 2.1 · Given either a code file or a capability as input, up returns its dependencies and down returns its dependents to the requested depth, with each returned node once at its nearest depth.

2.2 · Selection accepts file paths, capability ids or numbers, promise ids or numbers and story names; kind filters the returned node kinds without stopping traversal through other kinds, and an absent or ambiguous selection is refused explicitly.
2.3 · In a fixture plan where apps/desktop/src/view/view.ts belongs to the app Projects capability, selecting that file with up 1 returns Projects and its contracts, including Projects 2.5.
2.6 · A selection in the library's record names, or a bare record id, selects its node
2.7 · The focus tool refuses a call that gives neither select nor crossing, or a crossing with a select that names no mapped story or with dry_run, before it reads anything

2.8 · With capabilities and select story:<name>, the focus tool answers that story's capability tree as `map --capabilities` does (3.11), as text and as data; with crossing, or a select that names no story, it is refused before anything is read

capabilities.title: 3 · Counts before detail
capabilities.description: Return complete counts and estimated token cost before detail; show every selected row or refuse above the ceiling, never truncate.

contracts.title: 3.1 · The default map answer gives counts by depth and kind, verified health tallies and the estimated token cost of the full answer, plus hints to narrow, without detail rows.
3.2 · Dry-run returns the selected row count and estimated token cost without detail rows.
3.3 · Show returns every selected row with id, kind, title, health, depth and edge provenance; above the safety ceiling it refuses with the counts and never silently truncates or ranks rows away.
3.4 · The map command exposes the same selection and counts, dry-run and show modes in text and JSON, including a structured refusal above the show ceiling.
3.5 · The agent-link focus tool accepts select, up, down, kind and mode counts, dry_run or show, defaults to counts, and returns the same complete-or-refused answer as the map command.
3.6 · In a branch's checkout the map reads the plan with that branch's increment's pending changes laid over; elsewhere the live plan

3.7 · Focus on a mapped story, or on a file of an imported folder (by its path there or its full path), answers counts first with the word mapped in place of any health, and names a loop among the mapped stories it reaches
3.8 · The map command and the focus tool answer for a mapped story from the folder this machine imports it from
3.9 · For folders or file patterns in a mapped island, the map counts the files outside that import files inside and the files inside that import files outside, and lists each import on show
3.10 · An explored capability named cap:<id|number> in place of folders draws the crossing's line round the files it covers, among its story's files; one covering nothing is refused

3.11 · With --capabilities, the map answers a selected story's capabilities in one read: each with its health word and reason, its contracts (number and title), the capabilities it depends on, and its source files with their lines of code, tests left out; --json gives it as data
3.12 · A repeat map or focus on an unchanged checkout reads and parses no file
3.13 · a new process's map or diff focus on an unchanged Git checkout parses no file of it

capabilities.title: 4 · Diff impact
capabilities.description: Focus a git diff on changed files, their promises and dependents, including the tests that name those promises.

contracts.title: 4.1 · Given a git range, defaulting to the branch against origin/main, affected joins changed files to their capabilities and promises, their downstream dependents and the tests naming those promises, using the map counts, dry-run and show modes.

4.2 · For each story whose package fetched origin/main changed within a given time, the newest such commit and when it was committed; a story whose package did not change then is absent, and with no origin/main there are none.

4.3 · The health worklist read at a checkout gives the library each contract carrying "no test names it" that a numbered test in its story's package on fetched origin/main names, with main's commit and its time; a test only off main names nothing, and with no origin/main none is named
4.4 · With no range given in a repository with no origin/main, affected reads the branch against its local default branch (init.defaultBranch, else main, else master)

capabilities.title: 1 · Run results
capabilities.description: A CI job log's test output, read into one result per test (passed, failed or skipped) with the commit the run tested.

contracts.title: 1.1 · A job log's TAP, as the Actions API or `gh run view --log` prints it, reads as one result per test: `ok` passed, `not ok` failed, `# SKIP` or `# TODO` skipped, a subtest under the names of the tests it sits in; other lines give nothing
1.2 · The commit a run tested is read from its log's checkout (`git log -1 --format=%H`), and a log that names none gives no commit
1.3 · A job log in node's spec format reads as one result per test, as its TAP would

1.21 · pytest's -rA summary lines read as one result per test: PASSED and XPASS passed, FAILED and ERROR failed, XFAIL skipped, each with its node id's file and classes; a SKIPPED line, which names no test, keeps its file, line and reason

capabilities.title: 2 · Contract verdicts
capabilities.description: Each test result tied to its story by the test file that carries its title at the run's commit, and to its contract by the title's leading number; each contract then judged passing, failing or not checked.

contracts.title: 2.1 · A result counts for contract N.M of the one story whose package's tests carry its exact title at the run's commit (its outermost numbered name); a title carried by two stories' tests, or by none, credits no contract and is listed as unmatched
2.2 · A contract is passing only when it has tests and every one passed, failing when any failed, and not checked when one was skipped or none ran

2.3 · A test skipped on one platform for a platform reason counts passed when the same test passed on every job of the platform it needs; otherwise it stays skipped, and a contract a skip leaves not checked carries the skip's kind

2.4 · A result no test holds by its exact title counts for contract N.M of the one story whose test calls a helper with N.M and a title (contract("11.8", "…")), when the result's name begins with that number and ends with that title; held by two stories, it credits nothing
2.5 · A failing verdict's note carries, after its tally, the first line of the first message its failed tests carry, cut to 200 characters; a failure with no message leaves the tally alone

2.6 · A pytest result counts for contract N.M by the number its test's name carries (test_2_3_… or test_<package>_2_3_…), for the one story whose package holds that test in the node id's file, or the story whose package the name names; a docstring's number reaches no log
2.7 · A skipped pytest test, which -rA names only by its file and line, is tied to the test at that line (its decorators' or its body's), so its skip leaves that test's contract not checked

capabilities.title: 3 · Reading the project's CI
capabilities.description: The newest finished push run on the project's default branch, read through the GitHub Actions API, and its verdicts written to the library's verified column; the agent's reported column is never touched.

contracts.title: 3.1 · Reading a project's CI writes each judged contract's verified column, by the project's CI with its tally, commit and run, and only from the newest finished push run on the default branch; the agent's reported column is never written, so a capability the agent reports passing reads unhealthy when CI failed it, and healthy only when CI passed it
3.2 · A project with no GitHub origin, or with no finished push run on its default branch, writes nothing and says why; its contracts keep reading not checked
3.3 · A job log holding terminal escape sequences is read all the same, whether gh refuses to print one unless allowed (2.102) or prints it as it is
3.4 · A story whose tests live in its package's own test folder, outside src, is verified from its CI as one with them under src is
3.5 · A job the run skipped, which has no log, is passed over: the run's other jobs are read all the same
3.6 · A cancelled job with no log cannot hide available CI results; available cancelled-job logs still count, absent tests stay not checked, and other errors remain visible

3.7 · Each job's results are read as its platform's: a test skipped on Windows for a platform reason and passed on the Linux and macOS jobs verifies passing, and a contract a skip leaves not checked records the skip's kind
3.8 · A cancelled push run is passed over for the newest finished one that ran to its end
3.10 · The merge queue's run of a commit the default branch holds is read in place of its cancelled push run
3.11 · Only the merge queue's run of the push run's own workflow is read, never another workflow's
3.13 · A contract whose package the newest run's scope left out is judged from the newest run that scoped it in
3.14 · CI health declares the `health` verbs the command line mounts: `health ci` in a project with no GitHub origin says why and writes nothing
3.15 · A push run that ran no tests, standing on the merge queue's run of its commit, is passed over for that queue run

3.16 · A contract whose tests were skipped or crashed is recorded not checked with its skip kind; a verdict the reading or run did not reproduce is recorded as not re-run at the commit, carrying that verdict and its time; an entry already saying the same is not written again, and a contract with no tests keeps a verdict from elsewhere.
3.17 · Every verdict recorded carries its writer's source: reading a project's CI writes it as from CI, a factory plugin's own tests or a local run of a project's tests as verified locally
3.18 · A Python story's pytest tests are verified from its CI as a JavaScript story's are: the run's commit's .py files under packages are read beside its JS and TS

capabilities.title: 4 · A factory plugin's own tests
capabilities.description: A user's factory plugin's own tests, run through its package's test command in their factory and read back, recorded as the verified health of the promises of the story that plugin is the package of (ADR-0902 narrowed for factory plugins, which have no CI to read).

contracts.title: 4.1 · `storytree health plugin <plugin>`, on the command line only (it has no MCP tool: record_plugin_health is marked absent), runs a plugin's own tests in this computer's factory by its package's test command, and records each numbered test's verdict on the promises of the story that plugin is the package of, in the project, as verified locally: passing when its tests pass, failing when one fails; a plugin with no test command, or no story, writes nothing and says why

capabilities.title: 5 · A project's own tests, run locally
capabilities.description: A user's project with no CI to read, perhaps with no repository at all, has its own tests run through its package.json test command on the command line and read back, recorded as the verified health of its stories' promises, labelled a local test run (ADR-1193 D1, D2: the ladder's local rung).

contracts.title: 5.1 · `storytree health local`, on the command line only (it has no MCP tool), runs the project's own tests by its package.json test command in the project's folder, which needs no git repository, and records each numbered test's verdict on its story's promise as a local test run: passing when its tests pass, failing once one fails; a project with no test command writes nothing and says why, and so does one whose CI storytree reads (a GitHub origin with a workflow), which points to health ci instead

5.2 · `storytree health local` runs a Python project's own tests by pytest -rA (through uv run or poetry run when its lockfile is uv's or Poetry's), when it has a pyproject.toml, setup.cfg or setup.py and no package.json test command, and credits its numbered pytest tests from its .py files as CI does; a run with no results names pytest -rA's output for a Python project

capabilities.title: 6 · Agent tools (the MCP server)
capabilities.description:
The toolbox the agent calls, served as an MCP server: plan work (arc, story, capability, contract), see the plan and who is on what, claim or release a capability, report a contract red or green, report a capability landed, say a capability is built so it is no longer proposed (`mark_built`, ADR-0744 D2), and search, read and write artifacts (plus list and add a node's front covers, once the library has them). Each tool is a thin wrapper over the library API and the claims above that answers in a short plain sentence the agent can act on, and every artifact read is logged in the agent activity log (ADR-0624); a new artifact with no place named goes onto the claimed capability's shelf of front covers (ADR-0627 D4, which redirected ADR-0624's default link).

As built: the 6.21 MCP cancellation checks cover claim, make_workspace and attach_workspace before and after library admission. They wait for their blocking and observing database connections to disconnect before removing the throwaway project. An admitted claim still finishes normally; this corrects the test teardown, not the cancellation contract.

contracts.title: 1.1 · A folder whose marker names "site" gives "site" asked from the folder, from a sub-folder of it, and from a git worktree of it.
1.2 · A folder with no marker, in it or above it, gives "not a storytree project".
1.4 · With the app's database stopped, asking where to send activity answers "storytree isn't running" in well under a second.
1.5 · A leftover address from a crashed app counts as not running: it answers in well under a second and never hangs.

1.6 · With the library set to Cloud SQL, a project folder routes to that instance (its connection name and user) whether or not the app's local database is running, and no local address is tried; with it local, routing is exactly as in 1.1 to 1.5.

1.7 · Routing reads only the library setting: damage elsewhere in settings.json (an unusable context guidance, say) does not stop it, while a damaged library setting, or a file that is not a JSON object, refuses naming the file and is never read as local nor rewritten.

1.12 · A marker alone reaches no project (ADR-0942): a checkout whose marker names an existing project, with or without its identity, is refused until its trunk on this machine is approved, and a trunk recorded before approval counts as unapproved until it joins on purpose; an approved trunk and its git worktrees reach it.

1.15 · Project and caller's routing entry alone (@storytree/project-and-caller/routing) routes a folder: one that is no project gives "not a storytree project", and a project whose app is stopped gives "storytree isn't running", without the caller loading the package's root

1.16 · An authenticated local installation routes only through its private, matching versioned credential handoff; damaged or exposed material refuses without a passwordless fallback, while legacy discovery, app liveness and explicit remote routing remain usable
1.17 · Only a git worktree its trunk's repository registered inherits the trunk's project and approval; a copied or forged .git file pointing at a trunk makes no worktree of it

1.18 · A forgotten trunk's remembered approval opens nothing: removing the project from this machine, or deleting it everywhere, drops this machine's remembered approval for it, so its folder is refused until approved again (ADR-0942)

1.19 · An imported folder is recorded on its project beside the trunk, per machine, approved by the import; recording it again updates its repository and commit, and forgetting the trunk forgets its imports
1.20 · The projects with a trunk are read as one set across every machine: a forgotten trunk leaves it, and an imported folder is no trunk

1.21 · A folder's marker is .storytree/project.json, and a root .storytree.json is still read while projects move: the nearest marker at or above a folder names its project, and a folder holding both is routed by .storytree/project.json
2.1 · Two separate processes write lines for two sessions, and reading from the start returns every line once, in the order written.
2.2 · Reading "since line N" returns only the lines after N, in order, each carrying the number to pass next time.
2.3 · Lines written for project "site" never appear when reading project "app".
2.4 · The log never shows up in the library's list of projects, and writing lines leaves the library's own records and change feed untouched.

2.5 · The log opens on whichever server the library resolved to, reached through the library's connection: lines two machines write for one project on one Cloud SQL instance are both read back from either, in order (live, opt-in).

2.6 · A line may name the earlier line of its own project's log that caused it (`causedBy`, ADR-0746 D2), and reads back naming it. A line naming a line its project's log does not hold (another project's, or none) is refused, whether appended alone or under the project's lock, and nothing is written.

2.7 · A bounded read sends only the lines it asks for, oldest first: by kind, session, cursor and time, by a field's value, values or absence, by a field carried, the latest for each key, the newest or oldest few, and inside folders whatever their case or slashes, with the fields it never reads left out.
2.8 · A read inside folders, latest line per session, on a log of many lines elsewhere is served by an index: it never scans the project's whole log

2.9 · An activity line can be formatted with its complete recorded command, including quotes and line breaks, for both started and finished commands; its number, time, session, kind and recorded cause remain visible. Compact formatting still clips long commands to 60 characters.

2.10 · A claim-refused line's text names the part, the session holding it, the file whose edit asked for it and the refused session's reason; a claimed line's text names its file and the session it was taken over from

2.11 · A line appended for a hook event is not added again when the log holds a line exactly like it, of the same event, that came the other way within two minutes of its time; the same way twice adds it twice

2.12 · A log opened in a storytree home whose settings name an experiment and arm stamps both on every line it writes (ADR-1064 D2); a log opened in a home that names none writes its lines without them.

2.13 · Lines written earlier, appended as one batch, go in at their own times and in order in a few round trips however many they are; a line exactly like one the log holds at that time, or like an earlier one of the batch, is added once, and a line of an event that came the other way within two minutes is kept once
5.1 · Session A claims "email form", and the claim shows A and the reason.

5.2 · A second live claimant is refused naming the holder and why it still binds, including any unverified close-out disagreement; a claim-refused line records the refusal. An idle holder, including one whose standing safe close-out is verified against its branches and running work, permits takeover even with stale command telemetry. A prompt, admitted claim or non-compaction restart voids that close-out.
5.3 · When A reports it landed, the claim ends and a "landed" line is written. A release, or A's session ending, also ends it.
5.4 · A claim on a capability the library doesn't have is refused, and when two agents claim at the same instant exactly one wins.
5.5 · An edit made while A holds "email form" counts toward it, and an edit from a session holding nothing counts as unplanned activity.
5.6 · While a command A started is still running, past the quiet time, B's claim on A's capability is refused, naming A.

5.7 · Session A claims a proposed increment, and the claim shows A and the reason while the library shows the increment active; B's claim on it is refused, naming A. An active one is not started again, and a closed one is refused.

5.8 · Claiming an increment whose own wait holds, or whose arc's wait holds, is refused, naming each blocker and its reason, and one held on an open question is refused as waiting on the owner. Nothing is written and the increment is not started. Once the wait releases, the claim succeeds.
5.9 · A capability claim is never refused because the open increments naming it in their touches wait: touches is a plan, never a lock (ADR-0944 D2). The waiting increment itself is still refused.

capabilities.title: 7 · Instructions (the habits card)
capabilities.description: One short text, a screen or less, that teaches the agent storytree's habits: plan the story first, claim a capability and open the knowledge it needs before touching it, write the failing test and report red, make it pass and report green, report it landed, and record an artifact for anything worth remembering. The tool server hands this text to the agent at the start of every session, as its instructions; Claude Code reads it from there. Codex (0.158 on) does not: it shows the model neither a tool server's instructions nor its tools until the agent searches for them, so connecting Codex also writes one short marked section into the AGENTS.md in Codex's home that sends the agent to check_setup before its first change in a storytree project and keeps it silent elsewhere (7.4; measured 0 of 3 without, 3 of 3 with, packages/app-setup/evidence/codex-first-session).

contracts.title: 7.1 · The text names every tool the server offers an agent, and no tool the server lacks; a harness's own tools (ADR-1056 D2) are left off.
7.3 · The tool server hands the text to the agent at the start of every session.
7.5 · The card says who decides what

7.7 · set_up_project's answer, and check_setup's in a project, carry the whole card, so an agent whose harness keeps only the start of the server's instructions (Claude Code keeps 2,048 characters; Codex shows none) still gets all of it.
7.8 · The card says what one contract is: a behaviour visible from outside, in what goes in, what comes out and the errors
7.9 · The card says how to build beside mapped code

7.10 · The card handed at session start is composed from the guidance each story package the server mounts declares in its manifest, in the manifests' order, between the server's own opening and closing lines
7.11 · The kept start of the card tells the agent to plan requested work before building it

capabilities.title: 8 · Reading the tools' use
