The left rail (2.39) and the forest beside it start directly below it, at 48 px, the forest and its controls never under the rail. With the overlay closed, the forest receives pointer input beside the rail and below the bar. The backdrop click that closes the overlay is consumed; subsequent forest input works. The existing data-state and data-drew smoke readings remain valid.
2.9 · A capture settles each requested animation frame before measuring or taking a picture
2.10 · A capture names a seed story's file by the package the seed's own story title gives, from a shared seed, so a later rename of the live package cannot desync it
2.11 · The empty page shows storytree's mark drawn in the page theme's own colours, light or dark, from no file
2.12 · A capture's stand-in bridge opens the page with the first-run guide already seen, so it pictures the globe; a capture of the guide itself opts back in to a first launch
2.13 · A capture whose browser close hangs after disconnect still ends
2.14 · A hung close kills the real browser's process and lets its pipes go

2.15 · The app bar holds two tabs: a factory icon that switches straight to the user's factory (greyed "No factory yet" without one), and "Projects", which always reads Projects and opens a dropdown of the products ending with "New project…"; after them a label names the product on show, with a button that copies its name
2.16 · A capture's stand-in bridge hides every teaching card as it appears, so none intercepts the capture's clicks; a capture of the cards themselves opts back in to seeing them
2.17 · The window mounts a switched-on stand-in surface's view from the factory
2.18 · An evidence capture's build goes to the checkout's ignored build folder, never beside the evidence it serves
2.19 · The capture kit's build holds every file its page names, the road worker's script included

2.20 · The desktop renderer writes every failure it catches to the console (so app.log), including those it does not show: a failed surfaces read (every surface on), a failed projects poll or forest read once drawn, and a failed start mark
2.21 · The capture kit's page runs React's production build, as the shipped app's does
2.22 · A desktop page opened with a problem says the library could not be opened, and why, and reads no projects
2.23 · A failed projects read shows its reason only while nothing is on show; a drawn forest or the empty page stays
2.24 · A failed project choice says why in place of the project and reads the projects again; a failed surfaces read mounts every surface
2.25 · A surface switched or set in the Surfaces menu draws the project on show again, as the settings now say
2.26 · A read or mount that lands after the user switched project changes nothing on show, and what it mounted is let go
2.27 · The forest kept at the last start is drawn at once, marked not fresh; a first read that fails says so over it, or over the page when none was kept, and once drawn a failure changes nothing
2.28 · A territory click opens its story on that capability, and a redraw of the open story keeps its open details, the panel tree's place and the popped-out tree
2.29 · Teaching cards hear whether the project on show is the factory, and each card is placed beside its target on the page
2.30 · Each start-timing mark is sent once, however often the page reaches it, and what the forest drew joins the page's census beside other surfaces' readings
2.31 · A capture launches the newest Chromium its browsers folder holds when Playwright's pinned one is missing
2.36 · A capture launch that finds no Chromium to take the pinned one's place fails naming CAPTURE_CHROMIUM and what the browsers folder holds
2.37 · A start with a kept forest is marked settled only once the globe has drawn a frame of what is on show after the fresh tree
2.38 · A capture on a live library answers the page with the app's own reads, its first activity read bounded to the newest lines and its changes folded

2.39 · The sessions list and the arcs each mount in their tab of one full-height left rail down the page's left, Sessions then Arcs, one tab on show at a time; a project opens on the tab it last showed, kept per project in the page's storage, and on Arcs with none kept; the Arcs tab badges what waits on the owner there, and none waiting shows no badge; a surface switched off has no tab, and with both off there is no rail
2.40 · The arcs read nothing until the page's start is settled, or until the forest's first read fails
2.41 · The arcs mount once the forest has asked its first tree read, at its first news or its first failed read, so their drawing never holds that read back

capabilities.title: 3 · Surfaces
capabilities.description: The app's window hosts the surfaces for the project on show: the forest, which the app opens on (until it lands, today's plain list), with the arc surface as an overlay that the forest hosts. The page cannot reach the database, so the app carries everything a surface reads to it, and tells the surfaces when the project changes.

contracts.title: 3.1 · The page can ask the app for the library's changes and the agent log's new lines since a point, for the project on show, and only newer ones come back.
3.2 · A name that is not a project is refused, and never created.
3.3 · The smoke check, pointed at the surface on show, passes only if that surface says it drew every story and capability of the project.
3.4 · The page can ask the app for a story's or capability's shelf of front covers, and for the artifacts that link to an artifact, for the project on show.

3.5 · The page can ask the app for the context readings of named sessions in the project on show (agent link 9.5, 9.8), each parsed from the transcript records in the shared log, with no access to the machine the session ran on (ADR-0749 D3); a session with none named reads as an absence, and a name that is not a project is refused.

3.6 · The page can ask the app for a session's window in the project on show (agent link 9.10), or several sessions' in one ask that reads the log once, parsed from the transcript records in the shared log, with no access to the machine the session ran on (ADR-0749 D3); a session with none named reads as an absence.

3.7 · The Surfaces menu lists every surface with its switch and its settings; a surface switched off is saved to the settings file and reads back off, and one that follows it goes off with it; switching an always-on or unknown surface, or to an unknown choice, is refused with its reason and the file is untouched.
3.8 · The page can ask the app for the project's standing delegations

3.9 · After an app start, context readings and single or batched session windows take only the requested sessions’ latest transcript references from the activity log; the bytes read do not grow with the project’s activity history.

3.10 · After a restart the app reuses stored transcript records and fetches only appended records, preserving token counts, composition, historical openings, compactions and kept segments; retention keeps the final readings before raw records expire.
3.11 · The app reads the folders this machine imports for the project on show, so its survey draws the project's mapped stories; a name that is not a project is refused

3.12 · The desktop app's Surfaces menu lists the surfaces named by the manifests of the story packages it depends on, as the plugin loader composes them into its bundle and as its `#parts/surfaces` gives them run unbundled: the forest's, then the arc surface's
3.13 · The page can ask the app for the system notes the project on show reads from its factory
3.14 · The app reads where a project sits among factories, from its library already open, and whether it builds itself

2.16 · settings.json names the story parts switched off on this computer ("parts-off"): setPartOff switches one off or on and returns the parts off, sorted, leaving the other settings as they were; readPartsOff reads them alone, none when it names none; the core is refused with the reason and nothing written; a damaged value is reported naming the file
3.15 · Every canvas, gear menu tab and dialog the app opens carries a declared surface id, and the corner names it
3.16 · An agent switches the factory folder with the switch_factory tool, and settings show says who switched it
3.17 · The whole desktop page, every story's surface mounted in it, bundles for the browser as the app's build bundles it
3.18 · The desktop page offers the drawing engine's road worker: its page names the script, and the script the app's build makes answers a routing as a worker
3.19 · `settings show`'s factory line names where a plugin's contract is read (`storytree plugin contract`), and how to start and check one
3.20 · A Surfaces menu that cannot read or save the surfaces says so in its status line and writes the failure to the console (so app.log)
3.21 · A project's library closed under the page's reads is opened again
3.22 · The page's reads open each project with the kinds of record the app's mounted factory plugins declare
3.23 · The page the app's build makes runs React's production build

capabilities.title: 4 · Updates
capabilities.description:
The app keeps itself up to date by itself: on the owner's machine it runs from its own copy of merged main, notices new merges within a few minutes, and rebuilds and restarts itself in the background, so it never runs unmerged work and nobody rebuilds it by hand. Check for updates in the top-right gear asks that same merged-main updater to check now and shows the running build and its progress or failure. A ready build waits with the window open until no seed or start-up or daily snapshot is being written. A checkout explains that it does not update itself. Installed apps select releases from their own channel: development follows each merged release; stable follows only the owner-pinned existing build (ADR-0871). As built (increment_aca4e6853237): an installed app's downloaded release waits for a quiet moment (packages/app whenToInstall: ten minutes after launch, ten minutes without window input or agent activity from a session that has not ended), because a first install was replaced 17 seconds after setup said the app was open (packages/app-setup/evidence/acceptance, F1). The gear answers from the release updater in an installed app, marks itself with a dot while an update is pending, and its Restart to update installs at once. A seed or snapshot still holds any restart, including one requested from the gear. The owner accepted contracts 4.4 and 4.7's wording for this on 2026-09-29 (question_df551985ad62).

As built (increment_c3e1441890f9, contract 4.12): installed release updates read named, independent run holds under the app home/update-holds before each automatic installation. packages/app/src/updates/hold-run.mjs wraps a foreground command, publishes its hold before launch, removes it on return and preserves its exit code. Holds expire after the requested positive duration, at most six hours; overlapping runs do not release one another. Downloads continue, the pending status names the run, and the user's Restart to update still overrides holds while respecting seed writes and snapshots. The standalone wrapper and usage/proof are in packages/app/evidence/update-hold. No laptop acceptance run is part of this implementation.


As built (increment_402e76453e34, contract 4.17): the follow-main updater start-checks each new build before it may restart into it (apps/desktop/src/main/start-check.ts, wrapping follow-main's build through mainUpdates' update option). The build is started with --start-check, which goes only as far as registering the main process's handlers and exits 0: no library, no network, so a library on Cloud SQL or a local Postgres the running app holds never holds back a good build. A check that does not exit 0 within 60 s fails the build as 4.2 does, and that commit is remembered and not rebuilt. Lifecycle 1.13: run()'s rejection now ends the app (exit 1) instead of leaving it half-started holding the single-instance lock.

As built (increment_78ac958384c9, contracts 4.4 and 4.13): the follow-main updater restarts into a built main commit only at the moment the user's install choice allows, as a downloaded release does. Owner, 2026-10-21: the follow-main app "keeps closing on me" (app.log held 1,135 restarts). mainUpdates takes a quiet option; the desktop builds one quietMoment check (packages/app/src/updates/install-moment.ts: whenToInstall over launch time, window use, agent activity and the saved install choice) and gives it to both updaters. A built commit waiting for that moment reads pending, so the gear offers Restart to update, which restarts at once in every mode; seeds and snapshots still hold either restart. Settings → Updates offers When updates install in an app following main as well, and a pending update says when it installs: at the next quiet moment, during quiet hours, or when you click Restart to update. With agents working on the laptop most of the day, quiet mode may rarely find a moment; quiet hours is the predictable choice.

guardrails.check: Fresh-install sweep: a fresh user on the old laptop installs the release candidate with the stable one-liner, connects Claude Code and builds a small project through storytree, judged by a separate model; `storytree release pin` waits on its pass (4.25)

contracts.title: 4.4 · An installed app checks for a newer published release offered by its own release channel, downloads and verifies it, and installs it only at a quiet moment: not in the first ten minutes after a launch, not while the window has been used or an agent session has worked in the last ten minutes, and never while a library seed or project snapshot is being written. The user can install it from the gear without waiting for a quiet moment, but seeds and snapshots still hold the restart with the window open and the update pending. Installing stops its database and restarts through the platform's installer into the new app using the app's lifecycle handoff.
4.5 · A failed release check or download leaves the app running and can be retried; equal and older releases never replace it, concurrent checks share one download, and quitting stops updates.

4.6 · Releases contain only work merged to main and verified on all three systems by main's own CI run of that commit; every later main build has a higher version, and a rerun cannot replace a newer published release. One platform's failure holds only that platform: a release publishes with every platform whose build is complete, and a platform whose build is not keeps its last good build's update feed and installer entry, so an installed app never meets a release that lacks its own platform's feed, and its one-liner installs the last build that has its platform. Every asset is uploaded into the draft before it publishes, and publishing is its last write: a late platform's build waits for the next version; nothing is uploaded to a published release.

4.7 · Check for updates in the gear checks the published releases now, using the same updater as the automatic check. Concurrent requests share the work. If no newer build is needed, the menu says the app is up to date and identifies the running build.

4.8 · The menu shows when a new build is ready or restarting. A ready build restarts the app through the existing lifecycle, waiting with the window open while a seed writes the library or a start-up or daily project snapshot is being written, including when the user asks from the menu; waiting neither downloads the ready build again nor starts a second restart.
4.9 · A failed manual update check or download shows its reason, leaves the running app alone, and can be retried from the gear.

4.10 · In a copy that does not install releases (a development checkout, a portable build), Check for updates explains that it does not update itself; the request neither fetches a build nor restarts the app.

4.12 · A named acceptance run can hold automatic release installation until it releases its hold or a finite ceiling expires; overlapping runs keep independent holds. Downloads continue, and an explicit Restart to update still installs once no seed or project snapshot is being written.

4.13 · The user chooses when a downloaded release may install itself: whenever quiet (the default), only inside their daily quiet hours, or never on its own (manual only); the quiet-moment rule still applies inside the hours, and their own Restart to update installs in every mode once no seed or project snapshot is being written.

4.14 · The gear's Updates section shows which install choice is on and, for quiet hours, when the next automatic install may happen; changing it there saves it, and a refused change shows its reason and keeps the old choice
4.15 · Stable installs use only the owner pin; alpha follows each release, with a durable channel that survives upgrades
4.16 · Pin an existing released build without rebuilding it, recording landed increment notes since the preceding pin and refusing a concurrent overwrite

4.17 · A release whose installed app cannot start never publishes: the release's install check starts the installed build's main process and fails unless it exits 0 in time with no promise rejection left unhandled
4.19 · An installed app's releases.log keeps the update lines a person reads and stays bounded

4.20 · The release signs the Mac build with the Developer ID in a job that installs nothing, and gives Apple's notarisation a bounded wait, when the signing secrets are present; stays ad-hoc when they are absent; and refuses a signed build Apple could not be asked to notarise

4.21 · An installed app knows it is installed (Windows by the installer's marker, a Mac by the delivery record naming its bundle, Linux by the delivery record naming the folder that holds its AppImage) and follows published releases on Windows, on Linux, or as a Developer ID signed Mac build
4.22 · A release rehearsal builds, signs and checks every platform's installers on a branch, and never drafts, uploads or publishes

4.23 · `storytree release candidate` names the newest published build fit to pin as stable: it covers every platform the pin covers, its release run published it with the Mac acceptance run passing, it has been out at least 24 hours, and no open friction or question names a regression in it or an earlier unpinned build; it prints that evidence and the notes a pin would publish, names what passed over each newer build, and changes nothing
4.24 · The user chooses the update channel, alpha or stable, in the gear; stable stays the default, and a switch takes effect on the updater's next check

4.25 · `storytree release pin` publishes a build as stable only once its fresh-install sweep passed: the stable routine's "Pin 0.3.N as stable?" question for that exact build, raised only after the old-laptop acceptance run passed it, unless retired; without it the pin refuses, publishes nothing and says how to run the sweep; the pin records the pass it stood on. A preview only reads, a move back to a build pinned before does not wait, and an expedited urgent fix waives the sweep as it waives the soak (ADR-1032 D7)
4.26 · After a repository cut-over, a stable pin's notes leave out work closed before it, whose number is the old repository's, and link work closed after it to the new repository
4.27 · A Windows update downloads only its changed blocks and verifies, even after an earlier downloaded update was never installed

4.28 · A release's packaged app cannot be run as plain Node, take NODE_OPTIONS or Node's inspector flags, or load its app from outside its own checked archive: each system's install check reads the built executable's fuses and fails unless each is set as the build sets them

4.29 · A failed read or change in the gear's Updates section is written to the console (so app.log) and shown: Update channel, When updates install and Open at sign-in show a failed first read, unchangeable, instead of vanishing, and a hidden switch or error line is never displayed
4.30 · A following app checks for a release at start and every three minutes until it quits; a failed check is logged and the next goes ahead, and a waiting release logs when it installs
4.31 · Only an installed Linux AppImage refreshes the agent tools beside it, and a refresh that fails is said
4.32 · The gear offers the update channel only where releases install themselves, and never in a smoke check
4.33 · The running app reports Electron's version when packaged, else its checkout's, else 0.3.0

capabilities.title: 5 · Recorder
capabilities.description: In the page: recognises each catalogue action its user takes from the input and the page's settled seam, and records its response, long frames up to settled (count and longest), settled time, whether progress was on show, its name and a size hint, handing them to the app in batches only when no action is under way.

contracts.title: 5.1 · A catalogue action its user takes becomes one reading of its response, long frames, settled time, progress, name and size
5.2 · Readings reach the app in batches, never between an action's input and its settling
5.3 · A drag that turns the map becomes one reading of its frames (p50, p95, longest and how many over 50 ms), named by the view it turned

capabilities.title: 6 · Readings file
capabilities.description: In the app's main process: appends each batch of readings, stamped with the app's version and time, to a bounded file in the app's home (STORYTREE_HOME), dropping the oldest past 30 days or 5 MB. Nothing is sent anywhere and nothing is written to the library.

contracts.title: 6.1 · Readings are kept in one file in the app's home, the oldest dropped past 30 days or 5 MB

capabilities.title: 7 · Lag report
capabilities.description: `storytree lag`: per action, over the last seven days, the count, median, 75th percentile and worst of the response, longest frame and settled time against the action's budget, the worst action first, saying so when an action has fewer than ten readings.

contracts.title: 7.1 · The report prints each action's count, median, 75th percentile and worst over seven days against its budget, worst first

stories.title: Map view
stories.description: Each project drawn as a globe of islands, one per story, cut into a territory per capability coloured by its verified health, with the agents at work shown where they hold claims: the surface that draws the code map, the plan and its health on a globe. Its code lives in packages/forest; it draws with The drawing engine (packages/forest-world), which lays the islands out, builds their ground and coasts and draws the globe, and which ADR-1076 D2 took back out of it.

radius.reason: 4 packages downstream; invited users, inherited from packages/app

capabilities.title: 1 · Story nodes
capabilities.description: The forest keeps one story node for every story in the project: where the story sits in the forest, with its title and its overall health. Nodes follow the library, so a new story appears as a new node and a retired story's node goes, with nothing arranged by hand.

contracts.title: 1.1 · Three stories give three story nodes, each with its title and its overall health as the agent reports it.
1.2 · Adding a story to the library adds a node, and retiring a story removes its node.

1.3 · A story's place is its row by dependency depth and its slot in the row: the bottom row has the story most depended on in the middle and the rest outward, a higher row is ordered by where its dependencies sit, and a loop in the dependencies never stops the layout (ADR-0839); the glass sheet lays each row out as a column of its own (1.12).
1.4 · A story's place is in a row above every story it depends on, and stories that depend on nothing share the bottom row (ADR-0839).
1.5 · Adding a dependency moves the dependent's island up a row (ADR-0839).

1.9 · A story's row is ranked by the stories its code's derived edges reach (with or without a capability at either end) together with its capabilities' recorded dependsOn rolled up to stories; package.json fields rank nothing; a project without a survey keeps the roll-up (ADR-0991 D2, D3).
1.10 · A five-story forest opens on the glass sheet with every nameplate readable, in a row and in a chain

1.11 · A mapped story sits in a row below the mapped stories whose code imports it, by the survey's roads among mapped islands, and a built story sits above the mapped story its package depends on; a loop among them still draws every island

1.12 · On the glass sheet a story's depth runs west to east: the foundation stories stand at the west edge, each deeper depth east of every shallower one, and stories of one depth spread north to south, clear of each other (ADR-1043 D2)

1.13 · The desktop's answer to the page's code survey answers a project whose origin has no fetchable main with no code rather than a rejection, so no handler stack is logged per poll; it says the refusal once in app.log per folder and reason, naming why, and says once when that folder's main can be surveyed again.

capabilities.title: 2 · Capability tree
capabilities.description: Each story node carries its capability tree: the story's capabilities, which ones build on which, and where each one stands, from planned through built to landed, and it grows as they land. Where a capability stands comes from two records kept side by side: the arc surface's rule for planned, in progress or landed, and the health the agent reports for its tests, always labelled as the agent's own.

contracts.title: 2.1 · A story with four capabilities, planned, being built, landed and reported passing, and landed with a failing report, gives a seedling, a seedling, a full green tree and a dead tree, in build order, each with the capabilities it builds on.
2.2 · A capability the agent reports red while it is being built stays a seedling.
2.3 · A landed capability with nothing reported is a pale tree.
2.4 · A story with no capabilities yet shows one seedling, so a new story is never invisible.

capabilities.title: 3 · Story node render
capabilities.description: The page opens in Forest mode, drawing every story node on the globe as a flat island cut into its capabilities' territories (ADR-0804 D1, D2) with the library core beneath them. Forest / Library switches this one globe (ADR-0660 D4): Library hides the story nodes and shows the knowledge points alone. You can turn and zoom in either mode, hover a visible artifact dot to see its title, and click a dot to read its summary in the right-hand story-panel slot (ADR-0661 D1/D2). Forest also lets you open a story by clicking its island. An artifact card and a story panel replace one another; Close and Escape dismiss the card. Switching modes preserves the scene, camera, rotation and zoom. Each launch defaults to Forest, with no saved mode. The flat forest and separate Look-inside view remain unavailable (ADR-0655).

contracts.title: 3.1 · The app opens a seeded project on the globe in Forest mode; its smoke check finds one story node per story, each drawn with its capability tree.
3.2 · A capability landing redraws just its story node, without a reload.
3.3 · Clicking a visible story node selects it, opens its story panel and closes any artifact card.

3.4 · With nameplates shown (the default), each near-side story node shows its story's name, readable as the globe turns and zooms (ADR-0636 D4: in 0.2 the names lived on the 2D map the owner cut, so the 3D forest carries them).

3.6 · Every "builds on" link between stories, each one the code survey derives between two capabilities and each recorded dependsOn (ADR-0991 D1, D3), has exactly one continuous trail chain; shared trunks are drawn once and their width counts the original links.
3.7 · A cross-story link docks at both actual clipped shores.

3.9 · On the website's tour (the forest page's two looks are 3.55), the Stories and Library switches each choose what the glass sheet shows: both on, the islands with the knowledge under the glass; Library off, the islands with no note points; Stories off, the Library look, the islands as outlines over the knowledge; both off, nothing drawn and nothing pickable, the switches staying. With the Surfaces menu's Library off, only Stories is offered.

3.10 · On the website's tour (the forest page's two looks are 3.55), each switch flips only itself, and every combination keeps the canvas, scene, core and view. Switching Stories off clears story selection and its panel; switching Library off closes a picked note's card. A launch opens with Stories on and Library off.

3.11 · In the default Forest view a failing island (one with a capability storytree verified unhealthy, never the agent's report alone) is never hidden: on the glass sheet no island lies behind another, and a failing island past the window's edge gets a marker at the edge nearest it whose click pans it into view, including after returning from Library. Library is the viewer's explicit choice to hide failure markers (ADR-0660 D4, ADR-0825 D3). Guided views may explicitly hide all island surfaces and their failure markers (ADR-0852 D5); restoring the default surfaces restores failure attention.

3.12 · In Forest and Library, hovering an eligible artifact dot shows its title and a pointer cursor, and clicking within 8 CSS pixels picks the nearest projected dot. Forest rejects dots behind land; Library admits every on-screen drawn dot. Off-screen or clipped dots cannot be picked, and movement of 5 CSS pixels or more is a drag rather than a click.

3.13 · Clicking an artifact dot opens its summary card in the right-hand story-panel slot and closes the story panel. Opening a story replaces the card. Close and Escape dismiss the card, and none of these actions writes to the library.

3.14 · Each capability is one connected, bordered territory on its story's island, its share of the island following its share of the lines of code; Unclaimed code is its own territory; the island shows only its territories, with no mark drawn per file (ADR-0804 D2, D3, ADR-1212). In a project with verified health, before a code survey is available, capabilities share the island equally.
3.15 · Clicking a capability's territory selects that capability, as picking it in the story panel does (ADR-0804 D2)

3.18 · The land wears the session's traversal (ADR-0804 D5, as narrowed by ADR-1212 D3): a capability's territory the selected session opened is filled in the session's colour, lighter once compacted, and letting go restores it; files have no stops on the land; everything else stays as it was.

3.19 · A surveyed island's land follows its story's lines of code alone, with a floor so a tiny story stays visible, never grown to make room for its files; an unsurveyed island keeps its capability ratio (ADR-0804 D3, D7, ADR-1212 D2)

3.20 · By default, each capability's territory is filled by its word (ADR-0744): healthy green, unhealthy red, and yellow while it is proposed or untested, except mid slate grey (#86939D) while it is proposed or untested and parked on purpose (ADR-0992); a claim never changes the fill. Unclaimed code stays neutral (ADR-0825 D3) A guided view may choose plain territory boundaries or hide territories explicitly (ADR-0852 D5).

3.21 · A guided camera stop turns to a story or capability, or frames the core, over its requested duration; framing and a CSS-pixel side offset keep the target clear of a neighbouring card. A new stop or manual drag replaces the old motion without a jump, and a missing target leaves the view unchanged.

3.22 · A guided view independently switches sea, island grounds, roads, nameplates, territories, knowledge core and session tints; territories can show plain boundaries or health colours. Defaults retain the ordinary Forest view, Library hides the islands and keeps the glass, and hidden marks cannot be picked.

3.23 · The public forest view exports the app globe and its controls; screen-position reads locate a story, capability, note or core in canvas CSS pixels from the actual camera and globe rotation, including zoom, side offset and resize. 3.30 · On a growing globe each territory fills in as the growth schedules it, ending as drawn without one

3.31 · Story names stay put on their islands as the globe turns, on a small globe as on a big one: where two shown names overlap on screen, the one whose island faces the eye less squarely fades and neither moves; the selected story's name always shows, and a dimmed name yields to the names in focus
3.32 · A selected story's capability names on the globe read without their number, each wrapped to at most two lines, and pointing at a capability's territory shows its full name and description
3.33 · Where a selected island's capability names overlap on screen, the smaller territory's name fades and the larger's shows; neither moves
3.35 · The live desktop forest draws its ordinary roads toward their destinations on opening and when dependencies arrive, while existing shared roads stay drawn and reduced motion is immediate
3.37 · Home eases the view back to the one it opened on, the short way round (on the glass sheet, the Home key and the compass, 3.60)

3.39 · A mapped story is drawn as one brown island, whole: no territories, no file circles and no hatch, brown used for nothing else; its land follows its lines of code up to a cap, so a very large one does not crowd out its neighbours; with no survey it is still brown land
3.40 · While the right-hand panel is open, the glass sheet glides into the free width left of it, and glides back when it closes
3.41 · The page's locator places each drawn island and note on screen, faces one at once, and says when the glide is over
3.42 · The lag catalogue names each action, picks its island by name or size, and knows settled from what the page shows
3.43 · A built story whose package depends on a mapped story's has a road from its island to the mapped island as a whole, lit when either is selected
3.44 · A pose the guide wrote but the page has not drawn still counts
3.45 · The locator reads still only once the globe sits beside the panel as measured now
3.46 · Territories arrive without a flash: borders trace on, then the fill eases in

3.47 · Switching to the Library and back, and sweeping the mouse across the globe, answer within 100 ms with no frame over 50 ms, settled within 1 s or showing progress (verified by the Mint box's lag run)
3.48 · A start on an unchanged project draws the globe once, from the tree and what it was drawn with, kept
3.49 · Opening the app, with a kept forest and without one, shows progress within 100 ms and keeps it until the globe is settled, or is settled within 1 s (verified by the Mint box's lag run)
3.50 · a mapped island draws each explored capability as a brown territory of its own, side by side with one for the unexplored rest, none over another; each is picked by its capability
3.51 · each drawn island's screen box follows actual transforms and zoom; islands on the far side or hidden are left out

3.52 · On the glass sheet the eye rests at a tabletop tilt from above, the edge at the window's top away from it, and the sheet opens there framing its height in perspective from its west edge; a drag or a sideways scroll pans the sheet, keeping the place grabbed under the pointer, and the wheel zooms it by moving the eye; neither changes the tilt (ADR-1043 D4, narrowed by ADR-1059 D1, ADR-1060 and ADR-1062)

capabilities.title: 4 · Drill-down
capabilities.description: Clicking a story node opens a panel that explains the story in plain words: its sentences, and its capability tree, each capability pointing at the ones it builds on, including any in other stories, named with their story. The tree has a space of its own inside the panel, where the user drags it around and zooms it; it opens zoomed out to fit the whole tree, as far as the least zoom allows, and an icon in that space's corner opens the same tree in a larger window over the forest, which opens fitted too. Each capability's card says proposed, healthy, unhealthy or untested on a strip coloured as 0.2 coloured those words, with the agent's report and storytree's as labelled marks (ADR-0743, ADR-0744). Clicking one of the story's own capabilities, in the panel's tree or in the larger window, shows it below the panel's tree: its sentences, its health as the agent reports it, and its contracts on request (ADR-0659).

contracts.title: 4.1 · A story whose third capability builds on the first two gives its sentences, its capabilities in build order each with its sentences and its health as the agent reports it, and a diagram with exactly two arrows.
4.2 · A capability that builds on a capability in another story shows an arrow to it, named with that story, and that capability's card says its word.
4.3 · A capability with no description says "no description yet" instead of leaving a blank.
4.4 · A contract the agent reported red, then green, shows "red, then green"; one reported only green says so.
4.5 · Storytree's own column shows beside the agent's report only where something wrote it.

4.6 · The panel shows the story's sentences and its diagram, and below the diagram only the capability selected: its word, its sentences, its health as the agent reports it, and its contracts folded until asked for. No front cover shows in it.
4.7 · When a story opens, the capability shown is the first in build order that is not healthy, or the first if all are; one clicked stays shown, and a choice outside the story falls back.

4.8 · Each of the story's capabilities is a card you can click, marked when selected and tinted by its word (a healthy card edged green, an unhealthy one red), never by the agent's report; another story's capability is in the tree but cannot be clicked.

4.9 · The capability tree is a graph of fixed-size cards: each capability sits above the ones it builds on, and another story's capability sits one row below the capability that builds on it, not in one row with every other outside capability.

4.10 · Each card, another story's too, has a strip across its top saying its word, proposed, healthy, unhealthy or untested (ADR-0744), coloured as 0.2 coloured it (proposed amber, healthy green, unhealthy red, untested grey), and the agent's report and storytree's as marks labelled "the agent reports" and "storytree saw", storytree's only where something wrote it. The work state (planned, in progress, landed) is not on the card.

4.11 · The capability tree has its own space inside the panel, moved by dragging and zooming, with no scroll bars and never out of reach. It, and the larger window, open with the whole tree fitted in the frame and centred, never above full size nor below the least zoom; the larger window's "Fit" puts that view back. An icon in the panel space's corner, labelled "Open in a larger window", opens the larger window.

4.12 · The capability selected, when it is not healthy, says why under its word and who moves it (the agent, or you), naming the contracts that carry it; a contract whose last verdict was not re-run says "last seen failing <date>, not re-run since"; a healthy one says nothing more.

4.13 · In a project whose health nothing verifies, a built capability's card and detail lead with what the agent reports, labelled as the agent's, and say storytree does not check this project's tests yet, never untested or who moves it
4.14 · A parked capability's card keeps its word and reason and says it is parked, naming the arc
4.15 · A mapped story's panel says it is mapped: here before storytree, assumed to be working, with its file and line counts, and shows no health

4.16 · Opening a story's island, the smallest, the largest or the library's, answers within 100 ms with no frame over 50 ms, and its panel is open within 1 s or shows progress; closing the panel likewise (verified by the Mint box's lag run)
4.36 · A selected story's panel shows a minimal risk bar: its rating out of ten, the users it could reach and its extra checks with what sets each off, no graph

4.37 · Wherever storytree's verified colour shows, on a capability's card and detail and on each contract, it says its source: verified locally, from CI, or locally and from CI; a reason not green names the source of the contracts carrying it; an entry with no source recorded says none

capabilities.title: 5 · Agent capability claims
capabilities.description: Shows on the world what each running session holds. Each capability claimed by a session the agent link lists (4.12), whether or not the running-sessions list shows its row (capability 7 shows only the sessions at work, ADR-1225), carries one flag in that session's colour, standing inside the capability's territory (ADR-0968, which replaced the inset border band of ADR-0923 D1 and the outline of ADR-0825 D3). Each session has its own stable colour, the same on its flags and on its row, never the proven green or the needs-you amber. The flag keeps its size on screen and becomes a dot on an island too small to carry a pennant; it drops in with one ring at its foot when the claim arrives, stands still while held, furls and greys when its holder goes quiet, and lifts away when the claim is released or lands, with no movement under reduced motion. On an island with no surveyed code the claimed capability's equal share is marked as a staked lot, a dashed white line inside its border; a capability with no code on an island that has code draws nothing. No band, outline, fill or coast tint is drawn for a claim, so a territory's fill stays health's. A flag carries no visible agent name, reason text or hooks warning. It follows the agent link's claims and sessions, so a holder whose hooks have reported goes quiet after the quiet time; a holder whose hooks have never reported is never quiet as idle. Subagents and supervised lanes folded under a parent flag in the parent's colour, a session with no row flags nothing, and an increment claim draws nothing on the world (ADR-0923 D2). A growth replay flags the capabilities its recorded sessions held as it reaches them (contract 5.7). Missing hooks are reported by the agent link's setup check (capability 8, contract 8.5). *History: the wisps of ADR-0736 were removed by ADR-0804 D9; ADR-0825 D3 outlined a claimed territory and tinted the coast; ADR-0923 dropped the coast tint; ADR-0968 (2026-10-10) made the mark a flag and added lots.*

contracts.title: 5.1 · Session A claims "email form", and a flag in A's colour stands on that capability's territory, with no visible agent name or reason text; A's claim on a capability on a second island is flagged there too. An increment claim flags nothing, whatever its touches name (ADR-0968 D1, ADR-0923 D2).
5.2 · For a holder whose hooks have reported, after the quiet time with no new line its flags furl and grey; when A reports the capability landed, its flag lifts away.
5.3 · A session seen only through its tool calls keeps its flags unfurled even past the quiet time; the map draws no hooks warning.
5.4 · None of this changes how a capability's state is drawn.

5.5 · A session's colour is the same on every read, on its flags and on its row in the sessions list, and is never the proven-green colour. A subagent folded under its parent flags its claims in its parent's colour. A session the agent link no longer lists (4.12: ended, gone, or quiet past the leave-after) flags nothing; an idle one it still lists flags its claims, furled (5.2), though the sessions list shows no row for it (7.10, ADR-1225).

5.6 · A capability a running session claims carries one flag in that session's colour, standing in its territory at a constant size on screen, a pennant on its pole however far out the globe is zoomed and never a dot (ADR-1039); it drops in with one ring at its foot, stands still while held, furls and greys when the session is quiet, and lifts away when the claim goes, with no movement under reduced motion. On an island with no code the claimed share is marked as a lot. The flag is the only claim mark: no band, outline or fill, and no coast tint (ADR-0968, ADR-0923 D1, narrowing ADR-0804 D9)

5.7 · Replaying a growth, the sessions recorded with the latest stage the replay has reached flag the territories they held, each flag arriving as the replay reaches it, none before the first (ADR-0968, ADR-0923 D3)

capabilities.title: 7 · Running sessions
capabilities.description: A see-through strip along the forest pane's bottom, spanning its width and collapsible by its header (contract 7.17) lists one plain row per session that has not ended, claimed or not (ADR-0749 D1; ADR-0737 D1's removal of off-plan rows and their evidence stands, and capability 6 stays retired), showing facts as labels and no prose on the owner's behalf: anything that needs the owner is an open question on the arc surface (ADR-0824). An unclaimed row is named from its harness and what it works in; a session working in several worktrees says so (D2). Each row shows what it is doing, its context bar and its available context total. Explicitly related subagents and supervised lanes fold beneath their parent behind “+N”. (Narrowed in place, 2026-11-03, by ADR-1218, decision_c3bb98f4b0e1: children show beneath a parent at work, indented with their own dots, a finished one greyed; “+N” and the expander fold them only once the tree is idle; the expander still starts closed on the row's own detail, contracts 7.2 and 7.8.) Each row has one expander (the same control as “+N”), closed at first; expanded, it lists each worktree the session works in (full path on hover) labelled unmerged or merged, the commands it started and has not seen finish, and the files in its window, read from the agent link's window reading (9.10) only when expanded, then its children. Each row leads with a status dot of its state (working, waiting for you, idle), and each root row wears its session’s own colour, the colour of its wisps on the forest (capability 5, ADR-0736), and a hovered wisp highlights its row. Hovering or focusing a row lights its claimed islands and dims the others. Waiting rows carry no mark beyond their dot, working and waiting read from each session's turns (ADR-0754 D5); rows neither working nor waiting are idle by their state alone, and an idle session is not listed: the list shows only the sessions at work, while an idle child of a session at work stays under it with the idle dot (ADR-1225, superseding ADR-1221 D2; there is no History tab, ADR-1221 D1); ended sessions are hidden. Parent relationships and totals are read only when recorded or supplied by the agent link; missing values are not guessed. *Narrowed in place, 2026-10-05 (ADR-0804 D9, decision_5aadb523c1cb; ADR-0923 D2, decision_027f3b08bb8b): no wisps are drawn, so a row's colour is the colour of its traversal and of its claimed territories' outlines, and the hovered-wisp clause no longer applies. Hovering or focusing a row lights only the islands holding capabilities it, or a subagent folded under it, claimed; an increment it holds lights none, whatever its touches name (contract 7.4).* *Narrowed in place, 2026-11-03 (ADR-1217, decision_e7888402d873): the owner put a status dot on every row, on trial, so a row reads dot, colour swatch, name, context bar; no row text is a model's summary (contract 7.9).* *Overtaken in place, 2026-11-03 (ADR-1219, decision_727e318c6bda; owner-directed): the list is no strip along the forest pane's bottom but the Sessions tab of the app's full-height left rail, filling it, with no header toggle or size control (contract 7.17).*

contracts.title: 7.1 · The list includes once each session the agent-link reading lists (agent link 4.9, 4.12) that is at work (7.10, ADR-1225), whether or not it holds a claim; that reading excludes a verified close-out, or an ended or quiet session with no open work past the user's leave-after setting (1 hour by default, read as idle-after is) (ADR-0754 D4, ADR-0758 D3, D5, narrowing ADR-0749 D1 and ADR-0737 D1), and the list excludes every idle one it keeps. A waiting row carries no mark beyond its status dot (7.9, ADR-1217); working and waiting come from the session's turns (agent link 4.8), and only a session whose hooks report no turns is judged by the user's idle-after setting. A row's task uses its claim reason or held increment title; a session with neither is named from its harness and what it works in (its latest claim's branch, else its last folder), held to 40 characters, and never labelled off plan. A session whose lines name more than one folder shows how many worktrees it works in, naming them on hover (D2).

7.2 · An explicit parent relation or subagent-started record puts that child under its parent, indented, with its own status dot. While the parent or one of its children is at work (not idle; an observed subagent, whose state is not known, keeps no tree open by itself), the children show beneath it without a click and no "+N" is drawn; a child known to be idle stays listed, greyed. Once nothing in the tree is at work, the tree folds behind the row's "+N" expander (7.8), which reveals the children and collapses them again (ADR-1218); a root row is listed only while at work (7.10, ADR-1225), so the trees that fold are those of an idle child under it. No child is duplicated at the top. A recorded subagent lacking its own session reading is shown as observed, without inventing a live state, until its end is recorded (a subagent-ended line, before or after its start): then it reads idle; absent parent relations are never inferred from claim wording.

7.4 · Hovering or keyboard-focusing a row lights the forest islands containing the capabilities it, or a subagent folded under it, claimed, and dims the other islands; an increment it holds lights none, whatever its touches name (ADR-0923 D2). Leaving the row restores the ordinary forest appearance. With no claimed capability the row does not arbitrarily select one.

7.5 · Every row reserves an empty context-bar slot. When an agent-link context total is supplied the row displays that total; when absent it displays an unavailable mark, never zero. This increment draws no composition segments, thresholds or estimated totals.

7.6 · Each row's bar is its session's tokens used (agent link 9.5), read again every 10 seconds, on one scale for every row: 1,000,000 tokens across the full width (the display's choice; a reading has no window size, ADR-0728). A Claude Code reading's bar is split into Injected, Grounding, Implementation and Other in proportion to its composition (9.8), and hovering gives the tokens and each group's estimated share; a Claude Code row marks its reading's context guidance (the user's setting, 600,000 by default; ADR-0739 D1), one mark; a row whose reading carries no guidance has none; a Codex row is one raw segment with no marks. With 400,000 tokens split 2:2:3:1, the segments are 10%, 10%, 15% and 5% wide. The list's header names the four groups in bar order, each beside a swatch in its segment's colour.

7.7 · The list hands the knowledge core its rows as the core's roster, each row with its children in the row's colour. Clicking a row selects its session in the core and marks the row (a child's row selects its parent); clicking the selected row again clears the selection, and the core then shows no session's traversal. The list and the core share one selection (ADR-0738 D5, ADR-0921).

7.8 · Every row has one expander, an arrow at the row's start, closed at first, opening the row's detail only when the user expands it; a row whose children are folded (7.2) counts them as "+N" after its name, and its expander opens them too (7.2's control, not a second one), while the children of a row at work show without it. Expanded, a row lists, under a small "Worktrees" label, every worktree it works in, oldest first, each by its folder's own name with its full path on hover and its merge label (7.15); then its "Running" block (7.16); then, under a small "Files" label, the files in its window (agent link 9.10), each once, in the order first opened, with files no longer in the window muted; then its children. Files are read from the agent link's window reading only when a row is expanded, never from a second reader; a session without a window reading says why and lists no files. Collapsing hides the detail, and folded children, again.

7.9 · The running-sessions list shows facts as labels and prints no prose about a session: no 'needs you' chip or line, no close-out why, no 'holding unmerged' line, and no text made by a model's summary. Every listed row shows, after its expander, a status dot read from its state alone: working (or a child at work), waiting for you within the idle-after time, or idle (an observed subagent's says its state is unavailable), named on hover, then, on a root row, its colour swatch, then its name and its context bar (ADR-1217). A row is idle by its state alone (neither working nor waiting within the idle-after time): a root row that is idle is not listed (7.10), so the idle dot is a child row's. Owner decisions surface only as open questions on the arc surface (ADR-0824 D1, D2, narrowing ADR-0758 D1; ADR-1225 D1).

7.10 · The list shows only the sessions at work: working, waiting for you within the idle-after time, or a parent with a child working. A session that is neither is not listed, whatever keeps the agent link's listing holding it (unmerged work, an unverified close-out, work on main, an app record not yet archived); there are no tabs and no "N idle" row. The header counts the rows. With none listed it says "No running sessions" (ADR-1225 D1, superseding ADR-1221 D2; narrowing ADR-0758 D5; ADR-0824).

7.13 · When the listed sessions run on more than one machine, each row names the machine its session runs on (the latest its activity lines name), beside its name, when the row has room: a row too narrow for it drops the machine first, before its name or its context bar are cut; when they all run on one machine, no row names one.

7.14 · A row whose session holds no claim is named by its app's title (agent link 4.19), held to the label limit, before falling back to its harness and place. Expanding any row opens with up to three lines describing it, from recorded words only: the app's title where the row's name is not it, the objective of the increment it holds, and the app's latest status. A row with none of these shows no description.

7.15 · Each worktree in a row's detail carries one short label from the branches its session recorded there: "merged" when none still holds open work; for an open branch with a pull request, "PR #n" and what it waits on (in merge queue, draft, failing, or in CI while its checks run), or "PR #n" alone when its checks pass or it has none; "unmerged" when no open branch there has a pull request read. The main line, or no branch, carries no label; a branch recorded with no folder is folded under the folder last worked in, and none is dropped.

7.16 · An expanded row's Running block lists the commands its session started and has not seen finish, background ones included, each by its first words (one line, ellipsised, full command on hover) and how long it has run.

7.17 · The list is the Sessions tab of the app's left rail (ADR-1219), filling the tab and scrolling vertically inside it, never horizontally. Its header names it and counts it and carries the colour legend; nothing on it hides the rows or sizes the list, since the rail's tabs choose what shows. Every row starts collapsed and its expander opens it (7.8): its detail, while the children of a row at work show without it (7.2), with no expand-all control; an expanded row lists its Worktrees, Running and Files one under another.
7.18 · A session that has named itself is listed by its own name

7.20 · A session the agent link flags for work on main shows it in its row's one-click detail, not on its row: a warning, "on main", for work outside a workspace; a neutral "first commit" while a new repository's first commit is pending; each with the reading's full words; an unflagged session shows none (ADR-0906 as narrowed by ADR-1223)

7.24 · The sessions list and the forest re-read the plan only when their news holds a change to a story, capability, contract, arc or health record: news of other records, or of lines alone, draws from the tree they already have; their first news always reads.
7.25 · Landing news refreshes the code survey without re-reading an unchanged plan
7.27 · A health change that re-records the state the tree already shows does not re-read the tree: news whose only tree changes are such health records draws from the tree held
7.29 · Clicking a session's row answers within 100 ms with no frame over 50 ms, and the row reads selected within 1 s or shows progress (verified by the Mint box's lag run)
7.30 · The reading starts from the survey kept at the last start
7.31 · A start is settled once the fresh tree and the start's first code survey are drawn (or the survey changed nothing or failed), and the page takes its progress bar away then
7.32 · After the start's first survey lands, the page asks for the survey once more at once, so a newer main fetched meanwhile still arrives
7.33 · A failed refresh says what failed; only persisting failures raise the banner
7.34 · An unreachable library reads as one plain banner

stories.title: Work board
stories.description: A read-only drawer over the map view showing the project's arcs and increments (what landed, what is in progress, what waits) and the questions waiting on the owner. Owns packages/arc-surface.

radius.reason: 6 packages downstream; invited users, inherited from apps/desktop

capabilities.title: 1 · Work states
capabilities.description: Every part, increment and arc shows exactly one state, worked out by one rule from the records, so no two views, and no two lines of one view, can disagree. A part is planned, in progress or landed; an increment, once closed, is landed or not completed (failed, withdrawn, or closed with nothing recorded), and before that is waiting on you, queued, held by an agent or open; an arc is waiting, blocked, claimed, idle, quiet, parked or closed.

contracts.title: 1.1 · A part no line names is planned. A claim makes it in progress, a landed report makes it landed, and a new claim after landing makes it in progress again.
1.2 · A part that is released, or whose window closes, without landing stays in progress, with nobody on it.
1.3 · A story is planned while every part is planned or it has no parts, landed once every part has landed, and in progress otherwise.

1.4 · A closed increment reads landed only when a landing was recorded or it carries a pull request. Every other close, whether failed, withdrawn or closed with nothing recorded, reads not completed (red), with the hover naming which. Nothing reads landed merely because it closed.

An open increment gets one reading, first match wins: waiting on you (held on a question you have not settled, or by a wait for an action of yours with its note while it waits on no open work; it drops back the moment you settle or clear it), then queued (its own wait, or its arc's, still holds, or a wait for an outside event before its check-back day, or a wait for an action of yours on work that still waits on open work, until that work lands), then held (an agent holds it, idle or not), then blocked (unclaimed, and its capabilities list names a capability another open increment holds through a live session; it names that increment and clears when it closes or releases, ADR-0949 D3), then open. An event wait past its check-back day holds nothing, and the reading says check-back passed (ADR-0938 D1). A proposal is never by itself waiting on you, but a question you have not settled holds it as it holds any open increment (ADR-0909 D2). An active increment whose agent released it reads open, still in progress, with nobody on it.

An arc reads one state, first match wins: closed or parked, as recorded; then waiting (a question on it you have not settled); then blocked (its own wait still holds); then queued (every open increment is held, on a wait, on you or blocked by another increment, and it names what it waits on); then in progress (a live session holds one of its open increments, ADR-0949 D1); then ready · N to take (N open increments nobody holds and nothing holds up), even while an idle agent holds other work on it: an idle claim does not hide free work (ADR-0938 D3); then idle, shown "in progress · idle N min" (every agent on it is idle and nothing is free); then quiet (nothing open). Queued, ready and quiet are read from its increments on every live reading (ADR-0760 D1).

capabilities.title: 2 · Agents on the board
capabilities.description: Every increment and part an agent holds shows which agent: Claude Code or Codex, when its window opened, the reason it gave when it claimed, and whether it is live or idle, and for how long. It reads the agent link's own claim reading, so the overlay and the claim tool always agree, and an idle holder still holds its work.

contracts.title: 2.1 · An increment Claude Code holds shows "Claude Code", when that window opened, and its reason. Two Claude Code windows are told apart by when they opened.
2.2 · After 30 quiet minutes the holder reads "idle for N min" and still holds the increment. Once it releases or lands it, its window closes, or its pull request merges, nobody is on it.
2.3 · A Codex holder whose hooks never ran is flagged "hooks not running".

2.4 · An arc's holders come only from its open increments: the agent holding one of them, or a capability claimed under one of them (ADR-0949 D1). A capability claim counts toward the increment it was taken under, never an arc directly; a closed increment contributes nothing, so a capability held by another arc's session reads nothing on an arc whose landed increment lists it.

capabilities.title: 3 · Arc surface
capabilities.description: A full-width arcs-only bar sits below the app story's separate gear-only app bar and opens one read-only drawer over the forest. The bar carries no project name. Both bars reserve their space above the forest so its controls remain reachable, and the drawer opens below them. The drawer, half the window's height, leaves the forest usable below; it can be expanded to fill the window below the bars and restored (3.10). It lists root arcs as dense two-line lanes (state chip, title and small counted wait marks, then the bars alone, wrapping), with a bar for each increment, finished work first, each bar coloured by its work state, a count of what landed and what is open spoken on the bars' label but not shown (ADR-0980), and a chip with the lane's state and who is on it; Active, Parked and Closed each show their own arcs. It stays current while it is open: about every two seconds it asks for what changed in the library and the agent log, which the app carries to it, and it re-checks the clock once a minute, so an agent that goes quiet turns idle without any new record. *Overtaken in place, 2026-11-03 (ADR-1219, decision_727e318c6bda; owner-directed): there is no arcs bar or drawer; the arcs are the Arcs tab of the app's full-height left rail, read while mounted, and an arc's briefing is a card over the map that opens only on its row's click (contracts 3.1, 3.7, 5.1).*

contracts.title: 3.1 · The arcs are the Arcs tab of the app's left rail (ADR-1219): they fill the tab, their scopes then their lanes, scrolling inside it, and are read from the page's start settling (ADR-1224) for as long as they are mounted, whichever tab is on show. An arc's detail opens only when its row is clicked, as a card over the map beside the rail; clicking that row again, the card's close button or Escape closes it and returns focus to the row, and no card opens on its own. Across the active arcs the surface tells the frame what waits on the owner (each lane's question-mark count, summed), which the Arcs tab's badge shows. No action writes library data, and it carries no Library switch or artifact links. While its first read is on the way it says so, and a read that fails says so rather than drawing an empty board, keeping the last board it drew.

3.2 · Each root lane has its state chip, its title and its wait marks on line one, then its increments alone below: one fixed-size flat oval per increment in its state colour, finished ones first and then open ones, longest-waiting first, wrapping onto further lines when they do not fit, never more than four lines at the width drawn at (ADR-1226): past four, the landed ovals fold into one "N landed" mark at the strip's start, and open ovals still beyond four lines into a "+N" mark at its end, each mark's hover naming what it folds; a strip that fits is drawn whole. A claimed increment's oval carries its holder's flag (the globe's pennant in the session's colour, furled and greyed while the holder is idle), and the ovals sit close under the title, leaving only a flag's headroom (ADR-1003). The count ("3 landed · 1 not completed · 2 open", skipping zeros, never a percentage) is not shown; it is the ovals' accessible label, whole even when marks fold some (ADR-0980).

3.3 · Lanes sort by their arc's priority first, 1 first and unranked last, and a ranked lane shows it as "P1" beside its chip (ADR-0963). Within one priority they sort waiting, blocked, in progress, idle, ready, quiet, then the most recently active; a ready lane that also has idle claims sorts with the ready lanes. An arc tag never says claimed: a live holder reads "in progress" and an idle chip carries its age on its face ("in progress · idle 42 min", ADR-0949 D1), and its hover names who holds what; a ready lane that also has idle claims names them, with their age and the work held, in its chip's hover. At the right of its title a lane counts what its open increments wait on: an hourglass with the number of distinct other work and event note waits that still hold, and a question mark with the number of its open questions and owner note waits that still hold; a mark with nothing to count is not drawn, and each mark's hover and accessible label carry the full wording. Each bar's hover names its note waits (ADR-0938 D2, ADR-0980). Active shows on the first launch, then the saved scope is restored; Parked and Closed show only their own arcs, and there is no "All".
3.4 · In the app: a claim written while the overlay is open shows on it within about two seconds, without reopening.
3.5 · In the app: with no new line, a holder turns idle once the quiet time passes. The test uses a stand-in clock.

3.6 · In the app: the smoke check visits every scope and opens every root arc's caret, then judges document.body.dataset.drew.arcSurface against the expected root lanes, expanded queue chips, root-lane increment bars and their agent marks. It does not count +N descendants, queued increments or the increment rows an open caret shows as drawn bars.

3.7 · Between launches, each project remembers the arcs' scope (Active, Parked or Closed). No picked arc is kept, so no arc's card reopens on its own; a value kept before the rail is read for its scope alone.
3.8 · The app's Surfaces menu lists the arc surface as Arcs, with no settings, on until the user switches it off; switched off, it is saved and reads off at the next launch (ADR-0750)

The open board re-reads the work only when its news holds an arc, increment or question change: news of lines alone, or of other records, redraws it from the work it already has, with the new lines. It reads the work itself once when it starts and draws fresh when that lands, without waiting on the page reading's first read: told the page's start, it starts once that has settled, reading nothing and hearing no news before, so the start never waits on it (ADR-1224; story node render 3.49); told none, it starts when it is mounted. News the page held by then is not read again, and until its own read lands the board kept at the last start is drawn as refreshing. Each reading carries the library's waits for the owner or an event (waitsFor) with the holds; an absent one reads as none.

3.11 · The arc surface declares the `arc` family, with `arc increment` within it, and the `question` family, that the command line lists 2nd and 3rd: a question raised holding an increment on its arc holds it, an empty --held-on clears the hold, and retiring a record that is no question names library retire

3.12 · The board reads live arcs and those closed yesterday and today; the Closed tab's Today and Yesterday draw from that, and 7 days or a From–to asks the library for its window when it changes, the kept board holding only the routine read

3.13 · `arc status` gives one line per active arc, moving ones first, each with its state and why: Working (increment, session, machine, since), Landed since --since (with its pull request), Ready, Waiting on you (question titles or owner-wait notes), Blocked (on what, until when) or Idle (nothing parked); the strongest state printed, the other mentioned

3.14 · `arc status` reads the board's arcs and the holds once each however many arcs there are, counts landings from the last two hours unless --since names a time or a span (30m, 2h, 1d), and refuses any other --since
3.15 · `arc recent` lists what landed since --since grouped by arc, each landing with its title and its pull request, then the arcs that closed since then; withdrawn, open and older work is left out
3.16 · `arc recent` reads the board's arcs once, counts from the last 24 hours unless --since names a time or a span (30m, 2h, 1d), and refuses any other --since

3.17 · `arc increment edit --escape-of <pr|increment> --escape-story <story>` records the escape an increment fixes, `--escape-of none` clears it, and one flag without the other is refused with nothing written
3.18 · The mounted arcs say once when they first draw a freshly read board
3.19 · Once the project has a repository cut-over, arc recent and arc show say a pull request closed before it as the old repository's owner/name#n, and one closed on or after it as #n
3.20 · The opened arc's title stays selected in its card across a refresh that changes nothing, and a copy button beside it puts the title on the clipboard as plain text, saying Copied

3.21 · Opening an arc row's gutter caret shows under the row its questions, then its increments (open first, landed folded behind "N landed"), then its queued arcs, never its intent; a question's row opens the card on that question, and the open caret survives the live redraw.
3.22 · The question family declares predict, prediction, score and prep, each calling the library's step for it and printing what was stored or read; a refused step prints its reason and exits 1

3.23 · question deviation prints, for questions settled in its window (default the last 14 days), per confidence band, how many would-be answers matched, matched with changes, differed or were rejected, beside the raiser's recommendation on the same questions

capabilities.title: 4 · Waits
capabilities.description: Every arc or increment that waits on other work says so and names what it waits for: an arc queued behind another arc folds away under that arc’s lane, behind a ▸/▾ caret in a fixed gutter; expansion shows chips, and an increment waiting on another increment, on any arc, draws yellow and names its blocker and why. A blocker shows what it holds up, a wait that will never release by itself says so, and an arc with something waiting on you is never hidden under its blocker.

contracts.title: 4.1 · An arc waiting on an open arc, or whose every open increment waits on work in another open arc, appears only as a chip under that arc's initially collapsed caret, not also at the top; waiting on several, it sits under the first on the board. Selecting the chip opens the queued arc's briefing. Once the wait releases, or it has work nothing holds up, it returns to the top, with nothing written. Waits that form a loop are cut at the loop's first arc on the board, so no arc disappears (ADR-0760 D1).

4.2 · A one-behind-one queue draws as a chain (A → B → C). Two arcs behind one blocker draw as a set, with a · separator and no arrow between them. A queued arc that holds up others carries "+N", one also waiting on another arc says "+1 other wait", and one queued by its increments names the increment it waits on in the arc above it.
4.3 · An arc with a question waiting on you stays at the top while it waits on another arc, and its other open bars still read queued.

4.4 · An increment waiting on another names it, its arc and the reason, and the blocker names what it holds up. If the blocker closed without landing, or cannot be found, the wait says it will not release by itself.

capabilities.title: 5 · Briefing
capabilities.description: Picking a lane, or a queued arc, opens its briefing: rows you scan, each a door into its prose, and no prose until something is opened (ADR-0980 D5). The arc's intent is one folded line. Its questions are one table, open first, each row a title and a status (open or settled); opening a row replaces the table with the full reading, the answer on top when settled, and “← back to questions” restores it. The reading is statement first, with its stakes, diagram, options as for and against, a recommendation marked not binding, and the longer parts folded with their word counts. After the questions, every increment on the arc is a row: its colour, its title and one short cell of chips for what it is doing, landed ones folded behind one row; opening a row shows its objective, its waits by name, the questions it waits behind, what it holds up, who holds it and how it closed.

contracts.title: 5.1 · Clicking an arc's row opens its card, which shows its title, its intent folded behind one closed line, then its questions as one table, open first, each row its title and its status (open or settled); an arc with no questions shows no questions section. A card opens only on that click: none at launch or after a refresh, and one whose arc leaves the board closes.

5.2 · Opening a question row swaps the card's briefing for one full reading; “← back to questions” restores it. The full reading is statement first, then stakes, the diagram or "no diagram stored", options split into for and against, the recommendation marked not binding, and analogy and context folded with their word counts. The row itself shows no word count, no diagram note and none of the question's prose.

5.3 · A settled question stays in the one table, below the open ones, with its status "settled"; it stops counting as waiting, and its answer shows only when it is opened, on top of its reading. A settled question published with only its title and answer opens on those two alone, with no empty headings.
5.4 · A parked arc's briefing says once, on its questions, that the open ones are parked with the arc (they wait for it to be unparked), never "Waiting on you"

5.5 · After the questions, every increment on the arc is one row: its bar's colour, its title on one line and one short cell of chips, never a sentence: "you" when it waits on the owner (a held question, an owner note, or questions behind its waits), "N increment(s)" for waits on other work, "event", "check-back passed", "blocked" by another increment's claim, the holder's label with its quiet minutes, "to take", "not completed", or a landed one's pull request number. Open work comes first (waiting, in progress, to take), then not completed, then landed, folded behind one "N landed" row.

5.6 · Opening an increment row shows in place its objective, each wait by name with its reason (the name alone when it has none), the owner's questions it waits behind, what it holds up, who holds it and how it closed (disposition, pull request, note), never its planning body; the intent fold, the landed fold and opened rows stay open across the live redraw.

stories.title: The command line
stories.description: `storytree` is the command a person types in a terminal to read and change their project's records. It is a front door and nothing more: each command is handed to the function its owning story already has (the library, Session management), so the command line and the agent's tools can never disagree.

radius.reason: 0 packages downstream; no audience of its own or downstream, so owner

capabilities.title: 1 · Front door
capabilities.description: `storytree <family> <verb>` works out which project the folder you are in belongs to, opens that project's library, and hands the command to the owning story's function, keeping no rule of its own. Every answer is a short plain sentence or listing; where it names records it may offer, under `next:`, the commands that open them, and nothing else (ADR-0786). A failure exits non-zero and says what to do; a command it does not have answers with the real one for that job.

contracts.title: 1.1 · In a project folder, `storytree library search <word>` finds an artifact written through the library.
1.2 · In a folder that is not a project, it exits non-zero with "not a storytree project".
1.3 · With storytree stopped, it says "storytree isn't running" within a second.
1.4 · A record the library refuses reaches you as the library's own message, and nothing is written.
1.5 · `storytree` alone lists the families.
1.6 · `storytree <family> <verb> --help` (or `-h`) prints that command's usage and summary and exits 0 without running it, even when the command needs arguments it was not given.

1.7 · A command or verb it does not have is refused (exit 2) naming the command for that job when agents are known to guess the word, else the nearest real one by spelling, and listing what the family has (ADR-0786 D3).
1.8 · An answer's `next:` offers only commands that open a record the answer just named or listed; no stock hints (ADR-0786 D2).

1.9 · `storytree --version` prints the 0.3.<n> of the build it comes from, the number the desktop app shows for that commit (ADR-0753 D2): from a source checkout, with its short commit; from an installed build, the release and commit stamped into it at packaging.

1.10 · Through `pnpm storytree` in a storytree checkout, a word arrives as written, holding double quotes, >, &, |, ^, %, backslashes or backticks, and nothing else runs or is written on its way (ADR-0851 D1).

1.11 · On Windows, a word the script shell still changes on its way (a $, a line break) is refused before the command runs: nothing is done, and the refusal names the word and says to pass that text from a file (ADR-0851 D2). On Linux and macOS pnpm 10 single-quotes each word, so such a word arrives as written.

1.12 · On Windows, a word given to the installed command whose double quotes the caller's own quoting changed, as Windows PowerShell 5.1 hands on a word holding a space and a double quote, is refused before the command acts, naming the word and saying to pass it from a file; a line quoted by Windows' standard rules (Git Bash, a program) is never refused (proven on Windows CI, skipped with a named reason elsewhere).

1.13 · A comma-separated id flag containing whitespace inside an id is refused before any write, naming likely PowerShell array conversion and showing a quoted retry example without guessing or splitting ids; valid comma-separated lists preserve their ids.

1.14 · A flag value opening with @ is read from the file it names; one holding whitespace that names no file is prose kept as written (so text opening with a scoped package such as @storytree/cli reaches the record); a one-word @ value naming no file is refused, naming the path.
