A start's reader (the desktop's) answers its first ask from the main already fetched while it fetches, and its next ask waits on that fetch (8.27). No checkout is changed. Without origin, the primary folder is surveyed; non-Git folders are read directly. Unchanged blob identities retain file and story surveys. The forest owns request pacing; each later request checks for the next landing, so no cooldown can swallow its only refresh.

contracts.title: 8.1 · A source file a test titled "N.M …" reaches belongs to capability N of that test's story, whether the test imports it directly or reaches it through any number of further ordinary imports and re-exports. When tests of several capabilities reach it, the capability whose tests reach it nearest (fewest ordinary imports away; a re-export adds none) owns it, then the one whose tests reach it that near most, then the lower number.
8.3 · A file's lines of code are counted for source files only: a test file, or a test helper under a testing/ folder, adds no lines to any file, capability or story.
8.4 · A relative import from one source file to another is reported as a link from the importing file to the imported one.
8.5 · Surveying again reads no unchanged file (same path and Git blob in a merged snapshot, or size and modified time on disk), reads changed files again, and reuses an unchanged story survey.

8.6 · A source file a numbered test's runs executed, in its own process or one it started, belongs to the capability whose tests executed it most (the package's coverage map); a direct import outranks it, and it outranks a file reached only through further imports.

8.7 · A source file a numbered test reaches only through type imports (a file of types, or one imported only for its types) belongs to the capability whose tests reach it so nearest, then most; any reach by a value import or by running it outranks a reach by types.
8.8 · Each surveyed story names the stories whose packages its package depends on, through any dependency field of its package.json.
8.9 · The survey includes apps/desktop/src files under the app story, attributing their capabilities by the same numbered-test ownership rules as package source files.

8.10 · The survey retains test files tagged as tests, their N.M numbered test titles and their import edges, without adding them to source file, capability or story line counts. Number lists are validated before expansion: at most 256 entries per title and 4096 per surveyed test file, counting repeated entries before deduplication; invalid or over-budget titles supply no proof identities and do not stop other files from surveying.

8.11 · Selecting current surveys that checkout, including local changes. The main default surveys fetched origin/main without changing any checkout, follows subsequent landings, and shares bounded asynchronous Git work per repository. If origin is unavailable it retains the last fetched main; without one it reports failure, in words that name why (Git's own reason, such as an origin with no main or one that cannot be read, or the reason its fetch was skipped) and that tell the refusal apart by its message alone. A repository without origin, or a non-Git folder, keeps the primary-folder reading.

8.12 · A CommonJS `require` of a string naming a relative file, or the package's own exported subpath, is an ordinary import: a test reaches what it requires and everything that requires in turn, so a CommonJS package's files fall in the capabilities whose tests reach them

8.13 · A numbered test outside the package’s src reaches its source as a test in src would; outside src the reader follows test files and their helper dependencies within the package, without counting their lines as source or reading unrelated scripts
8.14 · A test file that runs an imported behaviour suite carries the suite's numbered titles

8.15 · A source file's opening "Capability N · <title>" declaration (after a shebang) puts it on capability N's territory when N's numbered tests or coverage map reach it; a declaration they do not reach, or an undeclared file, is allocated by inference
8.16 · A survey can be read on a worker thread: the same answer as reading it in place, while the asking thread's event loop stays free

8.17 · A changed file is placed in its capability by its own declaration, else by the survey's inference, flagged as inferred; a file in no story's package, or a file that cannot be read, is placed nowhere
8.18 · A source file's import of a name from another story's package is an edge from its capability to the capability of the file that defines the name, type-only when every import behind it is
8.19 · A derived edge whose file at either end has no capability is kept as a story-to-story edge, naming the files that cause it

8.20 · A mapped story is surveyed from the folder this machine imports it from: the files of a language the survey reads tracked at its checkout's commit under its folders, leaving out the skip list's folders and a folder another package of the same import maps, each with its non-blank lines and no capability, read without parsing; a mapped story whose import this machine does not name is absent
8.21 · A mapped story's package dependency on another mapped story's package is a road between them; a loop among mapped stories is reported with the stories round it, and refuses nothing
8.22 · Surveying again while an imported checkout is at the same commit reads none of its files and keeps each mapped story's survey; at a new commit only the files whose blob changed are read
8.23 · A built story's package dependency on a mapped story's package is a road from it to the mapped story; a mapped story's dependency on a built story's package is never a road

8.24 · Work done at source in an imported checkout counts before it is committed there: a changed or new file Git does not ignore is read from disk over the commit's tree, a deleted one leaves, and only those files are read; while that work is unchanged a survey again reads none of them

8.25 · A start whose fetched main is the commit last surveyed, with the same plan, answers from the survey kept between starts without reading or parsing a file; another plan or a newer main is surveyed afresh and kept in its turn

8.26 · a mapped story's file under the folders or files an explored capability covers carries that capability, work not yet committed included; the rest carry none, and a change of covers is read at the same commit
8.27 · A start's reader answers its first ask from the main already fetched while it fetches, and its next ask waits on that fetch and surveys what it brought

8.28 · A '#' specifier the importing package's package.json imports field names literally is an ordinary import of the file it maps to, so a file reached only that way falls in the capability whose numbered test imports it

8.29 · A source file whose opening header's title is not the title of the capability its number names in its story (as a file moved from another story keeps) declares nothing: it is placed by the survey's inference, or nowhere, never in the capability its stale number names

8.30 · A story that owns several packages has each package's files surveyed under its capabilities, paths from the package named after its title, and its edit claims and tested numbers read from every one
8.31 · An edge file whose source file declares nothing of its own, imports nothing of its own package and passes on names from one other story's package is marked a forwarder
8.32 · A numbered test in any script extension's test file carries its contract's number
8.33 · Declared build steps and cleanups are marked on survey edges

8.34 · A test file's esbuild entry point, written as a literal new URL("./x", import.meta.url) inside an entryPoints array, is an ordinary import of the file it names, so a module a numbered test bundles for the browser falls in that test's capability

8.35 · The survey's Git runs no program its repository's settings name, and its fetch of main is skipped, with the reason, when those settings name an upload program, an ssh command or a credential helper

8.36 · A pytest test whose name is test_<n>_<m>_… or whose docstring starts <n>.<m>, in a test_*.py or *_test.py file anywhere in the checkout but Git's ignored files, carries that contract number for the landing check
8.37 · A pytest number prefixed with a story's package counts for that story only, and an unprefixed one counts for a story only while no other story plans a contract with that number

8.38 · Each path given, absolute or relative to the folder, is placed in its checkout: its story and that story's package, apps/desktop for the desktop app's, even for a file the survey does not read, and its capability when it declares one or the survey infers it; a path in no story's package is placed nowhere

8.39 · A bare specifier naming another package of the same story is an ordinary import of the file its exports map it to, so a test in one of a story's packages reaches the files of its other package it imports; another story's package stays unreached

8.40 · Reading a capability's story tests says whether its story's package was seen in the checkout: a story with no package there, and no pytest numbers, is unseen; testedNumbers still reads the numbers alone

8.41 · Deciding which strings are a call's first argument reads each prefix of a test file at most once in total, so the characters its patterns read grow with the file, not with strings × file length
8.42 · a current-checkout reader given its code's name answers a fresh start on an unchanged checkout from the survey kept in the checkout's Git directory, reading no file
8.43 · the survey code's name changes when any of the survey's own source files changes, or its bundle does, and is none when they cannot be read

8.44 · reading a mapped story's tests finds its numbered titles where it was imported from: the checkout itself when that is the import (by its top or its origin), else the folder this machine imports it from; a mapped story whose import is neither is unseen

8.45 · an import from a source file of one capability to a source file of another in the same story derives an edge between them in the story's survey edges, to its own story, following re-exports to the file that defines what it takes, type-only when every such import takes types alone; imports within one capability derive none

8.46 · a source file that calls composeParts with a literal manifest kind derives an edge from its capability to the capability of the file defining each part of that kind that a story package its own package depends on declares in its storytree manifest
8.47 · tree-sitter's Python grammar loads from its wasm bytes and parses a .py file's imports and definitions

8.48 · a bundle built with the survey's tree-sitter plugin carries the engine and the grammar in itself: as CommonJS, as the app's survey worker is, and as split ES modules, as the commands and hooks are, it parses a .py file from a folder with no node_modules
8.49 · A mapped Python package's .py files are drawn on its island through the survey's Python reader, each with its non-blank lines, its test files and conftest.py among them; nothing parses them

8.50 · a built Python story's imports are edges in its survey: import a.b, from a import y (a submodule, else the package), a wildcard, relative levels, nested imports and namespace packages, searched from its src/ then its root; a mapped island's from src/ then the top
8.51 · a Python source file's opening "# Capability N · title", after an optional shebang, declares its capability when the title is its number's, and nothing when the title is another's
8.52 · a built Python story's pyproject.toml makes roads to the stories whose projects it names, by [project].dependencies or a [tool.uv.sources] workspace source, names compared normalised

8.53 · The code survey names the languages a folder's code is in: those it reads, agreeing with the files its readers read, and those it cannot read, from Git's tracked files in a checkout, else a walk

8.54 · a built Python story's pytest tests, module functions and methods of a Test* class, carry the number their name (test_2_3_…, perhaps after the package) or their docstring starts with, and pin the files they reach to that capability
8.55 · a built Python story's numbered pytest test, read by both the survey and the checkout-wide pytest read, is counted once in its story's tested numbers
8.56 · the map's index bundles for the browser, as the desktop page does, with no Node module reachable from it: a reader importing one goes red here, naming the import and its importer

capabilities.title: 1 · Joined graph
capabilities.description: Read-only graph of plan, code and tests, owned by packages/map. Demonstrate Projects 2.5 reached from the desktop view file using a fixture plan.

contracts.title: 1.1 · The graph joins library stories, capabilities, contracts and declared capability dependencies with surveyed files, file ownership, file imports and numbered tests joined to their contracts, marking stored plan edges declared and survey or test-title edges inferred.
1.3 · a mapped file an explored capability covers implements it, and the map answers for either; the capability reads mapped until it has a contract

capabilities.title: 2 · Focus selection
capabilities.description: Select any file, capability, promise or story by upstream and downstream dependency depth and node kind.

contracts.title: 2.1 · Given either a code file or a capability as input, up returns its dependencies and down returns its dependents to the requested depth, with each returned node once at its nearest depth.

2.2 · Selection accepts file paths, capability ids or numbers, promise ids or numbers and story names; kind filters the returned node kinds without stopping traversal through other kinds, and an absent or ambiguous selection is refused explicitly.
2.3 · In a fixture plan where apps/desktop/src/view/view.ts belongs to the app Projects capability, selecting that file with up 1 returns Projects and its contracts, including Projects 2.5.
2.6 · A selection in the library's record names, or a bare record id, selects its node
2.7 · The focus tool refuses a call that gives neither select nor crossing, or a crossing with a select that names no mapped story or with dry_run, before it reads anything

2.8 · With capabilities and select story:<name>, the focus tool answers that story's capability tree as `map --capabilities` does (3.11), as text and as data; with crossing, or a select that names no story, it is refused before anything is read

capabilities.title: 3 · Counts before detail
capabilities.description: Return complete counts and estimated token cost before detail; show every selected row or refuse above the ceiling, never truncate.

contracts.title: 3.1 · The default map answer gives counts by depth and kind, verified health tallies and the estimated token cost of the full answer, plus hints to narrow, without detail rows.
3.2 · Dry-run returns the selected row count and estimated token cost without detail rows.
3.3 · Show returns every selected row with id, kind, title, health, depth and edge provenance; above the safety ceiling it refuses with the counts and never silently truncates or ranks rows away.
3.4 · The map command exposes the same selection and counts, dry-run and show modes in text and JSON, including a structured refusal above the show ceiling.
3.5 · The agent-link focus tool accepts select, up, down, kind and mode counts, dry_run or show, defaults to counts, and returns the same complete-or-refused answer as the map command.
3.6 · In a branch's checkout the map reads the plan with that branch's increment's pending changes laid over; elsewhere the live plan

3.7 · Focus on a mapped story, or on a file of an imported folder (by its path there or its full path), answers counts first with the word mapped in place of any health, and names a loop among the mapped stories it reaches
3.8 · The map command and the focus tool answer for a mapped story from the folder this machine imports it from
3.9 · For folders or file patterns in a mapped island, the map counts the files outside that import files inside and the files inside that import files outside, and lists each import on show
3.10 · An explored capability named cap:<id|number> in place of folders draws the crossing's line round the files it covers, among its story's files; one covering nothing is refused

3.11 · With --capabilities, the map answers a selected story's capabilities in one read: each with its health word and reason, its contracts (number and title), the capabilities it depends on, and its source files with their lines of code, tests left out; --json gives it as data
3.12 · A repeat map or focus on an unchanged checkout reads and parses no file
3.13 · a new process's map or diff focus on an unchanged Git checkout parses no file of it

capabilities.title: 4 · Diff impact
capabilities.description: Focus a git diff on changed files, their promises and dependents, including the tests that name those promises.

contracts.title: 4.1 · Given a git range, defaulting to the branch against origin/main, affected joins changed files to their capabilities and promises, their downstream dependents and the tests naming those promises, using the map counts, dry-run and show modes.

4.2 · For each story whose package fetched origin/main changed within a given time, the newest such commit and when it was committed; a story whose package did not change then is absent, and with no origin/main there are none.

4.3 · The health worklist read at a checkout gives the library each contract carrying "no test names it" that a numbered test in its story's package on fetched origin/main names, with main's commit and its time; a test only off main names nothing, and with no origin/main none is named
4.4 · With no range given in a repository with no origin/main, affected reads the branch against its local default branch (init.defaultBranch, else main, else master)

stories.title: CI health
stories.description: A user's project shows verified health from the test results its own CI already produced: storytree reads its CI runs on the main branch, matches each test to its contract by the contract number in its title, and writes the verified column (ADR-0901). Its code lives in packages/ci-health.

radius.reason: 2 packages downstream; no audience of its own or downstream, so owner

capabilities.title: 1 · Run results
capabilities.description: A CI job log's test output, read into one result per test (passed, failed or skipped) with the commit the run tested.

contracts.title: 1.1 · A job log's TAP, as the Actions API or `gh run view --log` prints it, reads as one result per test: `ok` passed, `not ok` failed, `# SKIP` or `# TODO` skipped, a subtest under the names of the tests it sits in; other lines give nothing
1.2 · The commit a run tested is read from its log's checkout (`git log -1 --format=%H`), and a log that names none gives no commit
1.3 · A job log in node's spec format reads as one result per test, as its TAP would

1.21 · pytest's -rA summary lines read as one result per test: PASSED and XPASS passed, FAILED and ERROR failed, XFAIL skipped, each with its node id's file and classes; a SKIPPED line, which names no test, keeps its file, line and reason

capabilities.title: 2 · Contract verdicts
capabilities.description: Each test result tied to its story by the test file that carries its title at the run's commit, and to its contract by the title's leading number; each contract then judged passing, failing or not checked.

contracts.title: 2.1 · A result counts for contract N.M of the one story whose package's tests carry its exact title at the run's commit (its outermost numbered name); a title carried by two stories' tests, or by none, credits no contract and is listed as unmatched
2.2 · A contract is passing only when it has tests and every one passed, failing when any failed, and not checked when one was skipped or none ran

2.3 · A test skipped on one platform for a platform reason counts passed when the same test passed on every job of the platform it needs; otherwise it stays skipped, and a contract a skip leaves not checked carries the skip's kind

2.4 · A result no test holds by its exact title counts for contract N.M of the one story whose test calls a helper with N.M and a title (contract("11.8", "…")), when the result's name begins with that number and ends with that title; held by two stories, it credits nothing
2.5 · A failing verdict's note carries, after its tally, the first line of the first message its failed tests carry, cut to 200 characters; a failure with no message leaves the tally alone

2.6 · A pytest result counts for contract N.M by the number its test's name carries (test_2_3_… or test_<package>_2_3_…), for the one story whose package holds that test in the node id's file, or the story whose package the name names; a docstring's number reaches no log
2.7 · A skipped pytest test, which -rA names only by its file and line, is tied to the test at that line (its decorators' or its body's), so its skip leaves that test's contract not checked

capabilities.title: 3 · Reading the project's CI
capabilities.description: The newest finished push run on the project's default branch, read through the GitHub Actions API, and its verdicts written to the library's verified column; the agent's reported column is never touched.

contracts.title: 3.1 · Reading a project's CI writes each judged contract's verified column, by the project's CI with its tally, commit and run, and only from the newest finished push run on the default branch; the agent's reported column is never written, so a capability the agent reports passing reads unhealthy when CI failed it, and healthy only when CI passed it
3.2 · A project with no GitHub origin, or with no finished push run on its default branch, writes nothing and says why; its contracts keep reading not checked
3.3 · A job log holding terminal escape sequences is read all the same, whether gh refuses to print one unless allowed (2.102) or prints it as it is
3.4 · A story whose tests live in its package's own test folder, outside src, is verified from its CI as one with them under src is
3.5 · A job the run skipped, which has no log, is passed over: the run's other jobs are read all the same
3.6 · A cancelled job with no log cannot hide available CI results; available cancelled-job logs still count, absent tests stay not checked, and other errors remain visible

3.7 · Each job's results are read as its platform's: a test skipped on Windows for a platform reason and passed on the Linux and macOS jobs verifies passing, and a contract a skip leaves not checked records the skip's kind
3.8 · A cancelled push run is passed over for the newest finished one that ran to its end
3.10 · The merge queue's run of a commit the default branch holds is read in place of its cancelled push run
3.11 · Only the merge queue's run of the push run's own workflow is read, never another workflow's
3.13 · A contract whose package the newest run's scope left out is judged from the newest run that scoped it in
3.14 · CI health declares the `health` verbs the command line mounts: `health ci` in a project with no GitHub origin says why and writes nothing
3.15 · A push run that ran no tests, standing on the merge queue's run of its commit, is passed over for that queue run

3.16 · A contract whose tests were skipped or crashed is recorded not checked with its skip kind; a verdict the reading or run did not reproduce is recorded as not re-run at the commit, carrying that verdict and its time; an entry already saying the same is not written again, and a contract with no tests keeps a verdict from elsewhere.
3.17 · Every verdict recorded carries its writer's source: reading a project's CI writes it as from CI, a factory plugin's own tests or a local run of a project's tests as verified locally
3.18 · A Python story's pytest tests are verified from its CI as a JavaScript story's are: the run's commit's .py files under packages are read beside its JS and TS

capabilities.title: 4 · A factory plugin's own tests
capabilities.description: A user's factory plugin's own tests, run through its package's test command in their factory and read back, recorded as the verified health of the promises of the story that plugin is the package of (ADR-0902 narrowed for factory plugins, which have no CI to read).

contracts.title: 4.1 · `storytree health plugin <plugin>`, on the command line only (it has no MCP tool: record_plugin_health is marked absent), runs a plugin's own tests in this computer's factory by its package's test command, and records each numbered test's verdict on the promises of the story that plugin is the package of, in the project, as verified locally: passing when its tests pass, failing when one fails; a plugin with no test command, or no story, writes nothing and says why

capabilities.title: 5 · A project's own tests, run locally
capabilities.description: A user's project with no CI to read, perhaps with no repository at all, has its own tests run through its package.json test command on the command line and read back, recorded as the verified health of its stories' promises, labelled a local test run (ADR-1193 D1, D2: the ladder's local rung).

contracts.title: 5.1 · `storytree health local`, on the command line only (it has no MCP tool), runs the project's own tests by its package.json test command in the project's folder, which needs no git repository, and records each numbered test's verdict on its story's promise as a local test run: passing when its tests pass, failing once one fails; a project with no test command writes nothing and says why, and so does one whose CI storytree reads (a GitHub origin with a workflow), which points to health ci instead

5.2 · `storytree health local` runs a Python project's own tests by pytest -rA (through uv run or poetry run when its lockfile is uv's or Poetry's), when it has a pyproject.toml, setup.cfg or setup.py and no package.json test command, and credits its numbered pytest tests from its .py files as CI does; a run with no results names pytest -rA's output for a Python project

stories.title: The MCP server
stories.description: The MCP server is the second front door: the tool server an agent's harness starts, which serves every story's work as tools through one wrapper (routing the folder, naming the calling session, recording the call, ending merged claims) and hands the agent the habits card naming exactly those tools. It depends on every story it serves, and no story depends on it.

depth.reason: no depth flag in its code

radius.reason: 1 package downstream; no audience of its own or downstream, so owner

capabilities.title: 6 · Agent tools (the MCP server)
capabilities.description:
The toolbox the agent calls, served as an MCP server: plan work (arc, story, capability, contract), see the plan and who is on what, claim or release a capability, report a contract red or green, report a capability landed, say a capability is built so it is no longer proposed (`mark_built`, ADR-0744 D2), and search, read and write artifacts (plus list and add a node's front covers, once the library has them). Each tool is a thin wrapper over the library API and the claims above that answers in a short plain sentence the agent can act on, and every artifact read is logged in the agent activity log (ADR-0624); a new artifact with no place named goes onto the claimed capability's shelf of front covers (ADR-0627 D4, which redirected ADR-0624's default link).

As built: the 6.21 MCP cancellation checks cover claim, make_workspace and attach_workspace before and after library admission. They wait for their blocking and observing database connections to disconnect before removing the throwaway project. An admitted claim still finishes normally; this corrects the test teardown, not the cancellation contract.

contracts.title: 6.1 · A test client talks to the server inside the test itself, with no real agent and no network. It lists the tools, then plans an arc, a story, a capability and a contract, which then appear in the library's tree, the story and the capability each with its founding decision as the first book on its shelf, and it can correct each of them.

6.2 · It claims the capability and the increment it drives, sees both named with their holders in the plan and its data, reports the contract red and then green (the library shows the agent's report going from failing to passing, while the verified column stays "not checked"), and reports the capability landed, which ends the claim.
6.3 · Every call is recorded against the session that made it, using the session id the harness passes, and the machine it ran on.

6.4 · A bad call, such as an unknown capability, gets a readable refusal rather than a crash, and with storytree stopped every tool answers "storytree isn't running, carry on without it". If the database accepts TCP but never completes a fresh handshake, a tool call gives up at the 3-second connection deadline, including its library open, and says storytree is not reachable with what to check before retrying. A later call on the same tool server recovers when the database answers.

6.5 · An artifact written with no place named while holding a capability claim goes onto that capability's shelf as ADR-0627 D4 says, even with a newer increment claim; one with no capability claim gets no default place.

6.6 · Searching and opening an artifact leaves a log line saying which session read it, how it was found (a search result, a link from another artifact, by id, or from a shelf) and whether it took a peek or the whole artifact.

6.7 · Each read also names the agent that made it: a subagent by its id, type and task, or the orchestrator, as the harness revealed them (Claude Code through the hook's line for the call, Codex on the call itself), and "unknown" for a call the harness said nothing about.

6.8 · After Claude Code's `/clear`, which gives the window a new session id the tool server never sees, each call is recorded on the new session, as the hook before it named it; a call no hook saw keeps the id the tool server was started with.

6.9 · The test client parks an increment on an arc, starts it by claiming it, and closes it landed with its pull request, which ends the claim; the library shows each step and the arc reads closed. It records a landing that was never parked, parks a new increment on the closed arc, which re-opens it, and parks and unparks the arc.

6.10 · It sets a wait with a reason, and a claim on the waiting increment is refused naming it; it clears the wait, and the claim succeeds. A wait that would close a loop gets the library's refusal as a readable answer.

It raises a question on an arc and holds an increment on it, which a claim then finds waiting on the owner; it settles the question with his answer, which releases the increment; retiring a held question releases the increments held on it, naming them, and a record that is not a question is refused.

6.13 · It corrects an artifact's wording in place: the artifact keeps its id and takes the new words, only the fields given change, and an artifact that is not there, or a field its kind does not have, gets a readable refusal.

6.14 · It retires a contract and then a capability with a reason, and each is gone from the plan, its history keeping it. An id that is not a capability or a contract gets a readable refusal, and nothing is retired.

6.16 · Every library write made by the tools names the calling session in history, including every record a compound call writes, increment starts, Claude Code's session after `/clear`, and Codex calls made by a subagent. A refused write leaves history unchanged, including a question whose requested holds include a missing increment or another record kind.
6.17 · Another story registers tools on this server beside its own, sharing project routing and the session log, and its short instruction line reaches the agent with the habits card.
6.18 · Another story supplies `land`'s final next line when needed, with none when it is not. A refused landing asks for none, and a failed follow-up keeps the successful landing explicit.

6.19 · It makes a workspace for an increment (`make_workspace`, 5.12): a worktree on a fresh branch from `origin`'s main, where Claude Code keeps its own, with the claim held by the calling session and the way into it named (`EnterWorktree` with its path); for work another session holds it gets a readable refusal naming the holder. For Codex, `make_workspace` instead returns instructions and the exact `ref` and `name` for the app's `create_worktree`, then `attach_workspace` takes that returned folder, ref and name and claims its verified branch. The agent uses the returned directory explicitly; an app registration error with a returned worktree is not a reason to create another. Attachment refusals say the app's folder is kept.

6.20 · An edit_plan call cancelled by MCP while its library write is still queued for the project write lock leaves the record and its history unchanged. A write already admitted completes normally and remains attributed to the calling session.

6.21 · MCP claim, make_workspace and attach_workspace calls cancelled before claim admission leave no held claim, claimed activity line or increment activation. A cancelled make_workspace creates no worktree or branch; a cancelled attach_workspace leaves the app worktree unchanged. Calls already admitted complete their claim, activation and workspace operation with the calling session retained in activation history.

6.22 · A test client calls `read_context` as session S and gets S's reading (session, harness, tokens used, when, source) worked out at the time of the call (9.5), including after S's transcript has grown with no turn ended; after a `/clear` whose hook named session T, the same call returns T's.
6.31 · `search_notes` answers with the library's ranked search (capability 14 of the library story), taking an optional `limit`, and says why when it fell back to words.

6.23 · `mark_built` switches a capability's proposed flag off once the agent considers it built, and back on (built: false), with the session as its writer; anything but a capability gets a readable refusal.

6.24 · A tool call a hook saw writes its `tool-called` line and every `note-read` it records naming that hook's `tool-requested` line as their cause, joined by the harness's call id. A call no hook saw names no cause, and nothing is guessed from timing (ADR-0746 D2).

`open` on a contract shows it whole: its title, its description and the capability it belongs to, as it shows an artifact; `open` on a question reads it whole, with its arc, state, wording, answer and the open increments held on it; an arc still gets a readable refusal.

6.27 · `correct_question` corrects an open question's wording in place through the library's editQuestion (12.7): only the wording fields given change and it keeps its id; a settled question is refused with its answer standing, and a missing question or no words given get a readable refusal, with nothing written.

6.28 · `move_increment` re-homes an open or closed increment through the library, keeping its id, lifecycle, outcome, waits and any claim, with the session as writer and the reason in history; open work moving to a closed arc and missing records are refused without a write.
6.29 · `show_plan` gives each capability's word, and for one that is not healthy its reason, who moves it and the contracts carrying it, in its text and its data.

6.30 · health_worklist gives the oldest three capabilities on the health worklist, each with its reason, who moves it, the contracts carrying it and since when, and a failing one its verified note, and how many more wait; a capability an open increment touches is not offered, and one a test run in progress will record is held back, counted and named in its data, and the run named.
6.32 · name_session names the calling session, latest call wins
6.33 · The built storytree-mcp command, started as a harness starts it, serves the agent's tools over stdin and stdout, and exits when stdin closes.

6.34 · A tool call a hook saw works in the folder that hook was run in, the session's worktree, not the folder the harness started the server in: a claim it takes carries that worktree's branch, so its merge ends it. A call no hook saw, or one whose hook named a folder of another project, works in the server's own folder.
6.38 · land names each planned contract of the capability that no numbered test in its story's package proves, and still lands

6.39 · A tool call's reads do not grow with the log's length: the same calls (show the plan, claim, read the context, release) take about as much from the store in a project whose log holds weeks of history as in one whose log holds an hour's.

6.40 · It sets a wait for the owner, with its why and any rank, or an outside event, with a note, and a claim on it is refused naming the note; an owner wait without a why is refused, and set again it keeps the note, why and rank left out; an event wait needs a check-back day; it clears the wait, and the claim succeeds
6.41 · A tool reports each phase as progress the client receives before the answer, and a cancelled call starts no further phase
6.42 · The close_out tool releases all of its calling session claims, reports the released ids in its text and structured answer, and reports no claims released when repeated.

6.43 · A tool called from a checkout not approved for the project its marker names is refused, saying how to approve it, before the project is opened or any line is appended; joining on purpose approves it
6.44 · Asking the owner releases the work it holds
6.45 · The tool server exits with code 0 when a delivery ran during its shutdown
6.46 · add_remedies adds live friction to a parked increment's remedies

6.47 · park_increment takes an increment's capabilities and links, and edit_plan replaces either, or its objective and body, after parking; a story given as a capability is refused with nothing written (ADR-0949 D2)
6.49 · stale_claims gives the session manager each claimed increment whose holder is quiet, with its holder and route; reading it ends nothing
6.50 · plan_contract numbers a new contract past the numbers its capability's landed tests already carry, naming those no contract carries; a landed test's own number is kept
6.51 · edit_plan sets and clears an arc's priority, and show_plan lists arcs by it
6.54 · A mounted verb's next steps are named as tools, below its sentence and in its data; a step with no tool is named as its command; an answer with none adds nothing
6.55 · present_question marks a question as being put to the owner by the calling session

6.56 · edit_plan and retire_from_plan, called by a session holding an increment, hold a change to a story, capability or contract planned before it as a pending change on that increment, leaving the live record alone; one the increment planned, or a call with no increment held, changes it live
6.57 · plan_contract adds an advisory line, never an error, when a contract's title runs past 300 characters, quoting the card's definition of a contract

6.58 · import_project imports a folder, given absolute or relative to the agent's folder, into the project as mapped stories, naming each one it added; a refused folder gets a readable refusal and nothing is written

6.59 · park_increment with waits_on parks an increment born waiting on another increment, so a claim on it is refused naming its blocker until that lands; a blocker that is not a live increment is refused with nothing parked

6.60 · every tool call's answer is recorded on the calling session as a door-answered line: the tool, answered, refused or failed with its class, and the next steps it offered as the tool door names them
6.61 · a tool whose door-answered line cannot be written still gives its answer
6.62 · park_increment and edit_plan set an increment's machine to a machine Machines knows, edit_plan's "none" clears it, and an unknown name is refused with nothing written
6.63 · The tool server names every tool it serves

6.64 · check_setup from an MCP client storytree has no hooks for passes as connected, says what storytree does not do for it, and names its session id; a watched harness whose hooks are missing still reads as needing attention

6.65 · A client that names no session keeps one session id for the tool server's life, or the one STORYTREE_SESSION_ID names in the server's environment, so its tool claims and its shell's commands are one session

6.66 · A tool call from Cursor, which sends the tool server neither a session nor a call id, is recorded on the session Cursor's hook named just before it (its newest request for that tool, in the last half minute); a call no hook announced keeps the server's own session

6.67 · show_plan's line for a mapped story says it is mapped, here before storytree and assumed to be working, and gives the story no health reading of its own (ADR-0993 D3); a capability planned on it keeps its own health line
6.68 · A tool call from Pi, which sends the tool server no session or call id, is recorded on the session Pi's hook named just before it

6.69 · plan_capability on a mapped story records what the agent explored with the folders and files it covers, refusing none or an overlap by naming the capability to correct, which edit_plan corrects

6.70 · set_up_project in a folder in no git repository makes one with a first commit holding the .storytree folder, and says so, or with no git identity makes it with that folder staged and asks the user for a name and email (git config --global with their words), after which check_setup makes the commit; a folder already in one is left as it is, and joining makes none
6.71 · edit_plan lets the holder of a capability's claim list it, past a backed-off lane's list entry
6.72 · search_notes says each friction report's state, so a settled one found by meaning reads as settled
6.73 · plan_contract's reply names the capability's other contracts that no numbered test carries yet, so one is built rather than planned again, in words a user's project knows (no lanes)

6.74 · import_project on a folder already imported says the commit recorded before and now (or that it did not move), counts the files added, changed and removed between them, naming up to ten of each, and names each explored capability whose files are gone as left for an agent

6.75 · The tool server mounts the tool parts its story packages' manifests name (`#parts/tools`): the librarian's, then quality assurance's, then Session management's hook event tool and its claim, context and runs tools, then the map's, then App setup's, each given the project served and the server's tool names
6.76 · A mounted verb's optional text input may be left out of its tool call
6.77 · A mounted verb's many and fields inputs are served as a list and an object
6.78 · A mounted verb's count input is a whole number above 0 in its tool call, left out only when optional, and its fields input marked json an optional object of any values

6.79 · The tool server takes a hook event from a harness through its hook_event tool, mounted from Session management's manifest, and records it through its own connection with no tool-called or door-answered line; the habits card does not name it

6.90 · A tool the lane's experiment arm denies does nothing else: it answers as refused, saying which experiment and arm deny it, and is recorded as a door-answered line with outcome denied-by-arm carrying the experiment and arm (ADR-1064 D2).
6.91 · The claim tool takes several capabilities with one reason, all or nothing
6.92 · show_plan lists live arcs and those closed yesterday or today; given closed (today, yesterday, week) or from and to, only the arcs closed in that window
6.93 · edit_plan on project-anchor writes the project's what and audience, a half at a time, and refuses any other field with nothing written; a story takes no audience (ADR-1085 D1, ADR-1096)

6.94 · show_plan says the project's anchor first (or that it has none), and a plan-health line naming only the anchor's missing half, which fails nothing; it names no story for an audience (ADR-1085 D1, ADR-1096)
6.95 · The tool server serves no tool of a story part switched off on this computer, nor of a part standing on one, and serves the rest
6.96 · friction_drain answers, then the drain step's lines on the calling session, or why the doors learner did not run; the step spawns `doors learn` with no session in its environment
6.97 · The tool server opens the project with its home's system switches: search_notes leaves out the notes switched off, and open still reads one by its id

6.98 · With a factory folder chosen and a factory plugin named to stand in for experiments, the tool server serves the plugin's verb tools where experiments' were, and not once experiments is on again
6.99 · edit_plan records the escape an increment fixes, the change that caused it and the story it hit, its "none" clears it, and a story that is not live is refused with nothing written
6.100 · move_question moves an open question to another arc, parked included, keeping its id and holders; a closed arc, a settled question and a missing one are refused

6.101 · park_increment parks an increment born waiting for the owner with its note, why and any rank (wait_for_owner, wait_for_owner_why, wait_for_owner_rank), so a claim on it is refused until the wait is cleared; one without its why is refused

6.102 · land runs every claim check the parts it mounts contribute, a factory plugin's among them, and is held while one names a problem; with the contributing part not mounted, the claim and its landing still work and the check is not run (ADR-1170 D2)
6.104 · The tool server asks the arm checks its parts contribute; with none mounted, every tool runs
6.105 · The MCP server opens each project with the kinds of record its mounted factory plugins declare
6.106 · A knowledge note a tool writes for a session that has read outside text carries what it read in its history; one written for a session that read none carries no mark

6.107 · set_up_project tells the user in one line to commit the .storytree folder and why (git worktrees and fresh clones find the project through it), unless the first commit it made already holds it

6.108 · plan_capability, under an increment's claim, judges the story's capability numbers as that increment's pending changes would leave it: a number a pending move out of the story frees is given, and one a pending move into the story brings is refused
6.109 · apply_pending applies an open increment's pending plan changes under a merged pull request's mark, and refuses one that has not merged, applying nothing

6.110 · land on a capability whose story has no package it can read in the checkout says it cannot see that story's tests and why, lists the planned contracts it could not check, and does not advise writing them
6.111 · plan_story's and plan_capability's published input schema says founding is a title and a text
6.112 · land on a capability of a mapped story reads its story's numbered tests in the folder this machine imports it from, naming only the planned contracts none of them carries
6.113 · edit_plan with live: true, called by a session holding an increment, edits a story, capability or contract live and keeps the increment's claim
6.114 · check_setup reads a marker naming a project this library lacks as missing, and set_up_project replaces it

6.115 · set_up_project on a folder whose code is only in languages the map cannot read adds one sentence naming them and the languages it reads, and what still works: planning by hand, and the health the agent reports

capabilities.title: 7 · Instructions (the habits card)
capabilities.description: One short text, a screen or less, that teaches the agent storytree's habits: plan the story first, claim a capability and open the knowledge it needs before touching it, write the failing test and report red, make it pass and report green, report it landed, and record an artifact for anything worth remembering. The tool server hands this text to the agent at the start of every session, as its instructions; Claude Code reads it from there. Codex (0.158 on) does not: it shows the model neither a tool server's instructions nor its tools until the agent searches for them, so connecting Codex also writes one short marked section into the AGENTS.md in Codex's home that sends the agent to check_setup before its first change in a storytree project and keeps it silent elsewhere (7.4; measured 0 of 3 without, 3 of 3 with, packages/app-setup/evidence/codex-first-session).

contracts.title: 7.1 · The text names every tool the server offers an agent, and no tool the server lacks; a harness's own tools (ADR-1056 D2) are left off.
7.3 · The tool server hands the text to the agent at the start of every session.
7.5 · The card says who decides what

7.7 · set_up_project's answer, and check_setup's in a project, carry the whole card, so an agent whose harness keeps only the start of the server's instructions (Claude Code keeps 2,048 characters; Codex shows none) still gets all of it.
7.8 · The card says what one contract is: a behaviour visible from outside, in what goes in, what comes out and the errors
7.9 · The card says how to build beside mapped code

7.10 · The card handed at session start is composed from the guidance each story package the server mounts declares in its manifest, in the manifests' order, between the server's own opening and closing lines
7.11 · The kept start of the card tells the agent to plan requested work before building it

7.12 · With a story part switched off, the habits card the server hands leaves out that part's section and those of the parts standing on it, names them switched off with how the user switches one on, and teaches no tool the server does not serve

7.13 · The card storytree hands, with no factory plugin, still tells the agent to report each contract's test red and green, land and mark_built each capability, close_increment and close_out, and holds none of the build loop's stops for the user

7.14 · With a factory plugin standing in for a switched-off part, the card handed at session start carries the plugin's sections in the part's place, not the part's own, and does not name the part switched off; one that cannot be loaded adds nothing and the part is named off

7.15 · The card says the layout the map draws for Python as for JavaScript: packages/<story>/pyproject.toml with src/<module>, and a test carrying its contract number in its name (test_2_3_…, test_<package>_2_3_… for a dependant's proof)

capabilities.title: 1 · Manifests
capabilities.description: Reads the `storytree` manifests of the story packages a host depends on and returns the parts of one kind, in order, refusing a manifest that names what its package does not export.

1.2 · A manifest part whose `from` is not a subpath its package exports, or that lacks an export name, is refused, naming the package and the part, and nothing is returned
1.3 · storyParts orders parts by their manifest's order, lowest first and unordered last, ties by package name then position in the manifest, whatever order the host lists its dependencies in

contracts.title: 3.1 · An unbundled host importing #parts/<kind>, which its package.json's imports maps to its own module calling composeParts, gets as its declarations every part's declarations concatenated in storyParts' order, and an empty list for a kind no manifest names

capabilities.title: 1 · Project routing
capabilities.description: The first time an agent session starts in a folder that isn't a storytree project, storytree asks the user (through the agent) whether to set one up; if they say yes, this leaves a small marker in the folder naming the project, and from then on it routes everything an agent does anywhere in that folder to that project, whichever project the user happens to be looking at in the app. It never picks a project by itself: a folder the user hasn't said yes to is ignored, and when storytree isn't running it says so at once, so everything built on it quietly does nothing.

contracts.title: 1.1 · A folder whose marker names "site" gives "site" asked from the folder, from a sub-folder of it, and from a git worktree of it.
1.2 · A folder with no marker, in it or above it, gives "not a storytree project".
1.4 · With the app's database stopped, asking where to send activity answers "storytree isn't running" in well under a second.
1.5 · A leftover address from a crashed app counts as not running: it answers in well under a second and never hangs.

1.6 · With the library set to Cloud SQL, a project folder routes to that instance (its connection name and user) whether or not the app's local database is running, and no local address is tried; with it local, routing is exactly as in 1.1 to 1.5.

1.7 · Routing reads only the library setting: damage elsewhere in settings.json (an unusable context guidance, say) does not stop it, while a damaged library setting, or a file that is not a JSON object, refuses naming the file and is never read as local nor rewritten.

1.12 · A marker alone reaches no project (ADR-0942): a checkout whose marker names an existing project, with or without its identity, is refused until its trunk on this machine is approved, and a trunk recorded before approval counts as unapproved until it joins on purpose; an approved trunk and its git worktrees reach it.

1.15 · Project and caller's routing entry alone (@storytree/project-and-caller/routing) routes a folder: one that is no project gives "not a storytree project", and a project whose app is stopped gives "storytree isn't running", without the caller loading the package's root

1.16 · An authenticated local installation routes only through its private, matching versioned credential handoff; damaged or exposed material refuses without a passwordless fallback, while legacy discovery, app liveness and explicit remote routing remain usable
1.17 · Only a git worktree its trunk's repository registered inherits the trunk's project and approval; a copied or forged .git file pointing at a trunk makes no worktree of it

1.18 · A forgotten trunk's remembered approval opens nothing: removing the project from this machine, or deleting it everywhere, drops this machine's remembered approval for it, so its folder is refused until approved again (ADR-0942)

1.19 · An imported folder is recorded on its project beside the trunk, per machine, approved by the import; recording it again updates its repository and commit, and forgetting the trunk forgets its imports
1.20 · The projects with a trunk are read as one set across every machine: a forgotten trunk leaves it, and an imported folder is no trunk

1.21 · A folder's marker is .storytree/project.json, and a root .storytree.json is still read while projects move: the nearest marker at or above a folder names its project, and a folder holding both is routed by .storytree/project.json

capabilities.title: 2 · Settings
capabilities.description: The user's own settings on this computer, for every story: read and written by Project and caller's package (moved out of Session management by ADR-1025), set from the command line and from the app's settings panel (ADR-0728 D2, D3; ADR-0729; ADR-0739; ADR-0649). Per user only: one file, `settings.json`, in the storytree home (`STORYTREE_HOME`, else `~/.storytree/0.3`, capability 1) beside `project-choice.json`. Each setting has a name, a type, a default and a plain-language meaning. An unset setting reads as its default, marked as the default. A value of the wrong type, or a name that is not a setting, is refused with its reason and nothing is written. A settings file that cannot be read or is not valid is reported, naming the file and the problem; it is never silently replaced, and a set refuses to overwrite it.

contracts.title: 2.1 · In a throwaway storytree home with no settings file, `context-guidance` reads 600,000, marked as the default, with its type (tokens) and its meaning.

2.2 · `storytree settings set context-guidance 400000` writes it to `settings.json` in the storytree home, and `storytree settings show`, and a fresh read by Project and caller's reader, give 400,000 marked as set.
2.3 · Setting a name that is not a setting, or `context-guidance` to a value that is not a positive whole number, is refused naming why, and the settings file is left as it was.

2.4 · A settings file that is not valid JSON, or holds `context-guidance` of the wrong type, is reported on read naming the file and the problem, never read as the default; a set refuses to overwrite it, and the file is left byte for byte.

2.5 · With no library setting, `storytree settings show` reads the library location as `local`, marked default; `storytree settings set library cloudsql <instance> <user>` saves the Cloud SQL instance's connection name and the Google account to sign in as, and reads back as set; `storytree settings set library local` returns to local.

2.6 · `settings set library` with anything but `local`, or `cloudsql` with an instance not written project:region:instance or a user that is not an email, is refused with the reason, and the settings file is left byte for byte.

2.7 · Settings in the app’s gear opens a panel headed Settings, with “Yours on this computer · all projects”. Every setting returned by the reader has its current value, meaning, and default or set-by-you source; values can be saved with capability 2’s writers. A newly listed numeric setting needs no panel change.

2.8 · A refused value shows the writer’s exact reason beside its row, leaves the settings file byte for byte, retains the saved source, and can be corrected and retried. A successful save reads back when the panel reopens. Library location uses the same local/Cloud SQL writer and reports that changes apply when the app next opens.

2.9 · A failed read of the Settings panel shows the failure's reason and Retry, never fabricated defaults in place of the rows, and Retry reads again; a save whose transport fails shows its reason and leaves Save available for retry. The overlay that holds the panel (its focus loop with the reachable gear, Close or Escape returning focus to the gear, and its fit at narrow window sizes) is the app frame's: The app 2.6 and 2.7.

2.10 · With no settings file, `idle-after` reads 30 minutes, marked as the default; `storytree settings set idle-after 10m` sets it, and a value that is not a duration (such as `soon`, `0m` or `-5m`) is refused with its reason, and the settings file is left byte for byte. What the setting does to claims and sessions is Session management's Claims 5.43.

2.11 · With no settings file, `leave-after` reads 1 hour, marked as the default; `storytree settings set leave-after 2h` sets it, and a value that is not a duration is refused with its reason and the settings file left byte for byte (ADR-0754 D4; default from ADR-0758 D5).
2.14 · The app shows who decides what, read-only, from the habits card's own lines

2.12 · `storytree settings set library postgres <address>` saves a postgres:// address (host, port, database, user, sslmode), or a wss:// address for Postgres reached over a WebSocket (host, port, database, user), and reads back as set; an address carrying a password is refused, saying to save it as the `postgres` key with `storytree auth set postgres`, and the settings file is left byte for byte (ADR-0846 D1).

2.13 · Routing reads a Postgres-address library as the library's connect options for that address, and the settings panel offers it as a third library location beside local and Cloud SQL, saved through the same writer.

2.15 · settings.json may name the experiment and arm a lane runs in, and what that arm denies, `"experiment": {"name": …, "arm": …, "denies": {"tools": […], "commands": […]}}` with denies optional, read back by name; with none it reads as none, and a value missing either name, carrying anything else, or with denies not two lists of names is reported on read naming the file.

2.17 · `storytree settings set part <part> off|on` switches a part of the host off or on and says every part now off, each standing on another named with it, and that hosts take it when they start; `settings show` lists each part on, off, off with another, or always on (the core); the core, a part the host lacks and the setting does not name (a factory plugin may stand in for one: 2.20) or a state but on or off is refused, saving nothing

2.18 · settings.json names the system switched off and on ("system-off", "system-on": all, roles, checks, notes, or one record's title or id); `settings set system <name> off|on` keeps the two apart and leaves the other settings as they were, `all on` only clears all; readSystemSwitches reads them alone; a state but on or off, and a name in both lists, are refused

2.19 · a machine's health limits read as 6 GB of memory available, a load of 12 and a disk 85% full by default; each is set as a positive whole number, the disk's at most 100, and any other value is refused with the file left byte for byte

2.20 · settings set factory <folder> chooses this computer's factory folder, an existing folder saved as its full path; settings set part <part> plugin <plugin> switches the part off and names the factory plugin standing in for it, which readStandIns reads with the folder and settings show lists, a part no host's parts hold (one that has left the base, such as voice) included, which settings set part and settings show name; on switches it back on and drops the stand-in; a plugin with no name is refused, saving nothing

2.21 · With no factory setting, storytree makes and uses its own factory folder, your-factory, with the factory's shape and no setting saved: beside its versioned home (~/.storytree/your-factory), inside any other home
2.22 · Switching the factory folder needs no approval and records who switched it and when
2.23 · Switching a factory plugin in a part's place, and back, records who switched it and when

2.24 · A checked-in worktree setup's approval is kept in settings.json per repository, as its commands' fingerprint and when it was given, a later approval replacing the earlier one, and a damaged record is refused naming the file

2.25 · storytree settings set service <part>/<service> on|off turns a service on or off for this machine, saved in settings.json; every service is off until it is turned on, and a name not of the form <part>/<service> or a state but on or off is refused

2.26 · `settings set part <plugin> plugin <plugin>` adds a factory plugin that stands in for no part under its own name, and `settings set part` and `settings show` say it is added by that plugin, not that a part is switched off; a part no host has and no setting names, switched to a plugin of another name, is refused naming both forms, saving nothing

capabilities.title: 5 · Portable user identity
capabilities.description: A trusted sign-in resolves to a durable Storytree user id. The identity-owned Cloud SQL users store retains linked provider+subject identities, the verified email and a replaceable WorkOS user pointer. Proof uses real PostgreSQL persistence to resolve first, repeat, linked and conflicting sign-ins without using email equality as identity.

contracts.title: 5.1 · A first trusted social sign-in persists a Storytree-owned user id, its verified email, the replaceable WorkOS user id and every linked Google, GitHub or Microsoft provider+subject identity; reopening the store returns that same user.

5.2 · A returning provider+subject identity resolves to its existing Storytree user id even if its email or WorkOS pointer changes; an unrelated provider+subject with the same email creates a different user.
5.3 · Authoritative linked identities join the existing user's identity set atomically; an identity set spanning two existing Storytree users is refused without changing either user.
5.4 · Concurrent resolutions of the same provider+subject create one Storytree user and return its same durable id.

5.5 · The server resolves a user only from a valid WorkOS session token and authoritative supported social identity evidence; invalid, expired or wrongly issued tokens, unverified email, unsupported providers or missing subjects are refused before any user is written.

capabilities.title: 6 · Social sign-in and session
capabilities.description: The desktop and storytree sign-in use the system browser to authenticate through WorkOS with Google, GitHub or Microsoft only. Proof covers successful and refused exchanges plus a real authorized staging journey; production activation remains an explicit owner prerequisite.

contracts.title: 6.1 · Desktop sign-in opens the system browser with PKCE, offers only Google, GitHub and Microsoft, and completes only its matching authorization response; cancellation or a mismatched response leaves the user signed out.

6.2 · storytree sign-in shows the verification URL and user code, waits according to the device-flow interval, and reports the signed-in Storytree user only after authorization; denied or expired authorization leaves it signed out.

6.3 · A restarted desktop restores its protected signed-in session, refuses unavailable secure storage instead of saving plaintext tokens, and sign-out removes its session so the next status is signed out.
6.4 · A signed-in CLI reports its Storytree user without revealing tokens, and sign-out removes its saved session so the next status is signed out.

6.5 · The desktop signs in only with a public WorkOS client ID configured, verifies WorkOS's access token itself against the client's published keys with no identity server, waits for the storytree-auth callback, and refuses a provider refusal, a failed exchange, a sign-out or a sign-in that never returns.

stories.title: Experiments
stories.description:
The owner writes an experiment down before it runs, runs its arms in isolation under a budget, and reads its curves (ADR-1064). An experiment is a frozen record of its arms, hypotheses, measures and stop rules. Each arm is a named switch the doors enforce. It runs against its own throwaway library, storytree home and public repository, and it is dispatched only into capacity the real pool leaves idle. Every merge on an arm's repository leaves one point, and the points read back as one curve per arm. A Harbor task becomes an experiment's work with one import.

Its code is a plugin in the owner’s factory repo (HuaMick/storytree-factory, plugins/experiments; ADR-1174), no longer in storytree’s base: it stands in for the built-in experiments part, reaches storytree’s packages (the library, Project and caller, keys, Session management, the map and the agent runner) only through a linked storytree checkout, and its tests run in the factory, not in storytree’s CI. The command line and the MCP server ask it whether a verb is allowed only through the arm checks its manifest contributes. The labels on a lane's activity lines are stamped by Session management's activity log from the settings Project and caller reads, so the log never depends on this story. Not in this story: enforcing an arm's guidance, role or review variants; the arm record carries them, but nothing switches them until an experiment needs one.

capabilities.title: 1 · Arm switch
capabilities.description: The arm record, and the verdict the doors ask for (ADR-1064 D2). An arm names its experiment, its name, the verbs it denies by door (tools by name, commands by family), and the guidance, role and review variants it swaps. A lane's storytree home names its experiment and arm in settings.json (Project and caller's Settings); this capability reads it and answers each verb allowed or denied-by-arm. The doors stay thin: they ask, refuse and log; the labels on every line are Session management's stamp of the same setting.

contracts.title: 1.1 · A verb's verdict is read from the caller's storytree home: a home whose settings name no experiment allows every verb; a home naming an arm gets denied-by-arm, with the experiment and arm, for each tool and command family its settings say that arm denies, and nothing else; no arm is held in code.
1.2 · A home naming an arm but not what it denies is refused, naming the arm and saying that its run carries the denies, so a lane started outside its run never runs as if unswitched.
1.3 · An arm's denies are carried into the home that names it, its other settings kept; a home naming no arm, or another, is refused and nothing is written.
1.4 · Experiments contributes its arm check to the doors through its manifest

capabilities.title: 2 · Arm workspaces
capabilities.description: A throwaway library and storytree home per arm (ADR-1064 D3): a database and role named x-<experiment>-<arm> on the box's cluster, made and dropped the way tests make theirs, and a home whose settings point at it and name the arm. Never the real storytree project.

contracts.title: 2.1 · Making an arm gives it a role and a database named for it and a home pointing there, whose key opens the arm's own project, and never touches the real project
2.2 · Dropping an arm drops its database, role and home, and leaves the real library's records and every other arm as they were
2.3 · An experiment or arm name that is not lower-case words and hyphens, or one too long, is refused before anything is made; a home naming another arm is never removed

2.4 · Experiments declares `experiment arm make`, `grant` and `drop`, which act on the cluster holding the caller's library on this machine and are refused, making nothing, where the library is not there
2.5 · An arm's role reads and adds to the server's shared activity and QA databases and reads its routing and points, never deleting there; granted by make, again by grant, revoked by drop
2.6 · The arm verbs sign in to the cluster as this machine's own user over its local socket, with no password, never as the library's role

capabilities.title: 3 · Arm repositories
capabilities.description: A public throwaway repository per arm in the storytree-ai organisation (ADR-1064 D3, as the owner amended it 2026-10-16), seeded from the task, with Linux-only CI, the merge queue on, and the task's verifier as a job; archived when the experiment ends. stories.title: Agent runner
stories.description: Ready work is turned into landed pull requests without a person at the keyboard: a dispatcher picks ready increments from the library and starts lanes under a machine's cap and pace, each lane runs on the engine its allowance allows, and a watcher lands each handed-over pull request, starting a fix session on a red. Its Claude lanes carry the Claude Code mod, a story of its own (ADR-1216 D2), reached through that story's declared interface: its plugin folder, the function hooks variable and the session file variable. It works without the dev loop, and the dev loop works without it (ADR-1071 D3). Its code lives in packages/agent-pool; the repo root's agent-pool.json is the owner's configuration of it (the Mint box).

capabilities.title: 1 · A lane runs on the engine its allowance allows
capabilities.description: Codex below 95%, Claude at the limit, one handover and a queue-preserving fast-fail exit. Founded on decision_2122230a3140 (ADR-0929). When its engine exits, the runner stops what the engine left running (Linux: every process in the engine's own process group or carrying its run's STORYTREE_LANE_RUN marker), after a settling time in which a hook's hand-off may end by itself, with SIGTERM then SIGKILL, naming each in its log (1.23, increment_88f1b6cb5caa). Under systemd on Linux each engine runs in a systemd user scope of its own, limited to the pool configuration's laneMemory (else the box's memory less every other lane's peak) with OOMPolicy=stop, so an out-of-memory kill stops that lane alone, not the dispatcher's scope; a scope killed out of memory ends the lane OUT_OF_MEMORY (77), recorded failed, never requeued as signalled (1.27, increment_c2da34bf38e8).

capabilities.title: 4 · A watcher lands a handed-over pull request
capabilities.description: A session on any machine ends once its pull request is open and its gate is green, and hands the PR to a watcher with no model (packages/dev-loop/src/lanes/watch.mjs): `watch.mjs handover <pr> <increment>` runs `hand` on the box directly, or over `ssh mint` from another machine with the session's own id, refusing with the reason when the box is out of reach (ADR-0974). `hand` records the hand-off in ~/storytree-lanes/watch/, sets an event wait on the increment so no other session takes it while it lands, and starts the watcher if none runs. The watcher polls GitHub: on MERGED it clears the wait, closes the increment landed with the PR and releases the session's remaining claims; on a red (a failed check, a conflict with main, or an ejection from the merge queue) it clears the wait and starts one fix session for that PR, which fixes, pushes and hands back; after its fix limit it writes an owner wait with the PR and the logs. A conflict with main reads as one whatever else failed (13.18), gets one more fix session (13.12), and past that never waits on the owner: the hand-off is dropped and the increment goes back on its arc as ready work, its body naming the PR and its branch (13.20). A fix session whose branch moved while it ran is not counted when the next red is a conflict, and a cap on all sessions per PR (WATCH_FIX_CAP, 6) stops a loop (13.19). A fix session refused by another session's claim hands back with --refused and counts for nothing (13.14), and conflicts with main are merged by one fix session at a time, lowest pull request first (13.15). The watcher also owns a stopped release (ADR-1032 D2): every five minutes its look loop reads the latest published release, the release runs and main's CI runs from GitHub; a release attempt or main's newest CI run that failed is rerun once (main's, and a handed-over pull request's red, again up to a run's fourth attempt while every failed job is the runner's: no runner took it, or the browser crashed at launch, 4.29), and a stop that outlasts the rerun (main still red, the last two release attempts failed, or a commit green on main for over two hours in no published release) starts one fix session at a time, none while one lives or its pull request or question is open, and past the fix limit asks the owner on the release arc (arc_312aa103bfca) (13.16, 13.17). The watcher (`run`) is a keeper over its look loop (`watch`), which exits with the restart code once the dev loop's code in the shared checkout changes, so the keeper starts it again on the new code; `status` says when the running look loop's code differs from the checkout's, or predates the version it records (13.21). It is not an engine, so it counts against no engine slot; its fix sessions are. Founded on decision_e101df427118 (ADR-0955 D3). Every hour the look loop also reads main's first-parent history of the owner's secret-check exemptions list (.github/secret-check-exemptions.txt) from git and records one FYI per commit that changed the paths it exempts: what it added and took away, the pull request and who opened it; each FYI is about `<list>@<sha>`, which the library is asked for first, so a change is told once and none is missed between looks (4.42, increment_67dc251f5856: awareness, not prevention, question_82ab3da6eb69). The watcher and the sessions it starts run in freeOf's environment, without the handing-over session's id or its lane's run marker, so the lane runner does not stop them when that lane ends (4.43).

capabilities.title: 1 · Key store and resolver
capabilities.description: Keeps the keys storytree must hold in one auth.json in storytree's home, only the user can read and write it, and many processes can write it at once safely. It resolves a named key the same way in every process: an explicit value, then the file entry (a literal, or a `!<command>` run once per process), then the environment variable. `storytree auth set|list|remove` is its command-line front door: the cli family parses, calls this package and prints.

contracts.title: 1.1 · Saving a key creates `auth.json` in storytree's home (`STORYTREE_HOME` when set, else `~/.storytree/0.3`, the folder `settings.json` uses), readable and writable by the user alone: on macOS and Linux the file's mode is 0600; on Windows it relies on the user-profile folder's own permissions, and nothing changes them.

1.2 · Two writers saving different keys at once both survive: reading `auth.json` back after they finish finds both entries, because every write holds a file lock and writes a temporary file that is then renamed over `auth.json`, so a reader never sees a half-written file.

1.3 · Resolving a key returns, first to last, an explicit value given by the caller, then its `auth.json` entry, then its environment variable: with all three present the explicit value wins; with no explicit value a saved entry wins over the environment variable; with neither, the environment variable is returned; with none, resolving says the key is not set.

1.4 · An `auth.json` entry `!<command>` resolves to the command's standard output, trimmed, and resolving it again in the same process does not run the command again; a command that fails is an error naming the key and that its command failed, which never contains the command's output.

1.5 · `storytree auth set <name>` reads the value from standard input, takes none as an argument and never prints it; `storytree auth list` prints each key's name and where it resolves from (file, command or environment) and never a value; `storytree auth remove <name>` deletes that entry from `auth.json`, leaving the others.
