capabilities.title: 1 · The address and its guards
capabilities.description: The door's one web address, which claude.ai calls from Anthropic's infrastructure through a public tunnel, and the guards that keep strangers and floods off it: a secret route, a bare 404 everywhere else, the caller's address range, a Host list, body and batch limits, child limits and timeouts, and a keep-alive longer than the tunnel's.

contracts.title: 1.1 · A request to any path but /mcp/<secret> (/.well-known/* and /mcp/<wrong secret> included) is answered 404 with an empty body, never 401, and reaches no tool.
1.2 · On the secret route, any method but POST is answered 405 with Allow: POST and an empty body.

1.3 · With caller ranges configured, a request on the secret route whose X-Forwarded-For last hop (the one the tunnel adds) is missing, not an IP address, or outside every range is answered 403 and runs no tool; one inside a range is served, whatever entries the caller put before it.
1.4 · A request on the secret route whose Host is neither localhost nor a configured host is refused before any tool runs.

1.5 · A body over 64 KB, whether declared in Content-Length or found while reading, is answered 413 and the connection closed only after the rest is drained, so the client sees 413 rather than a reset; a body under it is served.
1.6 · A JSON-RPC batch (a body whose first non-blank character is "[") is answered 400 with JSON-RPC error -32600 and runs none of its calls.

1.7 · At most 2 storytree children and 4 git children run at once; up to 4 and 8 more calls wait for a slot at most one full command and its kill grace (25 + 2 = 27 s, ADR-1163 D3), and any call beyond that, or waiting longer, gets a "busy, try again" tool error without starting a child.

1.8 · A child that runs past its time limit (25 s for a storytree command, 30 s for a library search, 15 s for git) is stopped, and its call answers a tool error naming the limit, inside the client's 60 s request timeout.
1.9 · A caller hanging up before its answer stops that call's child, or takes the call out of the queue, and frees its slot.
1.10 · An idle connection stays open for 100 s, longer than the tunnel's 90 s pool: a second request on the same socket after 95 s idle is served, not refused.

1.11 · The door refuses to start, with a plain message and exit code 1, when its secret is missing, shorter than 32 characters or holds anything but letters, digits, "-" and "_", when its repository folder is not readable, or when a caller range is not a CIDR.

1.12 · Every child the door starts is given an argument array with no shell, runs in the door's repository copy, and inherits only PATH, HOME, LANG, TZ, STORYTREE_HOME, the temp folder and Windows' basics: none of the door's secret, settings or other variables, and a "$" or ";" in a caller's words reaches the child as plain text.

1.13 · Every storytree child runs with STORYTREE_SESSION_ID set to a voice session id (voice-YYYY-MM-DD) and no other harness's session id, so whatever it records names a voice session, never the owner.
1.14 · The door's log never holds the secret, the request path or a tool's arguments: each request is one line of method, tool name, status, time taken and caller address.
1.15 · With no sign-in service configured, no signed tool is registered and the sign-in metadata path is a bare 404; sign-in settings come all together or the door refuses to start

1.16 · With sign-in configured, GET /.well-known/oauth-protected-resource/mcp/<secret> answers protected-resource metadata naming the connector's exact address and the sign-in service; every other well-known path stays a bare 404

1.17 · A signed tool's call with no token, or a token that fails its signature, issuer, audience (the connector's exact address) or expiry, is 401 with a Bearer challenge naming the metadata, and runs no tool
1.18 · A valid token for anyone but the owner's own user id is 403; the owner's valid token runs the signed tool, which knows it is him
1.19 · Reads never look at the token: with sign-in configured, a read with no token, a bad one or an expired one is served, and even unreachable sign-in keys take no read down

1.20 · With VOICE_SIGNIN_EVERY_CALL=1, every call without the owner's token, initialize and reads included, is 401 with the sign-in challenge; the owner's token is served and anyone else's is 403; unset or 0, reads stay open.
1.21 · A tool call whose arguments hold more than 100 array elements and object members is refused before any tool runs, and a subscription stream is refused at once rather than held open.

2.9 · what_changed with a record id returns that record's history, newest first, at most 20 entries, each with when, who and what changed.

2.10 · search_code finds an exact piece of text, not a pattern, in the committed HEAD of the door's repository copy, never its working tree: at most 60 lines as path:line: text, at most 5 per file, each cut to 300 characters, saying when more were left out.

2.11 · search_code and read_code refuse a path that is absolute, starts with "~", holds ":" or "..", or resolves outside the repository, and search_code refuses empty or multi-line text; text or a path beginning with "-" is searched for, never read as a git option.
2.12 · read_code returns up to 300 numbered lines, at most 15,000 characters, of one file as committed at HEAD, from start_line (1 if not given), and says which start_line continues it when it cut.

2.13 · read_code refuses, with a short tool error, a path HEAD does not hold as a file (missing, a folder, a symbolic link), a binary file, a file over 5 MB, a start_line past the file's end and an end_line before start_line.

2.15 · tell_me reads one thing whole by a spoken handle: a question with its stakes, then its recommendation, then its options, a decision by number, an arc, an increment or pull request, a research result or a term
2.16 · count gives the library's fixed tallies (live records by kind and status) and the arcs with the most open increments, from the library's own count, taking no query
2.17 · find tries titles first (the library's title lookup, a decision by its number) and searches by meaning only when no title holds the words

2.19 · the instructions a client gets on connect follow the shared briefing (pattern_5ab3b3241c67): open with catch_up's actions and event-wait line alone and wait for "move on", then the questions in catch_up's order, then what landed, what changed since he last heard and the FYIs; they name no tool tools/list does not offer; the write rules (save notes in his words, his done actions included, mark each question being put to him, mark heard what he has heard, offer to send them to the manager) come only with writes on

capabilities.description: Follow-ups the owner can say aloud: spoken references such as "decision eleven-oh-three" and "number two" resolve to one record, two or more matches answer "which one?" with at most three names and act on none, answers stay short with "say more" pages, and record ids are never read aloud.

capabilities.title: 4 · The box service and its confinement
capabilities.description: Running the door on the Mint box confined: its own box user, its own repository copy refreshed by a timer, its own narrow database role, and system service limits, so the internet-facing process holds none of the owner's keys or superuser login.

contracts.title: 4.1 · The refresh fast-forwards the door's copy to main, reinstalls only on a lockfile change, restarts only when HEAD moved, and puts HEAD back when an install fails

4.2 · The install gives the door its own copy and units reading the spike's secret env file, enables only the refresh timer, changes nothing on --dry-run, and refuses the pool's checkout (agent-pool.json) as its copy

4.3 · The door's database role, granted exactly its grant files, answers every read the door's tools make through the real command line, and is refused every write to the library, its history, the activity log, transcripts, screenshots and the trunks; its one library write, adding voice.note records, is storytree's fence from voice's manifest (4.11), never these files
4.4 · The door's role may add to the search cache but never change or remove what is in it
4.5 · Voice can turn its writes off but never back on: the lock is a row the door's role may add and never remove, and only the box's own account clears it

4.6 · The confined units run the door as its own system user with no view of home folders, no new privileges and a 3 GB memory cap, and its refresh asks for a restart through a request file rather than any privilege of its own
4.7 · The confined door's env file carries only the door's own settings (its secret, PORT, ALLOWED_HOSTS, ALLOWED_CIDRS), never a path the unit sets itself
4.8 · the box's listener survives losing its database connection: it reconnects, catches up with a tick, and goes on starting confirmed runs

4.9 · voice's listener (run always) and committer (run every 15 minutes) are services its manifest declares, which the service host runs: each starts with the host's handle and ends when its stop signal fires

4.10 · the door runs the code the part switch names: the factory plugin standing in for voice while switched to one, none otherwise, since storytree's base ships no voice (voice-host part voice on is refused, naming plugin voice); its refresh keeps storytree's copy and the factory clone at main, points the door's link at the plugin, and restarts once when anything moved

4.11 · the door's role, fenced by storytree as voice's manifest declares it (`storytree plugin fence`: voice.note and voice.mark, each written by storytree_voice), adds voice.note and voice.mark records and is refused any other kind, an update and a delete

4.12 · voice-host refresh-status, run as the box user, reads systemd's record of the refresh and reports it FAILED, quoting what its last run printed, and exits 1 when that run failed, its timer is not active, or it last ran over an hour ago; otherwise it reads ok

capabilities.title: 5 · Drafted writes with read-back and undo
capabilities.description: The writes voice may make: save_note keeps what the owner says at once as a note, answers included (ADR-1155); start_manager_run is a draft read back in one line and, once confirmed, handed to the box at once by a database notification (ADR-1155 D3), carrying every unswept note to the run; confirm, cancel (until the run starts) and lock_voice. contracts.title: 5.1 · The write tools exist only with sign-in, each needs the owner's token, and while voice_lock holds a row every one refuses and writes nothing
5.3 · confirm sets a draft to take effect at once, with no window, once; an expired (15 minutes), cancelled or confirmed draft is refused, and the database enforces it for the door's role
5.4 · cancel stops a confirmed draft until its run starts; after it started cancel says so and changes nothing
5.5 · The box's committer carries out each due draft exactly once; a locked door's due drafts are dropped, not carried out

5.6 · start_manager_run briefs a session manager run from the door's template with the owner's words quoted as data; one voice run at a time, started on the next tick at any hour, and once it ends the box records only how many notes it swept (5.19)

5.9 · a confirmed manager run starts within seconds: the door's database notifies voice_run and the box's listener runs a tick, which also catches up on what was confirmed while it was down, and a run's end mark has its end recorded at once
5.10 · a note the scheduled sweep took, or one already routed, is never carried by a voice-started run or counted in its read-back

5.11 · catch_up tells, under Since you last heard, what has happened to what his notes became until mark_heard keeps the point he heard it, as of the read-out's time, as a voice.mark the door's role writes; then only what changes after it; the first read-out also reads, once, the replies older runs wrote, and keeping the point hears every ended run, once, at the database's time
5.12 · a run that fails to start after its claim ends as failed, saying why, and the box takes the next run

5.13 · on a box run by systemd each voice run is its own unit (voice-run-<id>), so it outlives the tick that launched it; a started run whose unit is no longer running and left no end mark is recorded stopped before it finished, with how many notes it swept, and the box takes the next run

5.14 · a voice-started run is told to take every unswept note in the library, those saved after it started and those waiting when it is restarted, read its notes from the library rather than its brief, and mark each with where it went

5.15 · an FYI catch_up reads is marked heard by voice (mark_heard, by its id, only one the library lists unheard): catch_up leaves it out at once, and the box's committer marks it heard in the library; the door's role may add a mark but never choose its time, change, clear or carry one

5.16 · save_note keeps the note in the library, and only there, at once as a voice.note record (its kind, his words, the question an answer names, the voice session) through `storytree voice note` run as the door's role, whose history says that role recorded it; a note the library refuses is not kept, and he hears so

5.17 · present_question marks an open question as being put to the owner by voice, in the door's database, for 30 minutes (marking it again renews it); it refuses a question another session is putting to him (the question list's flag) or one not open, marking nothing; done, or his saved answer, clears the mark; it works while writes are locked; the door's role may add or remove a mark, never choose or change its time

5.18 · a manager run takes exactly the unswept voice notes, each once, as the box's owner account, with whether each came through the door's role, and marks each with where it went, once; a run that never started gives back the notes it routed none of; the door's role can take or mark none
5.19 · a voice-started run writes no reply: once it ends, all the box records of it is how many of the notes it took it routed ("done, N notes swept")
5.20 · a run that ends with notes it took and never routed gives them back, so the next sweep takes them ("done, N notes swept, M given back")
5.21 · a voice-started run finds claude in ~/.local/bin, and node, whatever bare PATH the host has; the host's PATH follows
5.22 · the door survives the database ending its idle drafts connection: the pool lets that connection go, and the next draft is made on a fresh one

3.2 · A fresh, stale or unlinked worktree gets `pnpm install`.

3.4 · A primary checkout on main is fetched and, with no edits to tracked files and no local commits, fast-forwarded to origin/main at session start, so the agent-link server starts on current code; one still behind (edits, local commits, a failed fetch) names its gap, why, and the update command, and cannot start the server; linked worktrees and other branches are left alone.

capabilities.description: `pnpm test` runs the scoped units against a throwaway local Postgres, each unit under a deadline, reporting which test is still running, and ends in a PASS / FAIL / NOT RUN table; it holds whatever lock its caller hands it past the scope decision (storytree's own run hands it the heavy-run lock, Mick's dev loop's 6), a Node.js known to crash is refused at the start, and each run's reds are kept for the change-reviewer (test.mjs, unit-run.mjs, unit-pool.mjs, test-running-reporter.mjs, test-leftovers.mjs, server-log.mjs, red-runs.mjs, node-runtime.mjs, junit.mjs). contracts.title: 4.1 · A unit past its deadline is killed with its whole process tree, naming the test still running; completed failures print their assertion details and location before the deadline can kill the unit; a test that fails while leaving a handle open ends its unit with that failure, not a hang. A run given a deadline (STORYTREE_TEST_DEADLINE) cuts the unit running at it the same way and leaves later units NOT RUN; stalled outside any unit past it, the run names where it stalled and exits non-zero.
4.3 · On Windows, a Node.js without libuv's fix is refused at the start, naming the crash and the release that fixes it; off Windows none is refused.
4.4 · A run's start keeps the previous run's server log readable, one log deep, and says where it was kept.
4.6 · A test file whose process fails is named with its exit code or signal and the tail of its own stderr, apart from every other file's output

4.8 · When CI requests test evidence, each unit keeps a separate result with its checkout commit, platform, run attempt and repository-relative test identities; later or nested runs cannot overwrite it.

4.9 · The tests are handed the superuser's url for their setup as STORYTREE_TEST_PG_ADMIN_URL, beside the url they connect with; a run given a server's url uses that one for both unless given an admin url too

4.10 · A run tests several units at once (--jobs, else STORYTREE_TEST_JOBS, else 2 with a core left free, or the machine's own default under 6.13), slowest first; each unit's output prints whole under its name when it ends, and a unit's deadline is learned only from runs that tested as many at once
4.12 · A unit run alone starts only once every other unit has ended, and nothing starts beside it

4.13 · Where the test Postgres runs under emulation (Windows arm64) the default is one unit at a time and the run says why, --jobs and STORYTREE_TEST_JOBS still deciding; and a unit with too few passes at this concurrency is never given a deadline under twice its slowest recent pass at any

4.14 · Each unit's tests get a temp folder of their own (TMPDIR, TMP and TEMP name it, inside the system temp folder), removed with everything in it when the unit ends, so a test run leaves nothing of its own in the system temp folder
4.15 · A unit's tests start with no agent session: no watched harness's session variable and no STORYTREE_SESSION_ID, so a command a test runs in the real project records on no session

4.16 · A run that gives its own default unit deadline (STORYTREE_UNIT_LIMIT_MS) never gives a unit a learned deadline under it; a longer learned one still wins, and the row says when the default stood above the learned
4.17 · Once the timing history passes 5,000 rows, a recorded run trims it to each unit's last 40 rows on each machine at each concurrency, oldest first; under that it is only added to
4.18 · The urls a run hands its tests for the Postgres it started name a 30-second connect_timeout, so a loaded machine's slow handshake fails no test

4.19 · node's --test-* options given after a named file still reach node --test, so a name-filtered run (pnpm run test --test-name-pattern=

) runs only the matching tests
4.20 · A unit's end stops every Postgres server running on a data folder in its temp folder, whether it passed, failed or was killed, before the folder is removed
4.21 · A run's start stops any Postgres server in Temp left by a run that has gone, and removes that run's temp folders
4.22 · A run's start removes storytree scratch folders in Temp older than three days, keeping a newer one and one a live server still uses

4.23 · --shard=<i>/<n> runs the i-th of n shards: the units split longest-first by recent passes so the shards' times are near equal, every shard decides the same split, and each names every shard's units
4.24 · Each test's time limit is learned from its own recent passes on this machine, and grows after a timeout
4.25 · A run keeps each failing test's name, so a change's red can be shown later
4.26 · A run's reds are also kept in its clone's shared copy, by the commit they were seen at
4.27 · A run outside storytree keeps its reds through the base dev loop's red-run reporter

4.29 · A run of files named on the command line tells its hold its scope is files, so the hold can let it pass the full runs' queue

stories.title: Storytree's own repository checks
stories.description: The checks storytree's own repository runs on every pull request to keep itself honest: the package-boundary and type-import checks, the code allocation guardrail (the numbered-test refusal), the leak, secret and push scans, the seed-records check, the lockfile report, the capability-list check and own health. Repo tooling: not a base part shipped to users and not one of the owner's factory plugins. Its code lives in packages/repo-checks (story id repo-checks).

radius.reason: 0 packages downstream; no audience of its own or downstream, so owner

capabilities.title: 5 · Package boundaries
capabilities.description: Holds this repository to the package rule by running its own capability 9 · The package rule (src/rules/package-rule, moved here from packages/guardrails by increment_9a2329880e8b, ADR-1199 D5) with storytree's own declarations: its stories, the frame (packages/app, apps/desktop), the front doors (packages/cli, packages/mcp-server) and the owner's sanctioned edges in storytree.check.json (package-boundaries.mjs); and checks that every type-only import between stories ends at The library (type-imports.mjs, ADR-1017 D2). Both run in the lint step, pnpm lint (lint.mjs, capability 8), in pnpm gate and in CI on every pull request (ADR-1199 D2, increment_343265b93ea4). Moved from Mick's dev loop, where it was 3, by increment_fc3a008fe1c6 (ADR-1199); the plan-edge check (was 3.7) stayed with Mick's dev loop's 7 · The gate.

contracts.title: 5.1 · This repository keeps the package rule, run as capability 9 with storytree's own declarations (its stories, frame, front door and the owner's edge list)
5.2 · A type-only import from one story's package that ends at a story other than the library is refused, naming the importing file and the file defining the name

capabilities.title: 6 · Code allocation guardrail
capabilities.description: The lint step, pnpm lint (lint.mjs, capability 8), run in pnpm gate and in CI on every pull request, refuses a checkout that leaves any source file of a story package reached by no numbered test (ADR-0838 D5), by running its own capability 10 · The allocation rule (src/rules/allocation-rule, moved here from packages/guardrails by increment_9a2329880e8b, ADR-1199 D5) over this repository (allocation.mjs; ADR-1199 D2, increment_343265b93ea4). Moved from Mick's dev loop, where it was 9, by increment_fc3a008fe1c6 (ADR-1199).

contracts.title: 6.1 · This repository leaves no source file of a story package unallocated, checked by capability 10's allocation rule

6.2 · A passing browser proof that names its own story records the functions of its story's source it ran, read through the bundle's source map; a recapture replaces it, and a failed or unexecuted one records nothing and removes its earlier record

capabilities.title: 9 · The package rule
capabilities.description: Refuses a checkout that breaks the package rule: a story with no package or declared with several (each story owns exactly one, ADR-1071 rule 5), a package that is no story's, a story's code in a declared frame or front door, a reach into another story's files, workspace packages depending on each other in a cycle, and a story depending on a declared frame or front door unless the owner sanctioned that edge; a sanctioned edge no package.json uses is reported.

contracts.title: 9.1 · A story with no package is refused, and so is a package that belongs to no story (in a project that declares no stories, every package under packages/ is a story's).

9.2 · A story's code in a declared frame or front door is refused; a frame test reaching the story through its package passes; a refused file that leans on the frame is never told to move into the story's package.
9.3 · A package reaching into another story's files is refused, by relative path or by a subpath its package.json does not export.

9.4 · Workspace packages depending on each other in a cycle, even through a devDependency, are refused (roads run one way). Each distinct cycle is reported once; shared acyclic paths are checked without path enumeration, including paths leading into a cycle.
9.5 · A story depending on a declared frame or front door is refused, naming the edge, unless the owner sanctioned it in the edge list; a sanctioned edge no package.json uses any more is reported.
9.6 · A story owns exactly one package: a story declared with several is refused, and the package it would add belongs to no story

capabilities.title: 10 · The allocation rule
capabilities.description: Fails a checkout that leaves a story package's source file reached by no numbered test, naming each such file with its lines and the three ways out (number a test, plan a contract, delete the code).

contracts.title: 10.1 · A story package's source file that no numbered test reaches (by import, or by its coverage map survey-coverage.json) fails, named with its lines and the three ways out; reached, it passes; a test with no number allocates nothing.
10.2 · A source file whose opening comment declares a capability its numbered tests and coverage map do not reach fails, naming the file, its declaration and the capabilities that do reach it
10.3 · Asked to, a source file whose opening comment declares no capability fails, naming the file and suggesting the capability the survey infers for it

10.4 · A refused file whose package's coverage map has no entry for it is also told to re-measure that map with pnpm survey:coverage <package>; a package with no map, or a map holding the file, is not

capabilities.title: 7 · Own health
capabilities.description: Storytree's own health: a run of a project's tests, read from their junit report (storytree's own health is this run configured for storytree, `pnpm check:own-health` after each merge to main, ADR-1066 D2 G; a factory plugin's the same way, `pnpm check:factory-health`), judged contract by contract by the rule CI logs are judged by, and each verdict written to the verified column by CI health's writer, reached through CI health's declared interface (ADR-1112): passing and failing with where they were seen, not checked only for a skip or a crash. The agent's reported column is never touched. Its library scripts reach the library through the one-writer library server (check-own-health.mjs, library-server.mjs, test-run/test-run.mjs, record-run.mjs, main-commit.mjs, factory-run.mjs). Moved from CI health's capability 4 to Mick's dev loop (increment_df916acceacd), where it was 12, and from there into this repository's own checks by increment_fc3a008fe1c6 (question_eda214a321bb placed own health here), with Mick's 5.1 and 5.13; CI health keeps the verdict rules and the writer, which reading a project's CI uses too.

contracts.title: 7.13 · A library tool joins the running app's database instead of refusing, and two tools never write at once.

7.1 · A contract's verified health is passing only if every one of its tests passed; a skipped test, no test, or a file with no results leaves it not checked. A platform:win32 or platform:darwin skip counts only from passing Windows or macOS CI evidence for the exact recording commit and the same file, suites and title, with that system's run named in the health note; a run without that system's evidence leaves its earlier pass standing.

7.2 · A contract whose tests were skipped or crashed is judged not checked with its skip kind, read from the skip reason's first word (owner:, platform:<os>:, anything else other), for CI health's writer to record (3.16).

7.3 · Own health records each merge to main at its own commit, crediting the merge queue's passing run of that exact commit before main's push run, which stands on it and carries no evidence; a pull request's run or another commit's never counts.

7.4 · Before its tests run, own health marks pending each contract a numbered test at its commit names (its story's own package's, or a dependant's titled with the story's package) whose verified health is failing or not checked without a skip; a passing or skipped one is left as it is. The marks hold its capability back on the health worklist until the run records it.
7.5 · A dependant's test titled with a story's package and a contract number that story lacks is named in the run's output with the story it points at, and credits nothing
7.6 · Own health's log names each failing test, with its file and assertion message

7.12 · `pnpm check:own-health` runs each story's tests through this repo's test harness, with no sign-in to the library in their environment (no PG*, HEALTH_PG_* or Google sign-in variable), and reads back every test's result from their junit report, passed, failed or skipped with its reason, for CI health to judge and record
7.7 · A contract retired between a run's checkout and its record is skipped with a logged line naming it; the run records the rest and passes

7.8 · A story whose code is a plugin in the owner's factory (plugins/<package>) has that folder's tests run by the factory's own test command and recorded as its verified health, by a factory test run at the factory's commit; no storytree package's test counts for it

7.9 · A factory run with --unrecorded skips each plugin whose story already holds a factory test run's entry at the factory's checked-out commit and the commit of the storytree its `storytree` link names, and records the rest, so the Mint box's timer records each new factory commit, and each new storytree commit, once without a hand run
7.10 · A factory run that finds no story whose plugin folder is in the factory records nothing and fails, saying why, so the Mint box's timer never reports that commit recorded
7.11 · A test run on CI records its verdicts as from CI, and one run by hand, a factory run, an acceptance run or a lag run as verified locally

7.14 · A connection to the library lost while a story's tests run (dropped, timed out, or ended by the server as idle in a transaction) is retried with a fresh one, a few times with a pause, before a story's record fails; any other error fails it at once

capabilities.title: 1 · Leak, secret and push scans
capabilities.description: check:leaks and check:secrets refuse a branch that adds a personal path, name, address or link, or a credential's shape, in plain, gzipped, UTF-16 or archived text; the push check refuses a push adding a credential this machine holds (leak-scan.mjs, push-check.mjs). Moved from Mick's dev loop's 7 · The gate by increment_fc3a008fe1c6 (ADR-1199), where they were 7.14-7.16 and 7.19-7.21.

contracts.title: 1.1 · the leak scan finds each personal path, name, address and link in plain, gzipped, UTF-16 or archived text, and passes a clean file
1.2 · the leak scan reports a tree by folder and its worst files without the matched text, and refuses only a rise against the merge base
1.3 · check:leaks refuses a branch that adds a leak or a private name, and says when the private names could not be read
1.4 · the secret scan finds each credential's shape in plain, gzipped, UTF-16 or archived text, by its kind, and passes a link's placeholder password
1.5 · check:secrets refuses a branch that adds a credential, even in gzip or UTF-16 evidence, naming the file and kind but never the value, and passes files on the owner's exemptions list
1.6 · the push check refuses a push adding a credential this machine holds, even in gzip, UTF-16 or a damaged archive, naming the file and kind but no part of the value

capabilities.title: 2 · Seed and evidence records check
capabilities.description: check:seed-records refuses a seed, snapshot or evidence file the branch adds or changes that holds a work record, a withheld arc, a private detail or a UTF-16 transcript, and the evidence scrub rewrites one (seed-records.mjs). Moved from Mick's dev loop's 7 · The gate by increment_fc3a008fe1c6 (ADR-1199), where it was 7.10, 7.12 and 7.13.

contracts.title: 2.1 · The gate and CI refuse a seed or snapshot file the branch adds or changes that holds a work record, a withheld arc or a private detail, naming the file

2.2 · The gate and CI refuse a transcript, log, table or CPU profile under an evidence folder that the branch adds or changes when it is UTF-16 or carries a home folder, account, session id or connector, naming the file; the evidence scrub rewrites a folder's captures so they pass

2.3 · The gate's seed check refuses a website snapshot holding an increment's objective, outcome or body, a question, a writer named other than by role, a withheld arc, a wait's reason, or a recorded line's reason, why or session name, and passes one keeping titles and status

capabilities.title: 4 · Capability-list check

Moved from Mick's dev loop's 7 · The gate by increment_fc3a008fe1c6 (ADR-1199), where it was 7.4, 7.6 and 7.7.

4.2 · A branch's checks read the plan with its increment's pending changes laid over, and each pending change its record has moved since it was read fails the gate naming both entries

4.3 · CI's plan-read account, granted exactly infra/library-host/plan-read-grants.sql, reaches the capability-list check's verdict, its stale pending changes included, as the owner does, and writes nothing
4.4 · A plan-reading check run against a library holding no storytree project says so, naming the restore command, and reads nothing

capabilities.title: 8 · Storytree's own test and gate entries
capabilities.description: Storytree's own `pnpm test` and `pnpm gate`: the base dev loop's test runner and gate runner, entered from this repository with what is storytree's own (test.mjs, gate.mjs). The test entry hands the runner storytree's lists (the package-boundary and allocation checks every scoped run carries, the browser proofs run alone); the gate entry installs an uninstalled worktree before its first check and passes --guidance to the steps that read it; and both hold, around their heavy part, the run holds the parts this computer places contribute (the base dev loop's contributedHold): where Mick's factory plugin micks-dev-loop is named, the machine's heavy-run lock (ADR-1192 D2); with none named (CI, a clone of storytree), nothing. Moved from Mick's dev loop's packages/dev-loop by increment_fc3a008fe1c6, with its 7.5 and 13.5, when the heavy-run lock moved to the plugin and packages/dev-loop went; repository tooling, so this repository's own checks hold it (ADR-1199).

contracts.title: 8.1 · The gate installs an uninstalled worktree before its first check; one its install cannot fix leaves every check NOT RUN with the reason and exits nonzero
8.2 · Storytree's pnpm test hands the base runner storytree's own list: its browser proofs run alone; the package-boundary and allocation checks run in pnpm lint instead, not in every scoped run

8.3 · Storytree's pnpm test and pnpm gate take the run hold a plugin this computer names contributes: the test run past its scope decision and not for its usage, the gate once installed and before its first check; each lets it go once its run has ended
8.4 · The gate hands its steps --guidance only when given it

8.5 · pnpm lint runs storytree's code-structure rules (type-only imports, package boundaries, the numbered-test allocation, assert.equal on happy-dom nodes) and fails naming each rule and file that breaks; pnpm gate runs it as one step and CI on every pull request

8.6 · pnpm lint refuses, in a test file importing happy-dom, an assert.equal-family call whose operand may be a happy-dom node (a DOM query, a node-only property, a new Window, or a name bound to one), naming file, line and assert.ok(a === b, message); primitive comparisons there pass

stories.title: Claude Code mod
stories.description: Every Claude Code session given the mod's plugin folder, a pool's lanes and interactive sessions alike, hands storytree its hook events, its heartbeat and its live usage through the session's own tool server, with no process started for them (ADR-1076 D5). Its declared interface is its plugin folder, the variable that turns function hooks on and the variable naming the file it writes the session's id in; the agent runner, and any stand-in for it, reach it only through those, so switching the agent runner off never touches it (ADR-1216 D2). Its code is packages/claude-code-mod.

depth.reason: no depth flag in its code

radius.reason: 3 packages downstream; no audience of its own or downstream, so owner

capabilities.title: 1 · Forwards hook events through the tool server
capabilities.description: The mod hands each hook event storytree records (session start and end, prompt submit, a shell command's before and after, a file edit, a subagent start, turn end) to the tool server's hook_event tool through $.mcp, before the command hooks beneath it run, so they find it recorded and stand down.

contracts.title: 1.1 · Each recorded classic event reaches the tool server's hook_event tool before the settings hooks beneath it run; a storytree tool's PreToolUse and an unrecorded event are passed on untouched; a failed or slow delivery still runs the hooks beneath
1.2 · Beats from its own timer, reports the end and its session id

capabilities.title: 2 · Loads in the runner's lanes and in interactive sessions
capabilities.description: The mod's plugin folder is named by its module, so the lane runner gives it to every Claude Code lane it starts (--plugin-dir, with function hooks turned on), and an interactive session loads the same folder from CLAUDE_CODE_PLUGIN_DIRS, following the checkout's main without re-registration.

contracts.title: 2.1 · The mod names a plugin folder Claude Code accepts: its manifest, and hooks.json naming the hooks module that exports register

capabilities.title: 3 · Reports the session's live usage and failed turns
capabilities.description: The mod hands storytree the session's live context fill, rate-limit windows and cost, as Claude Code's status line has them, and each main-loop turn an API error or a refusal ended, through the tool server's hook_event tool (ADR-1056 D3).

contracts.title: 3.1 · At each main-loop turn's end, and each minute while a turn runs when a figure moved, the session's usage reaches hook_event; an idle or ended session sends none
3.2 · A main-loop turn ended by an API error or a refusal is reported with its reason; an answered or interrupted one as usage alone, and a subagent's turn sends nothing of its own
